```
count(+0xd8) 8-byte     0: 3700   1: 330   2: 88   3: 37   4: 11   5: 15   6: 11  7: 3  ...
count(+0xfc) trailer    3: 4232
slot(+0xb8) on disk     0: 4232
trailing group          12,696 outer entries, 47,055 inner 4-byte elements
`+0x78` pair            sentinel 3,860 | one value 337 | two values 35
```

(Whole-population versions of several of these follow, and supersede the
DLC-only figures above wherever the two cover the same field. The DLC block
is kept because it is the denominator the 4,232/4,232 tail result was
measured against, and mixing the two denominators is exactly how a rate
ends up meaning nothing.)

**Header fields and the head placement, over the COMPLETE 100,379-entry
population** — all five archives, measured with a separate lighter-weight
probe that reads the header and locates the embedded Mesh sub-blocks but
does *not* run the tail walk — so it is a genuinely second instrument over
the same population, not a restatement of the table above. Where the two
overlap they agree exactly: `validate_clmesh`'s own per-archive census
independently reproduces `count(+0xfc) == 3` in 100,384/100,384,
`count(+0xa8)` populated in 0/100,384, and the `+0xb8` slot zero on disk in
100,384/100,384. (The probe's denominator is 5 lower because its own output
dropped a line per large archive; that discrepancy is in the harness's
printing, not in the files, and is why the two denominators differ by five.)

```
entries                                        100,379
count(+0xfc) == 3                              100,379 / 100,379
count(+0x48) == count(+0x58) == count(+0x70)   100,379 / 100,379
slot(+0xb8) non-zero on disk                         0 / 100,379
count(+0xa8) 96-byte array populated                 0 / 100,379
count(+0xe8) populated while count(+0xd8) == 0       0 / 100,379
count(+0x48) > 0                                 1,454   (values 1..14)
count(+0x88) > 0                                   258
count(+0x98) > 0                                 7,194
count(+0xd8) > 0                                19,127
`+0x78` sentinel                                89,187
`+0x78` real values                             11,192   (one 10,275, two 917)
first embedded Mesh sub-block at exactly
  bodyStart + 8*count(+0x48) + 8*count(+0x58)    1,426 / 1,426 testable
  (28 more untestable: no paired `.glmesh_pc` in the same container, so no
   g-backed block can be located anywhere. ZERO entries put it elsewhere.)
```

Three of those are findings in their own right, none of them in
`spec-physics-format.md`:

* **`count(+0x48)`, `count(+0x58)` and `count(+0x70)` are always the same
  number** — 100,379 out of 100,379, across three archives that were
  authored years apart. Three different sub-parsers sized by one quantity
  means `FUN_00749b40`'s 56-byte records are **one per resolved reference**.
  That does not decode the record, which stays OPEN — but it gives the
  array a *scope*, which is more than "56 bytes of something" and is the
  kind of thing a future pass can actually use.
* **`count(+0xe8)` is never populated without `count(+0xd8)`** — 0 of
  100,379 — independently confirming §4.2's "if `count(+0xd8) == 0` the
  function skips straight to its final section", from file data rather
  than from the disassembly that stated it.
* **The `+0xb8` slot reads zero on disk in 100,379 of 100,379** — it really
  is a runtime pointer slot the loader fills in, exactly as §4.1's
  "header-populate-in-place" model says, and not a length or an index that
  could have sized the opaque middle.

**MeshBlock reuse, DLC population:** 30 files carry `count(+0x48) > 0`
(33 entries total). The Mesh sub-block's version-9 word sits at
`headEnd()` in **30 / 30** files, `sr3mesh::MeshBlock::parse()` accepts
**33 / 33** entries, and **30 / 30** files resolve every one of their
references.

That last figure was **27 / 30 until a measurement corrected a guess of
mine**, and the correction is the more useful half of the result. The
c-side step from one embedded Mesh sub-block to the next was originally
written as `roundUp16(anchor + cLength)` — the natural guess, since almost
everything else in this format 16-aligns. It cost every reference after
the first, which is invisible until a file carries two. Rather than try a
second rule, the harness was changed to *measure* the step: for any file
whose resolution stops short, scan forward for the next version-9 word
that actually parses and record its distance from `anchor + cLength`. The
answer came back **`+0`, with no other delta ever observed, in 140 files
across the DLC and `sr3_city_0` populations** (3 + 137) — no rounding at
all, on either side. `src/level_mesh.cpp` now does exactly that.
**The general shape is HANDOFF §3's "when a structure declares its own
size, read it rather than re-deriving it"**, and the specific trap is that
a wrong advance rule is completely silent on every file with only one
reference to advance past — which is 187 of the 343 in `sr3_city_0`.

**Whole-population MeshBlock reuse, post-fix** (`dlc1`-`dlc3` +
`sr3_city_1`, 1,111 files carrying 2,066 references):

```
                                        dlc1-3   sr3_city_1    combined
files with count(+0x48) > 0                 30        1,081       1,111
references in those files                   33        2,033       2,066
Mesh version-9 word at headEnd()         30/30    1081/1081   1111/1111
MeshBlock::parse succeeded                33/33    2028/2033   2061/2066  (99.76%)
files where EVERY reference resolved      30/30    1076/1081   1106/1111  (99.55%)
```

**1,111 of 1,111 files put the shared Mesh sub-block's version-9 word at
exactly `headEnd()`**, and 2,061 of 2,066 references parse through
`sr3mesh::MeshBlock` — meaning they open on their declared check value,
consume exactly their declared g-length, and close on a repeat of it. That
is the shared block's own contract, not a shape match. The 5 that do not
are unexplained and left OPEN.

**How much that one wrong guess actually cost, measured.** `sr3_city_0`'s
run used the pre-fix binary (it was locked by that very run when the fix
landed), which makes it an accidental but clean before/after on a
41,555-entry population: 343 files, 833 references, version-9 at
`headEnd()` in **343 / 343** — but with the 16-aligning step only
**326 / 833** references parsed and only **171 / 343** files resolved
fully. Same reader, same files, one arithmetic rule apart. **`sr3_city_0`
is the one archive not yet re-run post-fix**; expect ~99.5% like the other
two, and read its 326/833 as a record of the bug, not a property of the
format.

**`FUN_0074a110` finalization:** **2,061 / 2,061** bounding volumes
computed post-fix (33 DLC + 2,028 `sr3_city_1`), every one finite and
positive; plus 326/326 on pre-fix `sr3_city_0`. Radius spans
**0.161362 … 139.103058** across the population — small props at the
bottom, large structural pieces at the top. That spread is what a real
bounding-sphere radius looks like, and is the thing a degenerate or
constant computation could not produce.

#### Which sub-parsers got decoded, and which stayed raw bytes

| Sub-parser | Status |
|---|---|
| `FUN_007499d0` arrays 1/2 (`+0x48`/`+0x58`, 8-byte) | **Placement fully decoded.** Contiguous, no realign between them, at `bodyStart`. Array 1's entries **resolve to real Mesh sub-blocks** (below) |
| `FUN_007499d0` tail (`+0xb8` single reference) | **OPAQUE, and the biggest single gap in this format.** A real cursor-consuming step, not a no-op — it is what the whole MIDDLE region is — but nothing in either spec sizes it |
| `FUN_00749b40` (`+0x70`, 56-byte) | **Placement decoded** (16-aligned, `count × 56`). Contents **raw bytes** — §5 OPEN |
| `FUN_00748c70` / `FUN_00749ba0` (`+0x78`/`+0x7c`) | **Branch decoded and confirmed:** the sentinel selects the default-building branch, which reads NO cursor bytes. The non-sentinel branch's cursor cost is **not measurable from shipped data** — see below. Semantic meaning of the 1–2 values: OPEN, untouched |
| `FUN_00749c40` (`+0x88`, 16-byte outer / 12-byte inner) | **Placement decoded and confirmed against real bytes.** Zero of the 4,232 DLC entries populate it; **258 city entries do — 388 outer 16-byte records carrying 2,368 inner 12-byte elements — and every single one of those 258 lands exactly on EOF** (all 129 non-landing entries have `count(+0x88) == 0`). §4.2's literal "the inner region immediately following in the file" therefore holds on real data, not just synthetically. The 12-byte element's own field layout stays OPEN |
| `FUN_00749cf0` (`+0x98`, 52-byte) | **Placement decoded.** Contents raw bytes — §5 OPEN |
| `FUN_00749d40` (`+0xa8`, 96-byte) | **Placement decoded.** Zero of the 45,783 entries measured (all DLC + all of `sr3_city_0`) populate it. Contents raw bytes — §5 OPEN |
| `FUN_00749e80` (`+0xd8`/`+0xe8`/`+0xfc`) | **Fully decoded, including the alignment-discipline switch and the trailing group's real array order.** Contents of the 8-/16-byte arrays and the 4-byte inner elements: raw bytes — §5 OPEN |
| `FUN_0074a110` | **Implemented for real** — see below |
| `FUN_00749da0`, `FUN_00e401d0`, `FUN_00e3fcb0`, `FUN_00e3ffd0` | **Not touched.** §5 lists them as untraced; nothing here guesses at them |

Nothing in the 56/52/96-byte arrays or the 12-/4-byte nested elements is
given a field layout. They come back as `RawArray{offset, count, stride}`
plus `arrayBytes()`, exactly the discipline
`sr3geometry::GeometryBlock` already ships with for `.ccmesh_pc`'s arrays
1/2/3/5.

#### The `MeshBlock` reuse: it works, and here is the byte evidence

The brief asked whether `spec-physics-format.md` §4.2's "entries in the
`+0x48` array are resolved via `FUN_00e718b0`" really means "each is a
nested embedded Mesh sub-block", and to fall back to an opaque blob if it
did not check out. **It checks out, and the evidence is exact, not
statistical.**

`vent_metala.clmesh_pc` (dlc1, 2,532 bytes) has `count(+0x48) = 1`,
`count(+0x58) = 1`, header at file `0x80`, so `bodyStart = 0x1c0`. Bytes
`0x1c0..0x1cf` are 16 zero bytes — the two 8-byte slot arrays — and at
`0x1d0`:

```
0001d0  09 00 00 00  46 91 62 5c  e8 00 00 00  fc 10 00 00
        ^version 9   ^check value ^c-len 232   ^g-len 4348
```

That is the shared Mesh sub-block's pre-header, verbatim, and
`sr3mesh::MeshBlock::parse()` accepts it — meaning its g-segment in
`vent_metala.glmesh_pc` opens on the check value `0x5c629146`, consumes
exactly the declared 4,348 bytes, and closes on a repeat of the same check
value. That is the shared block's own contract, not a shape match.

`diner_wall_2_a01` independently pins the *layout* rule: it has
`count(+0x48) = count(+0x58) = 2` and its first Mesh sub-block sits at
`bodyStart + 32`, where `vent_metala`'s sits at `bodyStart + 16`. So the
head is `8·count(+0x48) + 8·count(+0x58)`, **both arrays laid down before
any resolution** — if the resolutions interleaved, those would be +8 and
+16 instead.

Population figures are in the numbers block above: 33 of 33 references
resolve, in 30 of 30 files, once the c-side step between consecutive
embedded blocks is the measured one rather than the guessed one.

#### `FUN_0074a110` is implemented for real, not stubbed

`boundingVolumeFromExtents()` is §4.2's last row exactly: half-extent
`(max−min)/2` per axis, centre `min + halfExtent` (the operation the
disassembly shows, not the algebraically-equal `(min+max)/2`), radius
`√(hx²+hy²+hz²)`. `computeBoundingVolume()` feeds it from the decoded
vertex positions of the Mesh sub-block a `+0x48` reference resolves to.

That source is a choice and it is worth being explicit about it: in the
engine the min/max arrives through a virtual call on the reference's own
vtable slot `+0x10`, into a sub-object §4.2 did not characterise. What
§4.3 *does* state is what that sub-object supplies — "bounding volumes are
derived from child geometry, not read as flat file data" — so decoded
child vertex positions are the thing §4.3 describes, reached by a
different route. The synthetic suite pins the arithmetic against
hand-computed values (a 3-4-5 half-extent giving radius exactly 5).

#### Six places real bytes disagree with, or refine, `spec-physics-format.md` §4

All six are in `include/sr3clmesh/level_mesh.h`'s file comment with the
file that settles each. **Trust the bytes. These are worth relaying to Team A
as refinements, not as errors in their disassembly** — every one of them is
a detail the decompiler output would legitimately not make visible.

1. **An empty array consumes nothing AND aligns nothing.** §4.1's four-step
   idiom puts the 16-align *before* the count read, which would mean an
   empty array still pushes the cursor to the next 16-boundary. It does
   not. `vent_metala`'s `+0x70` array (1 × 56, 16-aligned) ends 8 mod 16,
   three empty arrays follow, and the next real structure begins at that
   same 8-mod-16 position + 24, not + 32. Reading the align as
   unconditional puts every such file 8 bytes past its own EOF. *(This is
   the identical rule `sr3geometry::GeometryBlock` had to learn for
   `.ccmesh_pc`'s six arrays — `src/geometry_block.cpp`'s `layOutArrays`
   says so in as many words. Arrived at independently here, which is mild
   evidence it is a house convention of this engine's array walkers rather
   than a per-format quirk.)*
2. **The 16-align is per sub-parser, not per array — except it *is* per
   array inside `FUN_00749e80`.** §4.1 states one function = one array =
   one align, but three of the eight lay down more than one.
   `FUN_007499d0`'s `+0x48`/`+0x58` pair goes back to back with **no**
   realign (`vent_metala`, above). `FUN_00749e80`'s `+0xd8`/`+0xe8` pair
   **does** realign: dropping that realign costs 37 of 846 files in dlc1
   alone, all of them files whose `count(+0xd8)` leaves the cursor 8 mod
   16. Two different functions, two different behaviours; neither is a
   safe generalisation of the other.
3. **The trailing nested group is `+0x108` FIRST, then `+0x100`.** §4.2's
   prose introduces the parallel count array (`+0x100`) before the primary
   pointer array (`+0x108`); its own "Output slot(s)" column lists them
   the other way round. **The file agrees with the column, not the
   prose.** On disk: align 8, then `count(+0xfc) × 8` bytes, then
   `count(+0xfc) × 4` bytes, then per entry align 8 and that entry's own
   `count × 4` bytes. Building it the prose way lands 12 bytes off (for
   `count(+0xfc) = 3`) and the harness scores that as a control.
4. **The trailing group's inner elements are 4 bytes.** §4.2's "at 4-byte
   (not 12-byte) element granularity" is ambiguous between "the parallel
   count array's stride" and "the inner element size". It is the inner
   element size; both readings are in the harness as the real walk and as
   a control.
5. **`count(+0xfc)` is 3 in every shipped file.** Not "usually" — in every
   `.clmesh_pc` entry in every archive that carries the format. It behaves
   structurally as a count (its three entries carry three independent
   per-entry counts that vary freely: 1/1/1, 16/16/16, 5/2/7-shaped) but
   nothing in shipped data exercises any other value of the outer count
   itself. **Treat "3" as an unexamined constant, not a validated
   variable** — the same category `spec-geometry-format.md` §4.1 puts
   `.ccmesh_pc`'s never-populated arrays 5 and 6 in.
6. **The `+0x78`/`+0x7c` pair's two shapes are both real, which
   independently confirms the field pair is read at the right offset.**
   §4.2 predicts either the sentinel `-1`, or one value at `+0x78` with
   `-1` at `+0x7c`, or two values. All three occur in shipped data at the
   exact offsets §4.2 gives, with the sentinel much the commonest. Also:
   the header's first `0x40` bytes are real float data neither spec
   describes — `+0x0c..+0x18` is a centre/radius-shaped quad and
   `+0x20..+0x3c` a min/max-shaped set, and on `column_genki_b` the
   `+0x10` word reproduces `(min+max)/2` on the y axis to the last
   mantissa bit (2.0012546 both ways). **Not decoded here** — reported as
   a lead for Team A, exposed as `headerBytes()`.

#### What this did NOT settle, stated plainly

* **The `+0xb8` reference's payload size is OPEN**, and it is the reason
  the chain cannot be walked as one cursor. It is the whole MIDDLE region.
  Nothing here attempts it, and a future pass that wants "walk a
  `.clmesh_pc` end to end in one pass" needs that one number (or a trace
  of `thunk_FUN_00e3e590`) and nothing else.
* **The non-sentinel `+0x78` branch's cursor cost is NOT MEASURABLE from
  shipped data by this test, and the harness says so rather than printing
  a confident number.** The first version of that measurement was vacuous
  and was caught before publication: re-walking from a tail start that had
  itself been *found* assuming a cost of 0 can only ever re-confirm 0. The
  fixed version re-runs the entire search per candidate cost and counts
  only files that can discriminate at all (non-sentinel AND at least one
  later array non-empty, so the pair has something to push). Even on those,
  every candidate value still lands — **2,973 of 2,973 discriminating
  entries across the whole population (94 DLC, 607 `sr3_city_0`, 2,272
  `sr3_city_1`), identically for 0, 4, 8, 12, 16 and 20 bytes** — because
  the 16-byte align before the next array absorbs any shift of 0–15 and the
  search's own freedom to slide absorbs the rest. **The reader therefore
  uses 0 and says it is a parameter, not a finding**
  (`kGatedPairBytes`, and `walkTail` takes it as an argument). This is
  HANDOFF §3's "ask what else would produce this same number" applied
  before publishing instead of after — the first version of this
  measurement would have printed a confident "0 bytes, 85/85".
* **`count(+0x88)`'s two-level nested group — the one §4.2 calls "the
  strongest single piece of evidence in this whole structure for a
  collision-primitive hierarchy" — is populated in 258 of the 100,379
  entries and in none of the 4,232 DLC ones** (41 in `sr3_city_0`, 217 in
  `sr3_city_1`; it reads 1 or 2 and never more). **Its structural placement
  is no longer only-synthetic:** all 258 land exactly on EOF, walking 388
  outer 16-byte records and **2,368 inner 12-byte elements** under §4.2's
  literal "the inner region immediately following in the file". What those
  12 bytes *contain* is still OPEN and is the interesting part, since §4.2
  reads them as a plausible triangle or small plane/face descriptor. In
  `sr3_city_0` the carriers are a handful of
  distinct assets repeated across tiles: `int_hwy_2wayb` and
  `int_hwy_4wayb` (highway intersections, `count(+0x88) = 2`),
  `fountain_a_large_01`, `patio_01~l2`, `wallstair_4mthin_02~l2`
  (`count(+0x88) = 1`), plus their `~l1`/`~l2` LOD variants. Large
  multi-part structural pieces — exactly what a "N collision islands, each
  listing its own primitives" reading predicts would be the ones to use it.
  **2,368 elements across 388 groups is a small enough set to dump by hand.**
* **`count(+0xa8)`'s 96-byte array is populated in zero of all 100,384
  entries, on both instruments** — the same "confirmed to exist via
  disassembly, never exercised in shipped data" category
  `spec-geometry-format.md` §4.1 puts `.ccmesh_pc`'s arrays 5 and 6 in. Do
  not spend effort on it; nothing that ships can test it.
* **The tail start is not uniquely determined for a small minority of
  files.** The search counts distinct surviving layouts rather than
  distinct starts, and the reader keeps the earliest; where more than one
  layout lands exactly on EOF, which is right is **not established**. The
  figure is printed as a distribution, never collapsed into a rate.
* **A 0x50-byte fixed record sits immediately before the tail in most
  files** — 8 zero bytes, `{1, hash}`, 12 zeros, `0x80000000`, 16 zeros,
  `{1, the same hash}`, 24 zeros. Found by hand on four files and then
  counted across the population as an independent corroboration of the
  searched tail start: **54,472 / 100,255** overall — 2,743/4,232 (64.8%)
  on the DLC population, 26,177/41,523 (63.0%) on `sr3_city_0`, and
  25,552/54,500 (46.9%) on `sr3_city_1`. Common but nowhere near universal,
  and the DLC/`city_0` agreement that looked striking at two archives did
  not survive the third. It is a *partial* corroborator, reported as the
  raw fraction rather than dressed up; whatever distinguishes the ~46% that
  do not carry it is not known, and the fact that the fraction itself
  varies by archive says it is a property of the asset, not of the format.

#### How to re-verify

```
build_verify\sr3clmesh_tests.exe                      # 26 tests, no game data needed
tools\validation\build_one.bat validate_clmesh        # from PowerShell, check for BUILD_OK
build_verify\validate_clmesh.exe <archives...>
```

The format lives in exactly five archives — `dlc1`, `dlc2`, `dlc3`,
`sr3_city_0`, `sr3_city_1` — and in no others; `sr3_city_missions` carries
zero, which is worth knowing before spending an hour scanning it.

Two practical notes from running this, both of which cost time here:

* **A city archive takes roughly an hour and is I/O bound, not CPU bound.**
  Running three of these concurrently on one disk made all three several
  times slower than running them one at a time, even with 16 logical cores
  idle. Run them sequentially.
* **`build_one.bat` will silently link the OLD binary if the target `.exe`
  is still running.** MSVC reports `LNK1104: cannot open input file ...
  validate_clmesh.exe` — and that line appears at the *head* of the output,
  while the tail still shows a plausible-looking run. This session hit it
  once and caught it only by reading the head, and it is the reason
  `sr3_city_0`'s MeshBlock-resolution figure above is a pre-fix number:
  the binary was locked by that very run when the c-side advance fix
  landed. `build_verify/validate_clmesh.exe` **has since been relinked and
  is current** (verified by timestamp against `level_mesh.obj`), but
  `build_verify/` also holds `validate_clmesh_b.exe`, `_c.exe` and
  `_old.exe` — duplicate copies made to walk archives in parallel, all
  stale, all rebuildable, all safe to delete.

#### Independent re-verification (dispatching session, same day)

Rebuilt `level_mesh.cpp`, `validate_clmesh.cpp` and the synthetic suite
from source myself (own `.exe`s, not the agent's binaries) and ran all
three archives separately. **Every figure reproduced exactly, including
one that at first looked like it might not:**

* `dlc1`-`dlc3`: header-field census, gated-pair counts, MeshBlock
  resolution (30/30 files, 33/33 references), `FUN_0074a110` radius range
  — exact match, digit for digit.
* `sr3_city_0`: header-field census exact match. MeshBlock resolution came
  back **725/833 references, 308/343 files** — which at first read as a
  flat contradiction of the RESUME table's "2,061/2,066 references"
  headline. It wasn't: that headline is `dlc1`-`dlc3` + `sr3_city_1`
  **only** (this section's own body already said so; the RESUME row just
  didn't repeat the qualifier, so read alone it looked population-wide).
  Two different denominators, not two different answers to the same
  question — the exact "check the denominator" trap this project's own
  methodology warns about. Fixed the RESUME row to restate the scope
  inline rather than leave it a citation trap for the next reader.
* `sr3_city_1`: CONTROL start+4 = 5, `count(+0xfc)`=4 = 27, prose-order =
  0, spec-literal = 0/54,597, non-landing signature counts 75+18+4 = 97 —
  all exact. MeshBlock resolution **2,028/2,033 references, 1,076/1,081
  files** — combined with the `dlc1`-`dlc3` figures above, 33+2,028 =
  **2,061** and 33+2,033 = **2,066**, 30+1,076 = **1,106** and 30+1,081 =
  **1,111** — an EXACT match to the RESUME headline once the right two
  archives are added, confirming the scope note above rather than
  revising it.

**The 100,255/100,384 tail-landing headline is now independently
reproduced across all three archives, not just cited.** Nothing in this
pass changed any conclusion — the one substantive output was tightening
the RESUME row's own denominator statement before it became someone
else's false lead.

### 9.60 `.clmesh_pc`'s `+0x88` nested group's 12-byte inner element — CONFIRMED as a local-space (x,y,z) float32 position, not either literal reading `spec-physics-format.md` §4.2 posed

§9.59 left one thing open on its own recommendation: `FUN_00749c40`'s
`+0x88` two-level nested group — "the strongest single piece of evidence
in this whole structure for a collision-primitive hierarchy" — has a
12-byte inner element whose field layout `spec-physics-format.md` §4.2
calls OPEN, offering two literal readings: "3 vertex/point indices" or "a
small plane/face descriptor". This section tests both against the
**complete** population and settles on a third, better-supported reading
neither literal guess stated outright.

#### The tool, and the population it reached

`tools/validation/dump_group88.cpp` (new) walks every `.clmesh_pc` in
`sr3_city_0.vpp_pc` and `sr3_city_1.vpp_pc` — the only two archives where
`count(+0x88) > 0` at all (§9.59) — using `LevelMesh` exactly as shipped
(no changes to its parsing logic), and for every populated `group88()`
entry dumps each inner element three ways: raw hex, 3×`uint32_t`
little-endian, and 3×`float` little-endian. It only decompresses a file's
paired `.glmesh_pc` when that file's own `count(+0x88)` **and**
`count(+0x48)` are both nonzero (needed to test the index hypothesis
below), which is why it finished both archives in **~36 minutes**
end-to-end against `validate_clmesh.exe`'s own measured "~1 hour, I/O
bound" **per archive** for the full sweep (§9.59) — the brief's own
prediction that a targeted walk would be much cheaper than a repeat of the
full population validation held.

**The population reproduces §9.59's own figures exactly, a third
independent instrument in agreement with the first two** (the tail-walk
search and the from-scratch dispatching-session rebuild):

```
.clmesh_pc entries decompressed+parsed     96,152 / 96,152   (41,555 sr3_city_0 + 54,597 sr3_city_1)
count(+0x88) > 0                              258            (41 sr3_city_0 + 217 sr3_city_1 — exact split)
  ... tail NOT located                          0 / 258
group88 outer 16-byte records                 388
group88 inner 12-byte elements               2,368
```

258/258, 388, 2,368 — the exact numbers §9.59 already reported, reached by
a reader that never re-derives structure (it calls `LevelMesh::parse()`
and reads `group88()` straight off it), over the exact two archives §9.59
named as the format's only carriers.

#### Hypothesis 1 (3 indices, `uint32_t`): REFUTED, on two independent grounds

**Ground 1 — the raw magnitudes.** Read as `uint32_t`, the three slots are
not small numbers:

```
                min    max              zero    <16   <256  <65536  <16M   huge(>=16M)
slot 0 (u0)       0    3,249,277,120      16      16     0     0      0     2,352
slot 1 (u1)       0    3,219,008,752     606     606     0     0      0     1,762
slot 2 (u2)       0    3,244,003,200       8       8     0     0      0     2,360
```

Every non-zero value that is not exactly zero lands in the billions — the
mean magnitude is on the order of 3×10⁹, i.e. this is not "a large but
plausible vertex count", it is the general shape of an IEEE-754 float's
bit pattern read as an integer. No file anywhere in the 2,368-element
population has a slot value that reads as a small, index-shaped integer
apart from literal zero.

**Ground 2 — there is nothing in-file for an index to name.** The brief
asked whether `count(+0x88)` and `count(+0x48)` (the field that would give
an index something to bound against — a resolved Mesh sub-block's own
vertex count) co-occur in the same file at all, since they might not:

```
files with count(+0x88) > 0 AND count(+0x48) > 0 :   0 / 258
```

**Zero.** No file that populates the `+0x88` group ever also carries an
embedded Mesh sub-block reference in the same file. The "3 vertex indices"
reading has no vertex list in the same file to index into, at all, in the
entire population — this alone would be enough to call it dead even
before the magnitude test. A weaker candidate bound, `count(+0x70)` (the
56-byte array whose count §9.59 established always equals `count(+0x48)`),
was checked anyway and fares no better:

```
slot values (u0,u1,u2 combined) < count(+0x70) :   0 / 7,104   (0.0000%)
```

Not "rare" — exactly zero of the 7,104 individual slot readings (2,368
elements × 3 slots) land under that bound either. Both the field this
project would most expect an in-file index to reference, and a plausible
weaker fallback, produce a flat 0%. Hypothesis 1 is refuted, not merely
untested.

#### Hypothesis 2 (plane/face descriptor, read as float): the general float reading holds; the specific "unit-magnitude normal" guess does not

```
                |v| min     |v| max     mean       NaN  Inf  near-unit[.9,1.1]  small[0,2]
slot 0 (f0)       0        21.5043     5.36691       0    0        50 / 2368      948 / 2368
slot 1 (f1)       0         2.2866     0.441158      0    0         0 / 2368     2336 / 2368
slot 2 (f2)       0        13.7225     3.48196       0    0        16 / 2368     1052 / 2368
(x,y,z) magnitude 0.01629  25.4631     7.11294        —    —         8 / 2368         —
```

Zero NaN, zero Inf, across the entire population — these are well-formed
floats, not garbage reinterpreted. But **the "unit-magnitude normal
vector" reading is refuted**: only 8 of 2,368 magnitudes (0.34%) land
within 0.1 of 1.0, which is noise-level, not a signal — a real
unit-normal population would cluster there, not scatter from 0.016 to
25.5. What the numbers DO show, clearly: every slot is small and bounded
(max 21.5 / 2.29 / 13.7), non-uniformly so — **slot 1 alone is almost
always tiny** (98.6% under 2.0, vs. 40% and 44% for slots 0 and 2) — the
asymmetric-axis signature of a real local coordinate frame (one narrow
"vertical" axis, two wider "horizontal" ones), not of three interchangeable
plane-equation coefficients.

#### The confirming evidence: this is local-space position data, and the internal consistency is exact, not approximate

Two structural checks, run before trusting the float reading further:

**1. Byte-identical across every duplicate placement.** The same asset
(e.g. `int_hwy_2wayb~l1`, a highway intersection prop) is placed in many
different tiles across `sr3_city_0`/`sr3_city_1`, each a separate
`.clmesh_pc` entry. Deduplicating the 388 outer records by their own
content collapses them to **18 distinct stems, 24 distinct (stem,
outer-group) slots** — and **every one of the 18 multi-placement stems is
byte-for-byte identical across every one of its repeats (18/18)**. If
these were baked per-tile world positions, two different tile placements
of the same prop (different world transform) would read different bytes.
They do not — this is local/object-space geometry, exactly the "child
geometry" framing `spec-physics-format.md` §4.3 already uses for this
structure's sibling arrays.

**2. Closed-loop bit-exactness, and the loop shapes match the asset names.**
For each of the 24 unique groups, the distance between its first and last
decoded position:

```
stem                       n   first==last distance   shape
fountain_a_large_01       25   0.000000  (CLOSED)      circle, radius 5.2727, constant Y=-0.0055
drain_round_01             7   0.000000  (CLOSED)      circle, radius ~0.50
patio_01                   9   0.000000  (CLOSED)      irregular footprint polygon
wallstair_4mthin_02       15   0.000000  (CLOSED)      stair side-profile, Y climbs 0.1440 -> 2.2866
pocmedianendcap001        15   2.999310  (open)         X-symmetric, NOT closed
int_hwy_2wayb (both groups) 2  13.072507 (open)         2-point edge, X constant per group (+11.3937 / -11.3997)
int_hwy_4wayb (both groups) 2  12.878668 (open)         2-point edge, X constant per group (+21.5000 / -21.5043)
```

`fountain_a_large_01`'s 25-point loop is not merely "plausibly circular" —
every one of its 25 decoded (x,z) pairs lands within 0.001 of radius
5.2727 at a constant Y, stepping in equal angular increments, closing
exactly (first element bit-identical to the last, `struct` comparison, not
"close enough"). `drain_round_01` is the same shape at a different radius.
`wallstair_4mthin_02`'s loop traces a real staircase silhouette — up one
side (Y: 0.15→2.29 as Z advances), across the top landing, down the other
side, along the bottom — which is what "wallstair, 4-metre, thin" should
look like. `patio_01`'s 9-point loop is an irregular quadrilateral-ish
footprint, exactly what an authored patio boundary should be (not a
circle — patios are not round, and this one is not forced to look like
one). **`pocmedianendcap001` is the one asset that should NOT close, and
is the one that does not** — an "end cap" is by definition an open
profile, not a loop, and its own two decoded LOD variants agree on that
distance to 6 significant figures. `int_hwy_2wayb`/`int_hwy_4wayb`'s
2-point groups are edges, not loops: each outer group's slot-0 value is
literally constant across its own 2 points (highway barrier pieces
running along one axis), and the two groups per asset sit at
mirror-image X positions (2wayb: +11.3937 / −11.3997; 4wayb: +21.5000 /
−21.5043) — the left and right barrier of a symmetric intersection.

No index buffer, hash population, or plane-equation coefficient set
produces a perfect closed circle by chance, and it is implausible that six
unrelated, differently-shaped, differently-sized assets would each
independently produce a false-positive shape that happens to match their
own filenames. This is `CONFIRMED — empirical`, on the same internal-
consistency bar this project already uses elsewhere (`FUN_0074a110`'s
radius range, the group-search ambiguity counts): **the 12-byte inner
element is 3 little-endian float32 values, `(x, y, z)`, in local/object
space.** Whether every such group is specifically a *collision* boundary
(as opposed to, say, a simplified render silhouette) is not independently
traceable from file data alone and stays `HIGH CONFIDENCE — inferred` —
the same tier `spec-physics-format.md` §4.3 already assigns the broader
"collision-primitive hierarchy" reading, and the same open question its
own §5 already carries ("whether `.clmesh_pc`'s parsed data is ever
handed to a Havok shape constructor").

#### A second, secondary finding: the outer 16-byte record's `+0x04` field is NOT padding

`spec-physics-format.md` §4.2 characterises the outer record as
`{innerCount(u32), pad, innerPointer(u32, resolved here), pad}` — i.e.
bytes `+0x04` and `+0x0C` both unaccounted padding. Measured over all 388
outer records:

```
+0x04   zero:   0 / 388   (nonzero range 3,299,712 .. 23,812,808)
+0x08   zero: 388 / 388   (expected — the resolved inner pointer, runtime-filled, same as +0xb8)
+0x0C   zero: 388 / 388   (genuinely padding)
```

`+0x0C` is real padding, exactly as described. `+0x08` behaves exactly
like `+0xb8` — a real pointer slot the loader fills at runtime, reading
zero on every shipped file. **`+0x04` is not padding — it is populated in
100% of outer records**, with a real, non-trivial range. It does not look
like a per-asset name hash: it is **constant across every LOD variant of
one asset** (all of `int_hwy_2wayb`/`~l1`/`~l2` read `20,846,200`) but
**identical between two entirely unrelated assets** — `fountain_a_large_01`
and `wallstair_4mthin_02` both read `23,812,808` — which a real per-name
hash could not produce by coincidence across only 18 distinct stems, and
every one of the 24 values has its high byte in `{0x00, 0x01}` (bounded
under ~24 million), which a uniformly-distributed 32-bit hash also would
not produce 24/24 times by chance. This rules out "asset name hash"
specifically without identifying what the field actually is. **Left
OPEN** — flagged here rather than guessed at, per this project's own
"decode what's confirmed" discipline.

#### What this settles, and what stays open

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Is the 12-byte inner element 3 `uint32_t` indices? | **REFUTED** — magnitudes in the billions, zero in-file vertex list to index into (0/258 co-occurrence with `count(+0x48)`), zero bound against `count(+0x70)` either (0/7,104) |
| Is it a unit-magnitude plane/normal descriptor? | **REFUTED** — only 8/2,368 (0.34%) magnitudes land near 1.0, noise-level |
| Is it 3 `float`s, a local-space `(x,y,z)` position? | **CONFIRMED — empirical** — closed-loop bit-exactness, asset-name/shape correspondence, and byte-identity across every duplicate tile placement (18/18), all measured over the complete 258-file/388-group/2,368-element population |
| Is each outer group specifically a *collision* boundary? | **HIGH CONFIDENCE — inferred**, unchanged from `spec-physics-format.md` §4.3's existing tier — not independently re-derived here |
| What does the outer record's `+0x04` field mean? | **OPEN** — confirmed to be real, populated, non-hash-shaped data (correction to §4.2's "pad" reading), not decoded |

#### The new API, and how it was verified

`include/sr3clmesh/level_mesh.h` gains `struct Vec3 { float x, y, z; }` and
`LevelMesh::group88Positions(const NestedEntry&, ByteView content) const`,
which decodes one `group88()` entry's inner list as little-endian float
triples. It throws `FormatError` if handed an entry whose `innerStride`
is not exactly `kStride88Inner` (12) — `group88()` and `groupFc()` share
the `NestedEntry` type but have different inner strides (12 vs. 4), so
this guards against the one easy way to call it on the wrong group and
silently misdecode instead of failing loudly. `LevelMesh`'s own parsing
logic is unchanged — this is a pure decode layer on top of the existing,
already-verified `group88()` placement.

Two new tests in `tests/synthetic_clmesh_test.cpp` (now **28** tests, the
same 20th synthetic suite, `sr3clmesh_tests`):
`testGroup88PositionsDecodeAsFloatTriples` (a 3-point fixture using real
values from this section's own `int_hwy_2wayb~l1`/`fountain_a_large_01`
samples, checked bit-exact) and
`testGroup88PositionsMutationWrongStrideThrows` (the new load-bearing
rule's mutation case — a `groupFc()` entry must be rejected, not
misdecoded as if it were a `group88()` one).

**The mutation test's first draft was itself vacuous, caught the same way
this project's own methodology says to catch one** — worth recording
because it is a clean, small example of the exact trap `HANDOFF.md` §3
warns about. The first fixture used a `groupFc` entry sized `{1, 0, 0}`,
whose single 4-byte element sits right at the tail's real end; with the
stride guard temporarily deleted (`if (false && ...)`), the test **still
reported `[ok]`** — not because the guard was doing anything, but because
reading 12 bytes from that position ran past EOF and `ByteView`'s own
bounds check threw first, for an unrelated reason. Rebuilding with the
guard deleted and confirming the test still passed exposed this before it
shipped; the fixture was changed to `{1, 4, 4}` (plenty of real trailing
bytes after the entry under test, so a 12-byte read lands inside the
buffer instead of past it), and *that* version, re-checked the same way,
genuinely fails (`CHECK FAILED (expected throw)`) when the guard is
removed and genuinely passes when it is restored. Both states were run
and observed, not assumed.

**Full suite, guard restored, final state:**

```
build_verify\sr3clmesh_tests.exe
  ... 28 / 28 tests [ok], including the 26 pre-existing ones — zero regression
All synthetic clmesh-format tests passed.
```

#### How to re-verify

```
tools\validation\build_one.bat dump_group88          # from PowerShell
build_verify\dump_group88.exe <sr3_city_0.vpp_pc> <sr3_city_1.vpp_pc> <out-dir>
```

`<out-dir>/group88_dump.csv` carries every one of the 2,368 inner elements
(archive, stem, outer/inner index and offset, all three interpretations,
raw hex); the population-level stats in this section are printed to
stdout at the end of the run. Expect ~35-40 minutes for both archives
combined (I/O bound, like every other archive walk in this project) —
much less than `validate_clmesh.exe`'s ~1 hour **per archive**, because
this tool skips `.glmesh_pc` decompression for the >99.7% of files that
never populate `+0x88`.

#### Independent re-verification (dispatching session, same day)

Rebuilt `level_mesh.cpp`, the 28-test synthetic suite, and
`dump_group88.cpp` from source myself (own `.exe`s) — 28/28 tests pass,
zero regression. Ran `dump_group88` myself against `sr3_city_0` alone:

Went one step further than re-running the numbers: opened the written

### 9.61 Standing policy, given directly by the user: when only an invented fix is left, stop and defer — do not fabricate

**Context.** With today's clmesh/reggies/count(+0x88) threads closed, the
backlog was surveyed for a next item. Two candidates turned out to be
dead ends worth recording rather than silently dropping: `shaders.vpp_pc`'s
mode-(a) extraction failure (this session's own `vpp::Container` reader
independently reproduces Team A's exact 108/1693 success rate — a real,
useful cross-confirmation — but `spec-vpp-container.md` §3.2/§3.5-§3.8
already document three exhausted passes on this exact question, including
a live-debugger dynamic-analysis pass across broad real gameplay, with the
team's own conclusion that the remaining gap needs either instruction-level
register tracing or reverse-engineering a general deserialization
framework — both explicitly declined as bigger than the original
question; nothing here changes that, and it is not being pursued further
from the file side either) and vehicle material↔run association (§ table
above — search space exhausted, next step is a whole-binary disassembly
scan Team A itself flagged out of scope for a session).

That left the `.anim_pc` full-skeleton rendering fragmentation
(§9.56.2-§9.56.4) as the one big, real, unresolved item — and it is
unresolved in a specific way: not "more measurement would help" but "both
teams have exhausted the investigation and the only remaining move is a
rendering workaround" (dual-quaternion skinning, corrective vertex
smoothing, or similar) that would be the first thing in this renderer not
reproducing anything the shipped engine is confirmed to actually do.

**Put to the user directly rather than decided unilaterally.** Asked
whether to (a) implement a workaround now, clearly labeled as a
non-authentic engineering choice, (b) leave it as a documented limitation
and revisit later, or (c) something else. **The user's answer: skip items
that would end up requiring an invented fix, get them into their best
possible shape without inventing anything, and revisit later.**

**Standing policy this establishes, recorded so it generalizes correctly
next time this shape recurs (not just for this one item):** when an
investigation reaches the point where the confirmed facts run out and
only a plausible-but-unconfirmed engineering guess is left, stop there.
Polish the item's own documentation to reflect exactly what's confirmed
vs. still open (done for this item — §9.56.4's write-up already meets
this bar, nothing further added or invented into it), mark it explicitly
DEFERRED rather than closed or silently dropped, and do not fill the gap
with a workaround — even a clearly-labeled one — without asking first.
This is the same discipline as the project's existing hard rule (spec-*.md
and real data only, never the binary directly) applied one level further
out, to what the renderer itself is allowed to do when the authentic
answer is confirmed unrecoverable. See the RESUME table's `.anim_pc`
playback and keyframe-payload rows, both updated to point here.

**Not touched, not closed, explicitly waiting:** the anim-seam workaround
question itself. Nothing about §9.56.2-§9.56.4's findings changed — the
cross-limb displacement is still CONFIRMED real and still genuinely
unexplained; this section only records the decision about what to do
about that fact, not a new finding about the fact itself.

### 9.62 Multi-object scene composition + free-roaming camera — engine/renderer infrastructure, not format reading, built on already-confirmed readers only

**Why this item, and why now.** With §9.61 closing the readily-available
format-reading backlog (the remaining open items all need either new
information from Team A or are explicit user-deferred decisions), the
user pointed at a different, equally-legitimate category of "full recomp"
scope work that depends on nothing new from Team A: the renderer only
ever supported one object at a time, camera-orbiting that one object's own
bounding box. Every format this touches — character meshes, vehicle
geometry — already has a confirmed, working reader in this codebase. This
is engineering on top of already-correct decodes, not reverse-engineering,
and **no reader's own parsing/decode logic was touched** (`sr3mesh`,
`sr3rig`, `sr3geometry`, `sr3vehicle` are used exactly as `mesh`/`pose`
already use them, with zero changes to any of their source files).

**What was built, all four deliverables from the brief:**

1. **World/model transform** (`include/sr3render/mesh_renderer.h`,
   `src/mesh_renderer.cpp`). `MeshRenderer::draw()`, `drawTextured()` and
   `drawSkeleton()` each gained a trailing `const float world[16] = nullptr`
   parameter. **Design choice, recorded per the brief's request**: composed
   CPU-side into a single `world * viewProjection` matrix before upload,
   reusing the shader's existing single-matrix constant-buffer field
   unchanged, rather than adding a second `world` field to the HLSL cbuffer
   and multiplying on the GPU. This was chosen specifically because it
   touches nothing about `kShaderSource`/`Constants` that every existing
   draw call already depends on — the alternative would have meant editing
   the shader contract of a renderer explicitly flagged as
   already-confirmed-correct elsewhere. New helpers `multiplyMatrix4x4()`
   and `buildWorldMatrix(x,y,z,yawRadians,scale,outMatrix)` (uniform scale
   → yaw → translate, row-major row-vector convention matching the
   existing view/projection matrices) do the composition.
   **`world == nullptr` (every pre-existing call site) is byte-for-byte the
   old code path** — same pointer copied into the constant buffer with no
   multiply — not merely "expected to render the same."

2. **Scene composition** (`tools/sr3_viewer.cpp`, the new `scene` command).
   Exactly what the brief asked for and nothing more: `struct PlacedObject
   { std::unique_ptr<sr3render::MeshRenderer> renderer; float world[16];
   std::string label; }` plus `std::vector<PlacedObject>` — no file format,
   no serialization, positions are fixed documented constants
   (`buildWorldMatrix` calls in `runScene()`). Loads two real character
   meshes (any `<name>.ccmesh_pc` from `characters.vpp_pc`, unposed —
   deliberately NOT using the `.anim_pc` full-skeleton playback path; see
   "what was deliberately left out" below) and one real vehicle
   (`sr3vehicle::Vehicle::parse()` → `GeometryBlock::parseAt(meshRegionOffset())`
   → `sr3mesh::MeshBlock::parse()`, the exact pattern
   `tools/validation/validate_vehicle.cpp` already uses), each through its
   own `MeshRenderer` instance (one GPU buffer set per object; the shader
   compiles three times at startup, which is a non-issue at this scene
   size). One shared depth buffer, owned by `scene[0]`'s renderer and bound
   manually via `context->OMSetRenderTargets(1,&rtv,depthView)` after
   `SwapChain::bind()` — `MeshRenderer::draw()` only sets depth STATE
   (test/write mode), never a depth VIEW, so any renderer in the scene can
   own the shared view.

3. **Free-roaming camera** (`mesh_renderer.h`/`.cpp`'s new
   `buildFreeViewProjection(eye, yaw, pitch, aspect, nearZ, farZ, outMatrix)`,
   `sr3_viewer.cpp`'s `runScene()` main loop). Keyboard fly controls via
   `GetAsyncKeyState` polled once per frame — **deliberately NOT** hooked
   into `sr3render::Window`'s `WM_KEYDOWN`/`WM_KEYUP` handling, since
   `window.h`'s own header comment is explicit that the message loop has
   exactly one deliberate input behaviour (Escape-to-close) and nothing
   else; polling needed zero changes to that already-working,
   already-used-by-every-other-command class. W/A/S/D move, Q/E down/up,
   arrow keys look, Shift = 3x speed, Escape closes (Window's existing
   behaviour). `buildOrbitViewProjection` and every command that uses it
   (`mesh`/`pose`/`animpose`) is **completely untouched** — this is an
   additional camera mode, not a replacement.

   **A real bug was caught and fixed before calling this done**: the
   movement loop's first-written `right` vector
   (`{cos(yaw), 0, -sin(yaw)}`) was checked against
   `buildFreeViewProjection`'s own `cross(forward, worldUp)` derivation
   rather than trusted to agree with it by construction — it did not. The
   view matrix's actual right vector is `(-forward.z, 0, forward.x)`,
   the exact negation of what the movement code first used, which would
   have made D/A strafe backwards relative to what the camera itself calls
   right/left. Fixed to derive `right` the same way
   `buildFreeViewProjection` does (`{-forward[2], 0, forward[0]}`,
   normalised) — recorded here because it is exactly the kind of
   plausible-looking, silently-wrong code this project's own methodology
   exists to catch, this time in new engineering rather than format
   decoding.

4. **The `scene` command** demonstrating all three together — see
   verification below.

**Regression-safety verification, exact numbers:**

* **Synthetic suites: 20/20 green, 0 failures** — re-ran every
  `build_verify\*_tests.exe` after these changes; identical to the
  session-open baseline I captured before touching anything (same 20
  suite names, same "N passed" tail lines). Expected and unsurprising:
  this task never touched any reader source (`sr3mesh`, `sr3rig`,
  `sr3geometry`, `sr3vehicle`, `sr3clmesh`, `sr3anim` sources are
  byte-for-byte what they were before), so none of their synthetic suites
  could have regressed — confirmed rather than assumed.
* **Pixel-identical regression check on existing commands (deliverable
  1's actual safety requirement) — not visual, BYTE-IDENTICAL (SHA-256
  match) before vs. after the `world`-parameter change**, on the real
  invocations these captures already used earlier this project:
  `sr3_viewer mesh characters.vpp_pc brad.ccmesh_pc out.png --mode checker`,
  `sr3_viewer pose characters.vpp_pc brad.ccmesh_pc brad.rig_pc out --mode checker`
  (both `_bind.png` and `_posed.png`), and
  `sr3_viewer animpose characters.vpp_pc brad.ccmesh_pc brad.rig_pc preload_anim.vpp_pc auto_entrl_extct_shot.anim_pc out --mode checker --times 0,0.5`
  (`_bind.png` and both `_t*_frac*.png` frames) — **6/6 outputs SHA-256
  identical, before vs. after.** This is the strongest form of the check
  the brief asked for: not "looks the same", provably the same bytes.
* Rebuilt from source for real (not assumed): `cl.exe /std:c++17 /EHsc
  /O2 /W4` against `src/mesh_renderer.cpp` and `tools/sr3_viewer.cpp`,

  `CMakeLists.txt`'s `sr3_viewer` target was updated to add `sr3vehicle`

  "keep the hand-built binary and the CMake graph in step" lesson §9.56.1

— this project keeps its root sources-only, and no prior `sr3_viewer`

**An honest note on what the vehicle screenshot looks like, checked

#### Independent re-verification (dispatching session, same day) — and a real build-hygiene hazard found along the way

Read the actual diff before trusting the "byte-for-byte the old path"
claim: `src/mesh_renderer.cpp`'s `draw()` sets `wvp = viewProjection`
directly and only calls `multiplyMatrix4x4()` when `world != nullptr` —
confirmed at the source level, not just from the agent's own test run,
that every pre-existing call site (which all still pass no `world`
argument) takes the untouched pointer with zero extra arithmetic.

Then tried to independently re-link `mesh_renderer.cpp`/`sr3_viewer.cpp`
from source myself, the same way every other verification pass today
did — and hit a real crash (`0xC0000005` access violation) on the `mesh`
command, the simplest possible regression case. **Root cause, confirmed
by timestamp: not a bug in this task's own work.** `build_verify/`'s
shared object pool had `mesh_block.obj` compiled at `01:15` while
`include/sr3mesh/mesh_block.h`/`src/mesh_block.cpp` had just been
modified at `17:14` — by the Fable 5.1 agent working the animation-seam
task **concurrently, in the same shared `build_verify/` tree**, not by
anything in this task. My from-scratch link mixed a stale `mesh_block.obj`
against fresh headers mid-edit and got a real but unrelated ABI mismatch
(`mesh` reported "groups: NOT located" instead of the correct "4 LOD
group(s)", then crashed on the actual draw call). **Recorded as a general
lesson, not specific to this task**: `build_verify/`'s shared object pool
is not safe to re-link from while a second agent may be mid-edit on a
file either side depends on — check for another live background agent
before attempting a from-scratch rebuild, or verify against the
already-built, already-working `.exe` instead of re-linking.

### 9.63 The `.anim_pc` full-skeleton fragmentation is SOLVED, and it was never a seam: vertex blend indices index a per-mesh BONE PALETTE, not the rig, and rig→mesh is (−x,−y,−z) — a format finding read from the file, not an invented fix

**Dispatch context, stated so the §9.61 policy is seen to be honoured.**
The user directly authorised one serious attempt at the deferred
§9.56.2–§9.56.4 item, explicitly lifting §9.61's "no invented fix" rule
for this one task, with dual-quaternion skinning / corrective smoothing
named as acceptable *clearly-labelled engineering choices*. The brief's
own item 4 said: before assuming a generic fix is the only path, re-read
the exact vertex/weight data for the worst offending pairs. **That is
where the answer was. Nothing was invented. No DQS, no smoothing, no
weight floor — the "seam" is a decode error in how every prior section
read blend indices, and the correction is a field in the shipped
`.ccmesh_pc` that both teams' specs had already located but not
identified.** §9.61's policy stands untouched; this is a decode.

#### 9.63.1 The first measurement that gave it away

A per-bone cluster check — the same per-bone correspondence test §9.13
recommends over bounding boxes, but tabulated per bone rather than
summarised as one median — on `brad.ccmesh_pc` with blend indices read
as rig indices (every prior section's reading), mesh-space rest via
§9.13's `(x,−y,−z)`:

| blend index → rig bone (direct reading) | dominant verts | centroid of those verts | distance centroid↔rest |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15 `r-toe0` | 560 | (−0.03, **1.68**, −0.04) — the head | **1.70 m** |
| 8 `spine2` | 264 | (−0.15, **0.04**, −0.03) — a foot | 1.28 m |
| 13 `r-clavicle` | 61 | (−0.20, 0.02, 0.15) — a toe | 1.45 m |
| 21 `l-hand` | 40 | (**−0.66**, 0.97, 0.06) — the *right* hand | 1.25 m |
| 23 `l-finger1` | 27 | (−0.63, 0.97, 0.01) — right hand | 1.28 m |
| 48 `camfov` | 174 | (−0.56, 1.08, 0.00) — a wrist | 1.21 m |
| 50 `l-eye` | 171 | (−0.13, 0.85, 0.03) — a thigh | 0.87 m |
| 3 `l-thigh`, 6 `l-calf`, 9 `l-foot`, 35–39 `l-finger11..` | — | where they should be | 0.02–0.30 m |

A 1.7 m residual for 560 vertices on a 1.7 m character is not a weight-
painting choice. The full table (`diag_seam_pairs_brad.txt` in the
session scratchpad; the tool is a scratch diagnostic, its logic is now
`validate_bone_palette.cpp`'s cluster scorer) reads as a **permutation**
of the rig order: pelvis dropped, so `spine` onward shifts by one; every
l-/r- pair lands on its mirror; the hand-prop and upper-arm-twist-1 bones
absent; and the tail (`upperarmtwist2/3`, elbows, `foretwist1`,
`thightwist1`, knees, `calftwist1`) reached only after the finger bones.
Exactly the same permutation on `angel` and `brute_flamethrower`, offset
by two entries on `brad` (the eyes). **Under `(−x,−y,−z)` instead of
`(x,−y,−z)` the permutation becomes a monotonically increasing list of
rig indices with gaps** — the classic exporter output "the bones this
mesh uses, in rig order."

#### 9.63.2 The field, read directly from the shipped bytes

`brad.ccmesh_pc` (4,080 bytes; Mesh sub-block version field at `0x4F0`,
its `0x70` header at `0x500`, one 24-byte channel record at `0x570`):

```
0x538  (header +0x38)   38 00            u16 = 56
0x548  (header +0x48)   01 00            u16 = 1
0x588  (= records end)  01 02 03 04 05 06 07 08 09 0a 0b 0c 0d 0e 0f 11
                        13 14 15 16 17 18 19 1a 1c 1d 1e 1f 20 22 23 24
                        25 26 27 28 29 2a 2b 2c 32 33 34 35 36 37 38 39
                        3a 3b 3c 3d 3e 3f 40 41                        (56 bytes)
0x5C0                   38 00            [u8 count=56][u8 start=0]
```

= rig indices `[1..15, 17, 19..26, 28, 29..32, 34, 35..44, 50, 51, 52..65]`
— slot for slot the list §9.63.1's clusters predicted (`[0]`=pelvis,
`[15]`=head, `[40],[41]`=eyes, `[42],[43]`=upperarmtwist2, `[46],[47]`=
elbows, `[55]`=r-calftwist1), and 56 = brad's highest blend index + 1.
`angel` (`0x520`: 54; list omits 45–51 entirely — no eyes on a 66-bone
rig) and `brute_flamethrower` (`0x5B8`: 53; `[…44, 51, 53, 54…64]`,
skipping that rig's differently-placed camera bones) read the same way.
**No bone-name strings and zero bone-hash hits anywhere in the file** — the
mesh does not name bones, it lists their indices in *its paired rig*.

**This is the array `spec-geometry-format.md` §4.1.1 already confirmed by
disassembly** ("`+0x38`/`+0x40` … a u16-count-gated array … HYPOTHESIS:
a plain 16-bit index buffer") and `spec-vertex-format.md` §2 does not
list. Presence and gating were right; the content is the bone palette.
The sibling `+0x48`/`+0x50` array ("flat count × 2 bytes") is the **set
table**: `count` two-byte descriptors `[u8 count][u8 start]`, one per
palette set (§9.63.7).

**The mechanism, in one sentence:** a vertex whose blend lane says `k`
is skinned to rig bone `palette[k]`; the shader's matrix palette is built
per mesh from this list, which is why the vertex format's 8-bit index and
the `.rig_pc` spec's observation "highest blend index 63 against 66–68-
bone rigs" both hold — the runtime resolves palette slot → rig bone via
this table, and clips bind to rig indices (`spec-rig-format.md` line 116)
on the other side of it.

#### 9.63.3 Why four prior "confirmations" all missed it — each one is a §3 lesson already on the books

* **`spec-rig-format.md` "Blend indices address this bone array directly.
  There is no palette indirection. [CONFIRMED — empirical]"** was a
  *constant-shift* test (−6…+6). A permutation is not a shift; no shift
  fits it, and shift 0 wins by being least wrong. The test could not
  have found what was there.
* **§9.13's `(x,−y,−z)`** was fitted with direct indices. Direct index
  `k` lands on the *mirror* bone for every l-/r- pair (the palette drops
  pelvis, so pairs shift by one and swap), and an X-sign error un-mirrors
  it — two wrong readings cancelling on exactly the bones that could have
  discriminated. That fit's own weak numbers (0.68 m mean residual, 14.9%
  rank test, "not 100% and should not be") were the tell, rationalised
  rather than chased. §3's "a failed test with two plausible causes is
  evidence about neither" — this time the *passing* test had two causes.
* **§9.53.1 / §9.56's single-bone isolation renders "looked plausible."**
  Rotating rig bone `k`'s subtree moves the vertices whose blend index is
  `k` — a coherent chunk of *some* limb, just usually not the one named.
  A rigid chunk moving rigidly looks like a joint. M3b coherence measured
  exactly that and could not tell which limb it was.
* **§9.14's M4/M5 "near-degenerate rest edge, 328×, identical under
  scramble"** and **§9.56.1's "`l-finger1` 4–19 mm from `r-hand`"** were
  edges between adjacent fingers of the *same* hand, mis-attributed to
  two hands. Under the palette, blend slots 22/23 are `l-finger3`/
  `l-finger4`. Of course they are 4 mm apart.

#### 9.63.4 What was built — all opt-in, default path proven byte-identical

* `sr3mesh::MeshBlock::bonePalette()` / `bonePaletteDeclaredCount()` /
  `bonePaletteSets()` / `bonePaletteSetCountDeclared()` — additive,
  non-fatal on a truncated declaration (this parser is shared by six
  carriers whose populations were validated before the field was
  understood; a consumer compares size to declared count). Read only for
  g-backed blocks.
* `include/sr3rig/bone_palette.h` + `src/bone_palette.cpp` —
  `remapBlendIndicesThroughPalette()` (255 preserved; unmappable lanes →
  255/weight 0, counted two ways), `rigToMeshSpaceInverted()`,
  `conjugateToMeshSpaceInverted()` (M = −I; commutes, so a rig-space
  `(R, t)` becomes `(R, −t)` — §9.56's single-final-conjugation argument
  holds unchanged since −I is its own inverse). **`pose.h` and
  `animated_pose.h` are untouched** except a comment beside
  `rigToMeshSpace()` pointing here.
* `sr3_viewer animpose --bone-palette`, `probe_seam_absolute_displacement
  --bone-palette`. Both refuse a multi-set block rather than guess.
  **Without the flag: my no-flag `brad` render is md5-identical
  (`b23158f5…`) to the prior session's `animpose_verify/
  brad_noCam_t0_frac1.00.png`, and the bind renders identical
  (`28984320…`) with and without the flag.** The default path is
  pixel-for-pixel what every earlier section measured.
* Tests: `sr3mesh_tests` gains `testBonePalette` (fixture from the
  layout statement, not the parser; decoys at `+0x3A`/`+0x4A`, front/back
  entries pinned, truncation, two sets, a `[count,start]`-vs-u16 mutation);
  new 21st suite **`sr3bonepalette_tests`** (4 tests, every expectation
  hand-derived in the comments, a deliberately-wrong case per rule:
  identity remap, §9.13 conjugation, no-remap, a 2-bone end-to-end with
  both single-error mutations asserted to land elsewhere). Registered in
  `CMakeLists.txt`. **21/21 suites green, re-run by me on the final

* Real-data regression, re-run on the final objects: vehicles **372/372
  parsed, 5,629,811 vertices, normals unit 5,629,811/5,629,811**;
  characters **549/549 paired, 0 failed, g-length 549/549, stride law

* One build-hygiene finding of my own: adding members to `MeshBlock`
  changed its size, and the first test relink crashed `sr3zone_tests`/

  and `level_mesh.obj` were still compiled against the old layout. Fixed

  shared object pool is confirmed from this end. The final
  `build_verify/sr3_viewer.exe` was relinked after all edits on both

#### 9.63.7 Multi-set meshes: fully decoded structure, one OPEN selector

> **SUPERSEDED for its OPEN item, 2026-09-13 — see §9.63.10.** The selector
> is a stored field: an 8-byte record per draw range immediately after the
> 20-byte draw-range array, `u32` set index at `+0x00`. Everything below
> still stands as measurement (the set structure, the vote table, the
> material-id and LOD-group refutations, the contiguous-vertex-block
> observation); only "not stated anywhere this reader has decoded" is now
> false, and the reason is that no pass had walked the bytes between the
> draw ranges and the block's own declared c-length.

46/318 meshes carry 2–3 sets. Descriptor bytes, e.g. `angie` `3b 00 0d 3b`
= {59 @ 0}, {13 @ 59}; `liilian` = {64@0}, {62@64}, {12@126}, 64+62+12 =
138 = its palette. `angie`'s set 1 is `[8, 12, 17, 73…82]` — spine2, neck,
head and the ten face bones: **the face submesh gets its own set** because
the head needs bones the body set has no room for. A blend index in a
set-1 range is an index into *that* set (S4 above: max blend index <
largest set, 318/318).

**Which draw range uses which set is not stated anywhere this reader
has decoded.** Measured instead: every draw range votes near-unanimously
(e.g. `angie` g0 r6: 0 / 866; `gus` g0 r4: 34 / 1,251), and the set-1
ranges always form one **contiguous vertex block** (`angie` 3411–4601,
`joshbirk` 2889–3931, `gus` 1369–3151). It is **not** the material id
(`gus` material 1 → set 1 in groups 0–3, set 0 in group 8), **not** the
LOD group (`joshbirk`: 1 group, 2 sets), **not** in the group records'
five spare `u32`s (all zero on `angie`), and **not** in the 20-byte draw
range (all five fields accounted for). Untested candidate: the per-
material records after the Mesh sub-block (`spec-vertex-format.md` §8.3,
contents OPEN) — the sweep's per-range vote table (`sweep_all2.txt`) is
the ground truth any rule must reproduce across all 46. Until then the
flag refuses multi-set meshes with a message; **every mesh used in
§9.56.x (`brad`, `angel`, `brute_flamethrower`, `reggies`, `joleen`)
is single-set** — `nightblade` is two-set ({58@0},{26@58}), which is the
likely explanation for its §9.14 M3b anomaly (not re-measured here).

#### 9.63.8 What this supersedes, and what it does not

* **§9.56.1–§9.56.4's conclusion ("a real mesh-topology property; near-
  degenerate cross-limb clearances; no seam-avoidance mechanism found on
  either side") is RETRACTED in full.** The pipeline (§9.53/§9.56.1) was
  and is correct; its *input* — blend indices as rig indices — was wrong.
  There is no seam for the shipped engine to avoid, which is why Team A
  found nothing: they were looking for the fix to a defect that does not
  exist. §9.56.3's rotation-range statistics are still true numbers about
  the clips; they no longer "raise the stakes" on anything.
* **§9.56.4's side-finding "minority blend weight on the camera-rig
  bones contaminates body vertices"** is an artifact of the same misread:
  no palette contains 46–49; those "camera lanes" were slots 46–49 =
  elbows and `foretwist1`. The measurement was right about what it saw and
  wrong about what it was.
* **§9.14 / §9.53.1's "near-degenerate rest edge" M4/M5 reading** — same
  class, same retraction. §9.14's M3b lesson (a metric that does not move
  under scramble measures something else) stands on its own.
* **§9.13's `(x,−y,−z)` is superseded for skinning by `(−x,−y,−z)`.**
  Left in `pose.h` unchanged, with a pointer; every pre-§9.63 harness
  reproduces its recorded numbers. Note the transform is a point
  inversion (det −1): the mesh is a mirror of the rig's frame, or the
  rig's l-/r- naming is mirrored relative to the mesh's — the skinning
  math is identical either way (M = −I commutes with every rotation), so
  rendering is unaffected; which hand the *game* calls "left" is a
  question for gameplay logic later, not for this section.
* **§9.58's A-pose finding is unaffected** — droop angles are X-sign-
  independent by construction.
* **`spec-rig-format.md` "Blend indices address this bone array
  directly. There is no palette indirection."** — WRONG, to relay to Team
  A with the byte offsets above. **`spec-geometry-format.md` §4.1.1** —
  `+0x38`/`+0x40` is the bone palette (u8 rig indices), `+0x48`/`+0x50`
  the set table (`[u8 count][u8 start]`); "16-bit index buffer" was the
  hypothesis and is refuted. **`spec-vertex-format.md` §2's header table**
  should list both fields. Array 3 of the outer six-array structure,
  seen in passing on `brad` (11 × 40 bytes: `[u32 index][u32 rig bone]
  [quat][pos][radius]`, bones 1,3,4,5,6,7,12,16,18,19,20 = pelvis, thighs,
  calves, spine, neck, upper arms, forearms), looks like per-bone
  collision/ragdoll capsules — noticed, not chased, [HYPOTHESIS].
* **Not changed: the default.** The palette path is opt-in by the brief's
  own rule. Making it the default is the natural next step and is a
  decision for whoever verifies this independently; the evidence for it
  is the whole of this section, and the argument against is only that
  46/318 meshes need §9.63.7 resolved first.

#### A real scoping gap this cross-team exchange found, fixed same day

Team A's own vehicle-specific finding (a `+0x48/+0x50` u16 group-pointer
table on VEHICLE meshes, unrelated to skinning) raised a precise
question worth its own record: does this section's write-up, or the
actual parsing code, treat "bone palette" as a universal meaning for
these two header slots across `MeshBlock`'s six carrier formats, or
correctly scope it to skinned character meshes specifically? **Answer,
checked against the code, not just the prose: it did not scope it, and
the gap was real, not hypothetical.** `bonePaletteDeclaredCount_` was
being read and `bonePalette_`/`bonePaletteSets_` populated for **any**
g-backed mesh sub-block with a non-zero count at header `+0x38` —
unconditionally, not gated by the channel's `hasSkinning` layout flag.
Nothing currently calls `bonePalette()` on a non-character carrier
(vehicles, clmesh, trees, zones), which is why this hadn't produced a
wrong result yet and `validate_vehicle.exe`'s regression check never
caught it — but a future caller on a non-skinned mesh would have
silently received semantically wrong data if that carrier's own +0x38
slot happened to hold a real, unrelated value for some other reason.

**Fixed in `src/mesh_block.cpp`**: population of `bonePalette_`/
`bonePaletteSets_` is now additionally gated on at least one channel in
the block having `layoutInfoFor(layoutCode).hasSkinning == true`. Purely
additive — the bulk-segment cursor math a few lines below is computed
from `channelCount` alone, not from whether the palette was read, so
this cannot change behaviour for any of the five other carriers, and
does not affect the `MeshBlock` struct's size (no header change, no
stale-object risk this time). Also broadened the API doc comment on
`bonePalette()` to state the scope explicitly (confirmed for skinned
character meshes; other carriers may use the same header slot for
something unrelated) rather than reading as a universal claim.

**Verified**: rebuilt `mesh_block.cpp` alone at `/W4` (zero warnings),
relinked `sr3mesh_tests`/`sr3bonepalette_tests`/`validate_bone_palette`
against the new object — all three green, all four bone-palette tests
pass, and the 237-triple `characters.vpp_pc` population sweep reproduces
identically (237/237 across every invariant) — a complete no-op for the
population this feature was built and validated against, as expected
since every one of those 237 triples already has a skinned channel.
`validate_vehicle.exe` re-run: 372/372, 5,629,811 vertices, normals unit
5,629,811/5,629,811 — unchanged.
