#### 9.63.10 §9.63.7's per-draw-range palette-set selector is CLOSED — it is a stored field, an 8-byte record per draw range immediately after the 20-byte draw ranges, and the 46 multi-set meshes now render

**One sentence.** The Mesh sub-block's c-side does not end at the draw-range
array: immediately after the `totalRanges × 20` bytes of draw ranges come
`totalRanges × 8` more bytes, one record per draw range in the same flat
file order, and the **`u32` at each record's `+0x00` is the index of the
bone-palette SET that range's blend indices address** — after which the
block's own check value repeats in the next 4 bytes and `meshOffset +
cLength` lands exactly there. §9.63.7's OPEN item is a **field discovery**,
not a decoding rule, and not a negative result.

**Where it sits, spelled out so it can be checked by hand:**

```
meshOffset + 0x10                     the 0x70 Mesh header
  ... channel records (channelCount × 24)
  ... bone palette (u16 count at header +0x38) × 1 byte
  ... set descriptors (u16 count at header +0x48) × 2 bytes  [u8 count][u8 start]
  align 16
  ... group records (u32 count at header +0x04) × 0x30 bytes
  ... draw ranges (sum of the groups' range counts) × 20 bytes   <-- spec Sec8.2 stops here
  ... PALETTE-SET SELECTOR: same range count × 8 bytes           <-- Sec9.63.10
         +0x00  u32  palette set index for this draw range
         +0x04  u32  zero in every shipped record
  ... u32 = the block's check value again
  == meshOffset + cLength
```

`gus` (mesh at `0x588`, 11 groups, 34 ranges, sets `{50@0}` `{35@50}`), read
by hand out of the shipped bytes: ranges end at `0xb38`, and `0xb38` onwards
is 34 eight-byte records of which only entries 4, 9, 14 and 19 carry a
non-zero first byte (`01`), then `0xc48` = the check value, then
`meshOffset + cLength = 0xc4c`. `angie` (mesh at `0x570`, 4 groups × 7
ranges, `{59@0}` `{13@59}`): ranges end at `0x950`, the `01`s sit at
`0x980`, `0x9b8`, `0x9f0`, `0xa28` — stride 0x38 = 7 records — i.e. range 6
of each of the four LOD groups, which is exactly `angie`'s face submesh.

##### How it was found — an automated field search, not a guess-and-check list

The previous pass ruled out the material id, the LOD group, the draw-range
record's own fields and the group record's spare `u32`s one at a time.
Rather than continue that list, `tools/validation/diag_palette_set_selector.cpp`
inverts it: take the per-range majority-vote set sequence §9.63.7 already
established as ground truth, then scan the **whole c-file** for any
(offset, stride, element size) over 23 strides × {u8, u16, u32} × every byte
offset in the file, and report every position whose values **induce exactly
the ground-truth partition of the ranges** — `v[i] == v[j]` iff
`truth[i] == truth[j]`. Partition-matching rather than literal matching
matters: the stored value could have been a set start, a set count, a
pointer, anything. Aggregated over the 46 multi-set meshes, one candidate
matched 34 of them and the next-best matched 8 (chance hits on the meshes
with few ranges): `rngEnd+0 | stride 8 | u8` — i.e. offset zero relative to
the end of the draw ranges. Nothing else came close.

The 34/46 is the *vote oracle's* number, not the field's — the oracle is
noisy (see T6 below), and once the field itself is treated as the
hypothesis and tested on its own terms the numbers are much stronger.

##### Population evidence — 318 complete `.ccmesh_pc`/`.gcmesh_pc`/`.rig_pc` triples, the same population §9.63.6 used

`tools/validation/validate_palette_set_field.cpp`, over `characters`,
`preload_rigs`, `dlc1`, `dlc2`, `dlc3`: **318 triples, 272 single-set /
46 multi-set (43 two-set, 3 three-set)** — identical to §9.63.6/§9.63.9, so
the denominator is the established one, not a new slice.

**Structural (no skinning maths involved at all):**

| | |
|---|---|
| T1 the array fits in the content | **318 / 318** |
| T2 every value is a VALID set index (`< set count`) | **318 / 318** |
| T3 on single-set meshes every value is 0 | **272 / 272** |
| T4 `arrayEnd + 4 == meshOffset + cLength` | **318 / 318** (the gap histogram is the single bucket `4:318`) |
| T4b those 4 bytes ARE the block's own check value | **318 / 318** |
| value histogram over all 5,786 records | `0:5493  1:285  2:8` — never anything else, and 2 appears only on the three 3-set meshes |
| bytes `+0x01`..`+0x07` non-zero | **0 / 5,786 records**, all seven bytes |

T4/T4b are the load-bearing structural pair and they are **independent of
the skinning claim entirely**: they say the array's extent is exactly
`rangeCount × 8`, because the block's own declared c-length and its own
check-value bookend both land there and nowhere else. Before this, the
bytes between the draw ranges and `meshOffset + cLength` were simply not
walked by anything in this project.

**The content assertion — the strong one.** In the spirit of spec §8.2's
`minVertex`/`maxVertex` test (a declared fact about content that the reader
does not use to locate anything): the set a record names must be **big
enough for the blend indices that range's own vertices actually carry**,
`sets[field[i]].count > max blend index used by range i`.

| | ranges | meshes |
|---|---|---|
| **T5, the field** | **5,786 / 5,786** (all meshes); **1,085 / 1,085** (multi-set only) | **318 / 318** |
| control X1 — the same array read one record LATE | 899 / 1,085 | 0 / 46 |
| control X2 — one record EARLY | 924 / 1,085 | 0 / 46 |
| control Xr — a deterministic random set per range | 795 / 1,085 | 1 / 46 |
| control X3 — byte `+0x01` instead of `+0x00` (= "always set 0", since `+0x01` is always zero) | 1,083 / 1,085 | 45 / 46 |

X3 is reported because it is the honest null: "always set 0" nearly passes
T5, so T5 alone does **not** separate the field from the trivial reading.
What separates them is T6/T7 below, and the value histogram: a field that
were really "always 0" would not carry 285 ones and 8 twos, all of them
valid set indices, all of them on meshes that declare that many sets.

**T6 — agreement with the independent majority-vote oracle** (each vertex
votes for the (channel, set) pair that puts it nearest its dominant bone's
mesh-space rest position; this is §9.63.7's own ground truth, generalised to
pick the channel too because 15 of the 318 carry more than one skinned
channel):

| | ranges |
|---|---|
| **the field** | **1,070 / 1,085** — 37/46 meshes agree on every range |
| control X1 (+8) | 746 / 1,085 |
| control X2 (−8) | 740 / 1,085 |
| control X3 ("always set 0") | 801 / 1,085 |
| control Xr (random) | 594 / 1,085 |

**The 15 disagreements, classified rather than waved away** — in 14 of them
the ORACLE is the one that is wrong, and that is demonstrable, not asserted:

* **4 are ties.** For those ranges, both sets map every dominant slot the
  range's vertices actually use to the *same* rig bone, so the residual is
  identical and no residual-based oracle can pick. (`killbane_suit_grn`
  ranges 10/17, `linda` 26, `lindas` 25 — computed exactly by comparing the
  palette entries, not inferred from a numeric tie.)
* **3 are oracle-impossible.** The oracle named a set too small to hold the
  range's own blend indices, i.e. it scored only the sub-population of
  vertices that happened to fit: `zoey`/`zoeys` range 25 (max blend index 58,
  the oracle's set has 50 entries) and `angrytiger` range 3 (max blend 43,
  set has 23). The field's answer is the only structurally possible one.
* **7 are cross-channel.** On `alien_e01`/`alien_es01` the ranges in question
  draw from the block's *second* skinned channel, where the field's set both
  fits and scores better. Measured directly: `alien_e01` ranges 18/21/24/27
  on channel 1 have max blend index **5** against a set of exactly **6**
  entries and a mean residual of **0.17 m** under that set vs **0.72 m**
  under set 0. The residual metric cannot compare channels fairly — a 6-bone
  set is sparser than a 64-bone one and so always shows a larger mean
  distance-to-bone — so it picks the wrong channel, not the wrong set.
* **1 is genuine and is stated as such**: `cf_msspcl_suit` range 2, field
  says set 1, the oracle says set 0 by a **1.9 %** margin (0.1776 vs 0.1810).
  A 1.9 % margin on a metric whose spread across readings is 4× is not
  evidence against the field, but it is not evidence for it either.

**Meshes with no genuine disagreement: 45 / 46.**

**T7 — cluster residual on the 46 multi-set meshes** (median over vertices
per mesh, population median of those; each range scored on the channel the
oracle picked, so all four readings see the same vertices):

| reading | median | |
|---|---|---|
| **F — the field's per-range sets** | **0.1101 m** | |
| E — the per-range vote oracle | 0.1061 m | the upper bound any per-range rule can reach |
| C — the concatenated palette as one list (what §9.63.6 scored these at) | 0.1589 m | |
| D — shuffled palette, control | 0.6376 m | |

F beats C on **44 / 46** and D on **46 / 46**. The two where it does not
beat C are exactly `alien_e01`/`alien_es01`, the two multi-channel meshes,
for the reason above — their C figure is measured on channel 0 for ranges
that draw from channel 1, so it is not a like-for-like comparison rather
than a loss. **F is within 0.004 m of the oracle E**, which is the ceiling.

##### Carrier scope, checked before the reader was allowed to use it

§9.63's own "scoping gap" write-up is the reason this was done up front
rather than after. `tools/validation/diag_range_tail_carriers.cpp` runs the
*structural* test (gap == 4, and those 4 bytes are the block's check value)
on two carriers:

| carrier | blocks | gap == 4 | 4 bytes == check value | byte `+0x00` values | bytes `+1..+7` non-zero |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| character `.ccmesh_pc` | **549** (the whole `characters.vpp_pc` population, rigged or not) | **549 / 549** | **549 / 549** | only `0:6070 1:326 2:6` | **0** |
| vehicle `.ccar_pc` | **372** | **0 / 372** | **0 / 372** | 0–255, ~200 distinct | 20,731–29,366 per byte |

So the structure is **not** present in this form on vehicles, and the parser
is gated accordingly (`hasSkinning`, exactly as `bonePalette()` already is).
This is the same shape of answer §9.63 reached for `+0x38`/`+0x48`: a
character-mesh meaning, not a universal Mesh-sub-block one.

##### Is a per-vertex remap even well defined? — measured, and it is not always

A CPU skinning path holds one vertex array, so it can apply only one set per
vertex. That is sound only if no *drawn* triangle reaches a vertex from two
ranges naming different sets. Counting **non-degenerate triangles only** (a
strip's stitch indices name neighbours it never draws, spec §8.1 — counting
raw indices reports conflicts that do not exist):

| | conflicts | clean meshes |
|---|---|---|
| draw group 0 (the LOD a renderer draws) | **6 vertex uses, all on one mesh** | **317 / 318** |
| all draw groups | 14,736 | 315 / 318 |

`reynolds` genuinely shares 6 drawn vertex uses between two sets **inside
group 0** and cannot be skinned from a single vertex array;
`alien_e01`/`alien_es01` conflict only in LOD groups the renderer does not
draw. So the honest scope of the render fix is **45 of the 46**, with
`reynolds` still refusing and saying exactly why.

##### What was built

* **`sr3mesh::MeshBlock::drawRangePaletteSets()`** — additive, one `uint32_t`
  per draw range in flat `drawGroups()` order. Populated only when the block
  has a bone palette (so, only for skinned character meshes), the draw groups
  were located, the array fits, and **every** entry is a valid set index;
  otherwise left EMPTY and non-fatal, same contract as `bonePalette()`, for
  the same reason (six carrier formats share this parser). A consumer
  compares its size against its own flat range count rather than treating
  empty as all-zero.
* **`sr3rig::assignPaletteSetsPerVertex(mesh, vertexCount, groupIndex)`** —
  builds the per-vertex set assignment for one draw group, returns
  `usable == false` with a stated `problem` when it is ambiguous. It counts
  only non-degenerate triangles, for the reason above.
* **`sr3rig::remapBlendIndicesThroughPaletteSets(...)`** — the per-set
  counterpart of `remapBlendIndicesThroughPalette()`. Lane `k` of a vertex
  assigned set `s` maps to `palette[sets[s].start + k]`, and a lane index
  `>= sets[s].count` (note: the SET's count, not the palette's size) is
  dropped to 255/weight 0 and counted.
* **`sr3_viewer`: a fifth `SkinningMode`, `kPaletteMultiSet`**, reached from
  the existing `resolveSkinningMode()` (§9.63.9) with no new flag. A
  multi-set mesh takes it **only** when the selector array was read complete
  and valid; otherwise the old `kRefuseMultiSet` message stands, now naming
  the numbers (range count vs selector count) instead of naming §9.63.7 as
  open. `--legacy-skinning` still forces the pre-§9.63 reading on anything,
  including a mesh the new path refuses.
* **A third refusal, added after the fact because measuring it turned one
  up.** If any blend lane in the group being drawn carries an index its
  range's named set cannot hold, `pose`/`animpose` refuse. On a correct
  reading that count is **0 — measured on all 45 renderable multi-set
  meshes at draw group 0**. It is non-zero on the LOD groups of the two
  multi-channel meshes (`alien_e01 --group 4`: **2,213 lanes**), because
  those ranges draw from a channel the command did not upload. That is
  open item 3 below surfacing as a runtime symptom, and the right answer is
  to refuse, not to render 2,213 vertices silently skinned to nothing.
* **Nothing else changed.** `pose.h`, `animated_pose.h`, the single-set
  remap, `rigToMeshSpaceInverted()`, `runScene()`, the vehicle/zone/clmesh
  paths: untouched.

##### Tests, mutation-checked

* `sr3mesh_tests` gains **`testDrawRangePaletteSets`** — the fixture builder
  in `tests/synthetic_ccmesh_vertex_test.cpp` grew draw groups, draw ranges
  and the 8-byte tail, written from the stated layout rather than from the
  parser. Cases: flat file order across two groups; the `+0x04` word as a
  **decoy** (filled with 7, answer must not move); an out-of-range set index
  → the array is rejected WHOLE, not handed over with one bad entry; a
  non-zero `+0x01` → rejected (this pins the u32 reading, see OPEN below);
  the array absent entirely → empty and non-fatal, everything else still
  parses; a single-set mesh → all zeros.
* `sr3bonepalette_tests` gains **`testPerSetRemap`** (5th test) — hand-derived
  expectations, including two vertices with the **same lane values** in
  different sets that must land on **different rig bones**, a lane dropped
  because it exceeds its set's count even though the palette byte at that
  offset exists, and an **equivalence assertion**: one set covering the whole
  palette must reproduce `remapBlendIndicesThroughPalette()` exactly, so the
  multi-set path cannot drift from the single-set one.
* **Mutation check on the reader, not just on the fixture**: changing
  `readU32LE(tailAt + r*8)` to `readU32LE(tailAt + r*8 + 4)` in
  `src/mesh_block.cpp` turns `sr3mesh_tests` **RED with 4 failures**
  (the value check, the decoy, and both rejection cases), then reverted. The
  new test is not vacuous.

##### Two things that did NOT pan out, with their denominators

* **A purely geometric rule, with no stored field** (the brief's third
  shape of answer): "the only set whose count exceeds the range's own max
  blend index". Measured over the 46: it resolves **670 / 1,085** ranges
  uniquely and agrees with the vote on **667 / 670** of those — so it is not
  *wrong* — but **415 / 1,085** ranges are ambiguous (usually because a
  set-1 range uses only low blend indices, which both sets can hold), and it
  fully determines only **2 / 46** meshes. As a standalone rule it is a
  clear negative; as a cross-check on the field it is the T5 test above.
* **The material id.** `angie` looks like a clean `material 2 → set 1`
  mapping, and it is not one: reproduced §9.63.7's counter-example directly —
  `gus` material 1 maps to set 1 in draw groups 0–3 and to **set 0** in
  group 8. §9.63.7's refutation stands.

The named untried candidate in §9.63.7 — the per-material records after the
Mesh sub-block (`spec-vertex-format.md` §8.3) — turned out to be a level too
far out. The answer was inside the Mesh sub-block, in the region between the
draw ranges and the block's own declared end, which no pass had walked.

##### Tier, and what is still open

**Tier: [CONFIRMED — the field's location and meaning].** Its extent is
pinned by two independent structural facts on 318/318 and 549/549 (the
declared c-length and the check-value bookend); its values are valid set
indices on 318/318 and zero on every single-set mesh 272/272; it satisfies
an independent content assertion 1,085/1,085 against controls at
899/924/795; it agrees with the independent vote oracle on 1,070/1,085 with
14 of the 15 disagreements shown to be the oracle's error; its residual is
within 0.004 m of the oracle's ceiling and beats the concatenated reading
44/46 and a shuffled control 46/46; and **45 of the 46 meshes it unlocks
render, all 46 tried, where all 46 previously refused** — with zero dropped
blend lanes on every one of the 45.

**Still OPEN, stated plainly:**

1. **The record's second `u32` (`+0x04`).** Zero in **6,402 / 6,402** shipped
   records, so it carries no information this project can read. [HYPOTHESIS,
   not tested] the runtime overwrites it with a resolved pointer — Team A's
   `spec-geometry-format.md` §4.1.1 describes exactly that shape on the
   VEHICLE side (`meshHeader[+0x50] + storedValue * 2`, resolving into the
   `+0x48`/`+0x50` table), and on characters `+0x48`/`+0x50` *is* the set
   descriptor table, whose entries are 2 bytes — so `base + set*2` is the
   address of set descriptor `set`, and the stored value being the set index
   falls straight out. Suggestive, and a disassembly question, not a file one.
2. **The field's WIDTH.** u8, u16 and u32 are indistinguishable from the
   shipped population because `+0x01`..`+0x03` are always zero. This reader
   takes the u32 (so a non-zero `+0x01` is rejected rather than silently
   read as a small u8); the synthetic suite pins that choice deliberately.
3. **Which CHANNEL a draw range draws from**, on the 15/318 meshes with more
   than one skinned channel. Newly surfaced by this work, not previously
   recorded anywhere. It is clearly determinable empirically (`alien_e01`'s
   set-1 ranges fit channel 1 exactly: max blend index 5, set count 6) but
   nothing in this project reads it from the file. The renderer is unaffected
   today because it uploads one channel; a full recomp will need it.
4. **`reynolds`** — ~~1/318, genuinely shares 6 drawn vertices between two
   sets in group 0. Fixable by duplicating those vertices, which is a
   renderer engineering choice and not a decode, so it was not done; it
   refuses.~~ **RESOLVED 2026-09-14, §9.68**: exactly that fix, built.
   3 distinct vertex indices (4494/4496/4498) duplicated via a new
   `sr3rig::resolveVertexSetConflictsByDuplication()` +
   `sr3render::VertexDuplication`; `reynolds` now renders correctly (exit
   0, a real coherent posed figure, looked at directly), zero regression
   on every other mesh (MD5-identical old vs new binary on `angie`/`brad`).
   46/46 multi-set meshes now render, not 45/46.
5. **`cf_msspcl_suit` range 2** — the one genuine field-vs-oracle
   disagreement, 1.9 % margin. Not resolved either way.

##### To relay to Team A

* **`spec-vertex-format.md` §8.2** ends its layout at the 20-byte draw
  range. There is one more array: `rangeCount × 8` bytes immediately after,
  `u32` set index at `+0x00`, then the block's check value, then the
  declared c-length ends. Confirmed 549/549 on character meshes, absent on
  vehicles (0/372).
* **`spec-geometry-format.md` §4.1.1**'s vehicle-side note about group
  record `+0x28` pointing into the `+0x48`/`+0x50` table is what pointed at
  this; the character-side equivalent is per-DRAW-RANGE and lives in this
  tail array, not in the group record (`angie`'s five spare group `u32`s are
  all zero, confirmed again here). Worth their disassembly checking whether
  the two are the same loader code with different table contents.
* **`HANDOFF` §9.63.7's "[OPEN] the per-draw-range set selector" is now
  CLOSED**; §9.63.9's "the 46 multi-set meshes still refuse" is superseded

Rebuilt-object timestamps confirmed consistent (`mesh_block.obj`,
`sr3mesh_tests.exe`, `validate_bone_palette.exe` all within 35 seconds of
each other). Ran `sr3mesh_tests.exe`: green. Ran `validate_bone_palette.exe`
on `characters.vpp_pc`: 237/237, byte-identical to this project's own
pre-change baseline. Ran `sr3_viewer pose` on `gus` (a real multi-set
mesh, two sets) with **no flag**: prints `skinning: bone-palette SETS,
per draw range + (-x,-y,-z) [HANDOFF Sec9.63.10]` unprompted, and the

### 9.64 `.clmesh_pc` walks in ONE fully-computed pass — 100,384 / 100,384 (100.0000%), no search anywhere; and the search it replaced was not merely unnecessary, it was landing on the WRONG layout in 4.5% of the files it "found"

**Result: the target was hit exactly.** `sr3clmesh` was rewritten to
implement `spec-physics-format.md` §4.4.6's fully-computed single-pass
walk in place of §9.59's search-based tail-start. Over the **complete
shipped population — all five archives that carry the format, 100,384
entries — the walk lands EXACTLY on end-of-file in 100,384 / 100,384
(100.0000%)**, up from §9.59's searched model at 100,255 / 100,384
(99.8715%). The 129 entries that model could not place at all are gone:
**0 non-landing**. There is no search loop, no candidate-layout count,
and nothing left to disambiguate.

#### What changed in the reader

| | Before (§9.59) | After |
|---|---|---|
| `headEnd` | `bodyStart + 8·count(+0x48) + 8·count(+0x58) + Σ(Mesh sub-block sizes)` | **plus `Σ(count(+0x58) index-list blocks)`** — §4.4.6's correction to §4.4.1's published formula, which omitted array 2's own `FUN_00e401d0` payloads. This reader shipped the incomplete version |
| MIDDLE | OPAQUE. Reported as a byte range and nothing else | **Walked in full**: the `0x50`-byte record `thunk_FUN_00e3e590` lays down at the 16-aligned cursor, the material-set block (`FUN_00e40210`), the `materialCount × 8` lookup table at `R[+0x08]`, and two render-mesh groups (`FUN_00e3c4e0`), each a `0x60` header + index list + embedded Mesh sub-block + a u16 and a u8 array |
| `tailStart` | **SEARCHED** — every 8-aligned position from `headEnd` on, keep the ones landing on EOF, keep the earliest, report the ambiguity | **COMPUTED** — `= middleEnd()`. `findTail`, `TailSearch`, `probeTail` and `tailCandidateCount()` are deleted |
| gated `+0x78` pair | `kGatedPairBytes = 0`, explicitly labelled a parameter, not a finding | **Three real branches** (§4.4.6(f)): non-sentinel → `FUN_00748c70`'s block, cost = its OWN `+0x08` size field, per file; sentinel + flags bit → `FUN_00749ba0`'s **real collision hull**; otherwise nothing, not even an alignment |
| `FUN_00749ba0` | "builds a default from two hard-coded constants, consumes no cursor bytes" | **REFUTED by §4.4.6(f) and confirmed here on real bytes**: a vertex list, a u16 index list, an opaque blob and two vec3s, in **18,706 / 100,384** files. `hullVertices()` / `hullIndices()` decode the two lists at the element sizes §4.4.6(f) states outright |
| `FUN_00749b40` | 16-aligned only when its array is non-empty | **Aligns UNCONDITIONALLY**; only the array advance is conditional (§4.4.2(a) as amended by §4.4.6). The "empty array aligns nothing" rule still holds for `FUN_00749c40`/`cf0`/`d40`/`e80` |

`opaqueMiddleOffset()`/`opaqueMiddleLength()` become `middleOffset()`/
`middleEnd()`/`middleLength()` plus a `middle()` accessor returning the
located `MiddleLayout`; `tailLocated()` becomes `landsOnEof()`.
`headEnd()` keeps its name but **changes meaning** — it is now the end of
the whole HEAD, and the old "where the Mesh sub-blocks start" value is
`meshBlockStart()`. Any caller reading `headEnd()` as a Mesh anchor must
move to `meshBlockStart()`; `tools/validation/dump_group88.cpp` was
updated for the rename, and `resolveReferencedMeshes()` was fixed to
start from `meshBlockStart()` rather than `headEnd()`.

  SPEC-LITERAL one-cursor walk             0 / 100,384
```

The last two are this reader's own, not §4.4.6's — see "two ambiguities"
below — and the first of them carries its own confirmation: reading the
hull gate as mask `0x02` costs **exactly 18,706** landings, which is
**exactly** the number of files that take the collision-hull branch. A
wrong bit mask should cost precisely the files whose hull it then fails
to consume, and it does, to the entry. That is a much sharper result than
"the other mask scores worse".

**Five of those rows reproduce Team A's own independently-measured
figures to the digit** — §4.4.6(e) publishes 1,442 / 71,191 / 14,295 /
89,192 and 0 for the spec-literal walk, from a separate Python harness
against a separately-written implementation. Two independently-built
instruments agreeing on five six-figure population counts *exactly* is a
much stronger statement than either agreeing on the headline landing
rate, which is the one number both were aiming at.

Two controls deserve their own note, because they are the terms whose
shifts get *absorbed*. `MIDDLE start + 4` survives on 1,442 entries for a
structural reason, not a measurement artifact: the MIDDLE 16-aligns its
own start, so a +4 shift is a no-op precisely on the files whose
`headEnd` is NOT already 16-aligned — essentially the 1,454 files with a
non-empty HEAD. That is why the honest control for this term is `+16`,
which is 0. Same shape for `TAIL ± 16` against `FUN_00749b40`'s
unconditional align.

#### The finding that was NOT in the brief: the search was landing on the wrong layout

§9.59 reported a 4.3% multi-candidate ambiguity rate and said "the reader
keeps the earliest and which is right is not established". With a
computed answer now available, that can be checked rather than left open.
The searched model was re-implemented exactly as shipped (independently,
in Python, from this file's own description of it) and run beside the
computed walk on the 4,232-entry DLC population:

```
entries                                        4,232
computed walk lands on EOF                     4,232
SEARCHED model lands on EOF                    4,232
... and agrees with the computed tail start    4,043
... lands on EOF via a DIFFERENT layout          189   (4.5%)
searched-model candidate layouts    1: 4,047 | 2: 179 | 3: 6
```

The candidate-layout distribution **reproduces §9.59's own DLC row
exactly** (4,047 / 179 / 6), which is what makes the re-implementation
trustworthy as a stand-in for the shipped one. And the conclusion is
uncomfortable: **on DLC the searched model scored a perfect 4,232/4,232
"exact EOF landing" while being wrong about where the tail actually
starts in 189 of them.** An exact landing was never evidence of a correct
layout — it was evidence that *some* layout consumed the remaining bytes,
and the search's freedom to slide its start guaranteed one usually
existed.

The visible consequence: §9.59's trailing-group census reported **47,055
inner 4-byte elements** for the DLC population. The computed walk reads
**23,049**. The old figure was inflated by starts that began inside the
MIDDLE's own bytes and read array counts out of material data. Every
`+0xfc` inner-element count in §9.59 is superseded; the whole-population
figure is now **301,152 outer entries (= 100,384 × 3) and 861,558 inner
4-byte elements**.

This is HANDOFF §3's "ask what else would produce this same number",
arriving a section late. The searched model's headline was a real
measurement of a real property (the walk consumed exactly to EOF); it
simply was not a measurement of the property it was read as.

#### Two ambiguities in the spec's prose that had to be settled by measurement

Both are in §4.4.6(f), both are load-bearing, and both are now permanent
scoreable controls rather than assumptions:

1. **Which bit of the flags byte gates the collision hull.** §4.4.6(f)
   says the branch is taken when `+0x78 == -1` **and** "header byte
   `+0x08` bit `2` is set". §4.2 writes a *different* gate on the same
   byte as the literal mask `byte(+8) & 2`, so "bit 2" is genuinely
   ambiguous between mask `0x02` and bit *index* 2 (mask `0x04`).
   Measured, on the DLC population: **mask `0x04` → 4,232/4,232; mask
   `0x02` → 3,436/4,232**. `kHullGateMask = 0x04`, and the losing reading
   is scored as a permanent control.
2. **Whether the do-nothing third outcome still aligns.** §4.4.2(a) as
   amended says `FUN_00749ba0` "aligns first, then does its gated work",
   which would imply a 16-align even when the flags bit is clear.
   Measured: asserting that alignment **costs 24 of 4,232 DLC entries**
   their exact landing, and **214 of 100,384** population-wide. The reader
   performs no alignment on that path, and `gatedPairNoneBranchAligns`
   scores the alternative.

**Both figures come from the shipping reader, not only from the
prototype, and the binary that produced every number in this section is
the one built from the source as committed.** The two controls above were
added after the first full population sweep, so all five archives were
re-run with the final binary to prove the additions changed nothing:
`sr3_city_0` and `sr3_city_1`'s re-run output is **byte-identical to the
first sweep apart from the two new control rows** (41,555/41,555 and
54,597/54,597 again), and the DLC output likewise. That is the check that
makes it safe to quote a control added after the fact.

Neither was invented and neither came from the binary — both are choices
between two readings of Team A's published prose, decided by which one
reproduces the shipped bytes, with the loser's score recorded rather than
discarded.

#### Independent instruments, and what they agree on

* **The formula was prototyped separately before any C++ was written**, in
  Python, directly from §4.4.6(b)'s pseudocode. It and the shipping C++
  reader agree on the DLC population exactly (4,232/4,232) and on every
  internal boundary of the hand-checked files.
* **All SIX of §4.4.6(e)'s hand-derived byte boundaries reproduce exactly**,
  read back out of the shipping reader (not the prototype):
  `column_genki_b` MIDDLE `0x1a0`–`0x714`, ends `0x75c`; `vent_metala`
  HEAD `0x1c0`–`0x2cc`, MIDDLE record at `0x2d0`, MIDDLE ends `0x964`,
  file ends `0x9e4`; `gis_machine_c` MIDDLE `0x400`–`0x1fd4`, ends
  `0x2208`; `banner_b` MIDDLE `0x190`–`0x704`, ends `0x784`;
  `diner_wall_2_a01` HEAD `0x220`–`0x434`, MIDDLE `0x440`–`0xdb4`, ends
  `0xe80`; `fountain_a_large_01` MIDDLE `0x210`–`0xae4`, ends `0xcc0`.
* **The `+0xb8` record census reproduces §4.4.6(d) digit for digit**:
  `+0x00` zero and never `-1` in 100,384/100,384; `+0x18` zero and never
  `-1`, so **every shipped file has exactly two render-mesh groups**
  (100,384/100,384); `+0x24` and `+0x34` non-zero in 100,384/100,384 and
  equal to each other in **12,960**; `+0x48` zero in **93,469**; `+0x20`
  is 1 ×**97,802** / 2 ×**2,582**; `+0x30` is 1 ×**97,924** / 2 ×**2,460**.
  Material record count: 2 ×**53,674**, 3 ×**19,535**, 4 ×**10,074**,
  5 ×**2,760**, 6 ×**2,049**, 7 ×**1,531**, 8 ×**762** — every one an
  exact match, and never 0 and never 1, as §4.4.6(d) states.
* **The gated pair's branch split reproduces both sides' figures**:
  sentinel 89,192, real values 11,192 (one value **10,275**, two values
  **917** — §9.59's own numbers), and the hull branch taken in
  **18,706 / 100,384**, the exact figure §4.4.6(f) publishes. Those hulls
  carry **1,357,927 vertices, 1,357,927 u16 indices and 24,406,240 bytes
  of opaque precomputed blob** across the population — real file-resident
  collision geometry that the previous "builds a default, consumes
  nothing" reading discarded entirely.
* **Everything §9.59/§9.60 measured that is not tail-layout-dependent is
  unchanged**, which is the right outcome: `count(+0x88)` populated in
  **258** files, **388** outer records, **2,368** inner 12-byte elements;
  `count(+0x98) > 0` in **7,194**; `count(+0x48) > 0` in **1,454**;
  `count(+0xa8)` populated in **0 / 100,384**; `count(+0xfc) == 3` in
  100,384/100,384; `slot(+0xb8)` zero on disk in 100,384/100,384;
  `count(+0x48) == count(+0x58) == count(+0x70)` in 100,384/100,384.

**One figure does NOT match, and it is a definitional difference, not a
disagreement.** §4.4.6(d) gives the two most common exact MIDDLE lengths
as `1,204` ×21,341 and `1,396` ×13,070; this reader counts ×**21,345**
and ×**13,093**. Min (**1,172**) and max (**49,868**) match exactly. The
cause was checked rather than assumed: measuring the MIDDLE from
`headEnd` instead of from its own 16-aligned start moves files between
buckets, and only for the 1,454 entries whose `headEnd` is not already
16-aligned — demonstrated directly on the DLC slice, where the two
definitions give 1,426 vs 1,423 for length 1,204 and 238 vs 237 for
1,396. The remaining difference is the same effect on the two city
archives. **Not re-run to reconcile the exact city split**; stated as the
mechanism, not as a proven reconciliation.

They land. The aggregate is the primary evidence — **129 → 0 across the
population** — and a named sample makes it checkable rather than purely

stems (16 in `sr3_city_0` across 5 stems, 71 in `sr3_city_1` across 6)
all land exactly**. Note the honest limit of that check: those stems name
more entries than the 129, since the same asset repeats across tiles and

129-entry list did not survive §9.59 in enumerable form, so what is
verified is *(a)* the population-wide failure count is now zero and
*(b)* every entry carrying a named stem from that set lands.

#### Synthetic suite: 26 → 39 tests, all green

`tests/synthetic_clmesh_test.cpp`'s fixture builder no longer emits an
opaque MIDDLE filler — it **builds a real one from the layout rules**
(the `0x50` record, a material-set block with a name table and
size-declaring records, the lookup array, two render groups each with a
`0x60` header, index list, a real version-9 Mesh sub-block carrying its
c-side check-value bookend, and the u16/u8 arrays), plus the HEAD's Mesh
sub-blocks and index-list blocks and all three gated-pair branches. New
mutation cases, one per newly load-bearing rule: the HEAD without array
2's index-list payloads, a 16-align between consecutive Mesh sub-blocks,
the name table without its leading NUL, one render group instead of two,
no lookup array, the list block costed at zero, and the hull gate bit
cleared.

One of them earned its keep immediately: the name-table mutation
**passed for the wrong reason** at first, because a one-byte shift is
absorbed by the very next align-to-8 unless the table happens to end on
an 8-boundary — which is also precisely why the same control only scores
29% on real data. The fixture's material names were changed to make the
term observable at all, and the reason is written at the option that
controls it. A mutation test that cannot fail is not a test, and this one
could not have, as originally written.

#### What this did NOT settle

* **The MIDDLE's contents are located, not decoded.** Offsets, counts and
  byte ranges only. What a material record, a `0x20`-byte group-1
  sub-record or a `0x34`-byte trailer record *contains* is untouched, and
  §4.4.6(d)'s `+0x24`/`+0x34` stale-authoring-tool fields are read by
  nothing here either.
* **The collision hull's opaque blob is not decoded** — §4.4.6(f) does not
  say what it is. 24.4 MB of it ships. The vertex and index lists are
  decoded only because §4.4.6(f) states their element sizes outright.
* **§4.4.6(f)'s Havok question stays unjoined.** Team A reached
  `FUN_00d56010` with a (vertices, count, …, count, indices) argument
  shape and no `hk`-prefixed symbol. Nothing here advances it, and nothing
  here should be cited as if it did.
* **113 of 2,899 `+0x48` references still do not parse through
  `MeshBlock`** — unchanged by this work, pre-existing, OPEN.
* **The exact 129-entry list from §9.59** is not recoverable in
  enumerable form; see the honest limit stated above.
* **`count(+0xfc) == 3` and `count(+0xa8) == 0`** remain unexamined
  constants, exercised at exactly one value each by everything that ships.

### 9.65 `.clmesh_pc` MIDDLE record CONTENTS decoded, not just located — materials, group-1/group-2 feature indices, trailer material-slot + LOD-active flag (2026-09-14), from Team A's `spec-physics-format.md` §4.4.6(h)

With §9.64's walk closed and independently re-verified end to end, the
user chose to keep working the reading lane rather than start a new
collision-simulation feature (see the RESUME note's top for that
decision). Two concrete disassembly-shaped leads were handed to Team A —
§4.4.6(f)'s unjoined Havok question, and the MIDDLE's record CONTENTS
(located since §9.64 but never decoded). **Team A closed both the same
day.** §4.4.6(g): `FUN_00d56010` followed in full — a content-confirmed
Havok MOPP-tree handoff (a literal on-disk `"MOPP"` magic, `0x50504f4d`,
plus a composite constructor shaped exactly like Havok's public
`hkpMoppBvTreeShape(shape, moppCode)`), reported at HIGH CONFIDENCE, not
CONFIRMED, because an exhaustive check of all 1,010 functions in the
traced address range found zero `hk`-prefixed symbols — this project's
own bar for CONFIRMED. Nothing in this reader changes from (g); it is a
disassembly-only finding about what consumes the hull data, not a new
on-disk field. **§4.4.6(h)** is the one this section implements: real
runtime consumers (not the three walkers) read three offsets across the
material record, the group-1 `0x20`-byte sub-record, and the `+0x48`
trailer, and this reader now decodes exactly those three — verified by
reading `spec-physics-format.md` §4.4.6(h) directly (lines 340-410),
not from the relay alone, per this project's own standing discipline.

**What's now decoded, each CONFIRMED — disassembly, in the spec:**

| Record | Field | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Material record | `+0x00`/`+0x04` (u32) | Material/shader hash; a second per-variant hash. Population meaning OPEN for both — mechanism/presence CONFIRMED, transfers directly from `spec-foliage-format.md` §6 (same parser, `FUN_00e71090`) |
| Material record | `+0x08` (u8) | Flags byte; bit `0x08` CONFIRMED as a fallback-texture-path selector, rest OPEN |
| Material record | `+0x0C`/`+0x0E`/`+0x0F` | `u16` texture-binding count / `u8` constant-name count / `u8` vec4-constant count — CONFIRMED, read unconditionally by `FUN_00e71090` |
| Group-1 `0x20`-byte sub-record | `+0x18` (u16) | An index into the group's OWN resolved-mesh reference (not inline `.clmesh_pc` bytes) — read only outside the three walkers, in the real runtime constructor `glmesh_ctor_FUN_0074c530` |
| Group-2 `4`-byte inner element | `+0x02` (u16) | Same index namespace as the group-1 field above — cross-referenced by the same consumer (a vertex-welding/degenerate-feature-removal pass) |
| Trailer `0x34`-byte record | `+0x2C` (u32) | A **raw, pre-remap** material-slot index. The runtime remaps it through a temporary per-parse table (`materialHandleTable`, built via a stack `alloca` inside `FUN_00e3e590` itself) that has no on-disk form — this reader decodes the raw index only, not the remapped handle |
| Trailer `0x34`-byte record | `+0x30` bit `0x04` | An "active at this LOD tier" flag — CONFIRMED via a real introsort (`FUN_0074c2b0`) + comparator (`FUN_00748d50`) that partitions the trailer array on exactly this bit before truncating it |

Everything else in these three record types stays genuinely OPEN — §4.4.6(h)
says so explicitly per field, and this reader decodes nothing beyond the
table above. The material record's own leading `u32` is a **length
prefix for the whole record** (size field included), not a data field —
`materialSetStep()` already relied on this to skip records; the decoded
`0x30`-byte header starts 8-aligned *after* that 4-byte prefix, a real
subtlety worth flagging since it is easy to misread the header as
starting at the record's own `materialRecordOffsets[i]`.

**Cross-team loop closed the same day.** Flagged to Team A that
§4.4.6(h)'s original table gave offsets with no stated origin, reading as
if `+0x00` meant the record's raw start. Team A traced it precisely
rather than just accepting the flag: the underlying mechanism was never
wrong — `spec-foliage-format.md` §6's own prose already said "length-
prefixed: `u32 size`, then 8-align, a `0x30` header" — the physics
write-up's table just dropped that anchoring sentence when the table was
transferred over. Fixed at the source: the table header now reads
"relative to the aligned `0x30` header, i.e. `align8(record_start + 4)` —
NOT `record_start` itself" (verified directly against the synced
`spec-physics-format.md`, line 340, not taken from the relay alone).
Confirms this reader's `roundUp8(recOffset + kMatRecordSizePrefix)` was
already correct from the start; nothing here needed to change.
**What changed in the reader.** `include/sr3clmesh/level_mesh.h` gained
`MaterialRecord`/`TrailerRecord` structs and the field-offset constants
(`kMatRecordHash0` etc., `kGroupASubFeatureIndex`/`kGroupBInnerFeatureIndex`,
`kTrailerMaterialSlotRaw`/`kTrailerLodByte`/`kTrailerLodActiveMask`);
`MiddleLayout` gained `groupADetail`/`groupBDetail`
(`std::vector<NestedEntry>`, one entry per outer `0x10`-byte record, same
shape `group88()`/`groupFc()` already use) since the existing walk only
ever advanced a shared cursor past each outer entry's sub-list without
remembering where it started — needed to decode `+0x18`/`+0x02` per
sub-record at all. `LevelMesh` gained four accessors:
`materialRecords()`, `trailerRecords()`, `groupAFeatureIndices(entry,
content)`, `groupBFeatureIndices(entry, content)` — the latter two throw
`FormatError` if handed the wrong detail vector's entry (checked against

restructured) to populate the two new detail vectors inline in its
existing group-A/group-B loops; nothing about what bytes are consumed or

### 9.66 The 113/2,899 non-parsing `+0x48` `MeshBlock` references — characterized, not fixed: three clean failure classes, 16 named assets, 40 placements, no invented resolution

Pre-existing OPEN item (§9.64's "what this did NOT settle", §4.4.6(h)'s
own list) with no known cause until now: of 2,899 `MeshBlock` references
the `+0x48`-gated reference chain resolves across all 5 archives, 113 do
not parse. Its own resolver (`LevelMesh::resolveReferencedMeshes()`)
silently `break`s on the first exception in a file's chain, so the true
shape was hidden — a single early failure in a long chain drops every
remaining reference in that file too, not just the one that failed. A
purpose-built diagnostic (session scratchpad, not shipped —
`diag_meshblock_refs.cpp`) re-ran the identical chain but reported the
file, chain index, byte offset and the `FormatError`'s own message
instead of swallowing it, across the full independently-rebuilt
population (100,384/100,384 files, 1,454 with `count(+0x48) > 0`, 2,899
references — all matching §9.64's own figures exactly, confirming this
diagnostic walks the identical chain the shipped reader does).

**Result: all 113 land in exactly 40 file-instances of 16 NAMED assets**
(the same stem repeats across tile placements, as §9.59 already noted for
a different set of names) **splitting into three distinct, bounded
failure classes — no invented resolution for any of them:**

```
CLASS 1 - no paired .glmesh_pc, but the FIRST reference in the chain
          declares its bulk data lives there anyway (g-file 0 bytes):
  ceilingventa~l1 (10 placements) vent_metala~l1 (10) diner_wall_1_a01~l1 (1)
  diner_wall_2_a01~l1 (1, count=2) dnr_counter_curve_a01~l1 (1)
  mat_smiling_jacks_a01~l1 (1) sauce_pan_c01~l1/d01~l1/e01~l1 (1 each)
  stool_diner_a01~l1 (1)
  -> 28 placements, 29 unresolved refs, ALL fail at chain index 0

CLASS 2 - a 14-reference chain's SECOND entry (index 1) lands on
          all-zero bytes where a real check value was expected:
  bank_floor4_destroy / ~l1 / ~l2 (2 placements each = 6 total)
  -> 6 placements, 78 unresolved refs (index-0 entry resolves fine in
     every case; everything from index 1 onward in that 14-long chain is
     then dropped by the chain-break, which is most of the 78)

CLASS 3 - a 2-reference chain's SECOND entry (index 1) declares a
          c-side length that overruns the remaining c-file bytes:
  hotel_complex / ~l1 / ~l2 (4+1+1 = 6 placements)
  -> 6 placements, 6 unresolved refs (index-0 entry resolves fine every
     time; only the one index-1 entry is lost per file)
```

28 + 6 + 6 = 40 placements; 29 + 78 + 6 = 113 unresolved refs — both
totals match exactly.

**Reading the classes, without inventing an explanation for any of
them.** Class 1's stems are ALL `~l1`-suffixed except `stool_diner_a01~l1`
which also is - i.e. every Class 1 stem carries that suffix, and every
failure is the chain's very FIRST reference, meaning the file has no
g-side data at all for even its first Mesh sub-block. Classes 2 and 3
share a different shape: the FIRST reference in a multi-reference chain
always resolves; only from the SECOND onward does it break, which is
consistent with (but does not prove) the additive `cursor +=
block.cLength()` / `gCursor += block.gLength()` step being wrong for
these specific multi-part "destroy"/"complex" variant meshes - a
14-reference and a 2-reference chain are both long enough to have a
"step 2" for that to go wrong on, while every Class 1 stem's chain is
length 1 (except `diner_wall_2_a01~l1` at length 2, which fails at index
0 regardless, so the multi-reference theory doesn't explain it) or
already broken before a second step would ever matter. Nothing here
picks between "these assets are just built differently" and "the
resolver's stepping formula has an uncaught edge case" - that would be
guessing, and this project's own standing policy (§9.61) is to stop and
state the bound rather than fabricate the answer.

**A real, small, unrelated bug found and fixed along the way**:
`src/mesh_block.cpp`'s `FormatError` for a check-value mismatch
(`"segment does not open with the block's check value: found 0x" +
std::to_string(...)`) used `std::to_string` - which prints DECIMAL - but
labelled the output `"0x"` as if it were hex. This is why this section's
own diagnostic initially printed `"expected 0x663536740"`, which is not
a valid 32-bit hex value at all (9 hex digits); it was decimal
663,536,740 mislabeled. Fixed with a proper `std::ostringstream <<
std::hex` (the same idiom already used in `src/save_snapshot.cpp`) for
both the `found` and `expected` values. **Purely a diagnostic-message
formatting bug, zero behavioral change** - verified: `mesh_block.cpp`
rebuilt alone at `/W4` (zero warnings), no test in the suite asserts the
old (wrong) message text (checked directly, no matches), and
`sr3mesh_tests` (`synthetic_ccmesh_vertex_test.cpp`) re-run green
afterward on the rebuilt object. `build_verify/mesh_block.obj` itself was
NOT touched by this fix (built and verified in an isolated scratchpad
directory instead, per this session's own established discipline for
avoiding the shared-pool staleness hazard) - whoever next does a full
`cl /c src\*.cpp` pass will pick it up.

**This is a genuine, well-anchored candidate for a Team A disassembly
cross-check**, if they want one: does the `+0x48` chain's c-side/g-side
cursor step between CONSECUTIVE Mesh sub-block references ever differ
from the block's own `cLength()`/`gLength()` - anchored on 6 named files
(`hotel_complex`/`bank_floor4_destroy` families) where the SECOND
reference fails exactly where that naive additive formula would place
it, and Class 1's `~l1` stems as a separate, second question (do these
specific variant meshes genuinely carry no g-side data by design, or is
this reader's `bulkInGFile()` read wrong for them specifically). Not
forced on anyone - stated here so it isn't lost, per this session's own
"document and move on" pattern for every other genuine dead end today.

**Addendum (same day): Team A independently attempted the same 113/2,899
measurement and, before this was reconciled, reported a very different
count (~1,417, concentrated on different named files) from a Python
harness (`mesh_scan.py`). Cross-team reconciliation is IN PROGRESS, not
settled — do not cite either number as final without checking for a
follow-up dated after this entry.** Team A traced their own gap to a
16-byte-alignment restriction in their g-offset search that this
reader's computed (not searched) walk never had, fixed it, and reported
`bank_floor4_destroy`/`hotel_complex` now fully resolving byte-for-byte.
Before accepting that, this session independently dumped the RAW bytes
at the exact failure positions (not relying on either side's summary) and
found something that doesn't obviously fit that explanation: at
`hotel_complex`'s reference-1 position (cursor `1692` in
`sr3_city_1.vpp_pc`, landing there via the ordinary `cursor +=
block[0].cLength()` step and reading a fully plausible header there -
version 9, a real-looking check value, sane `cLength`/`gLength` - not
garbage), **the on-disk flags byte genuinely reads `0x00` (not
bulk-in-g) with `channelCount == 0`** - the exact same pattern at
`bank_floor4_destroy`'s and `hotel_complex~l2`'s own reference-1
positions too (three different assets, both city archives, always at
chain index ≥1, never at index 0). With `bulkInGFile()==false`, the
shipped `sr3mesh::MeshBlock::parse()` (not diagnostic-only code) looks
for the declared `gLength` (26,784 in this case) as INLINE bulk data
immediately after a zero-channel header, inside a c-file that is only
14,528 bytes total - which is the real, verified mechanism behind both
observed failure shapes. This does not obviously match "g-offset search
was over-restricted to 16-aligned positions", since the file itself says
(via a flags byte that reads correctly against every other field in the
same header) that this record isn't g-backed at all. Flagged back to
Team A with the exact hex bytes, asking specifically what their
now-passing harness reads for the bulk-in-g flag at whatever position it
lands on for this same block.

**RESOLVED, same day: real bug, found, fixed, and verified end to end -
113 → 29 unresolved, matching the predicted 84-reference delta exactly.**
Team A went back to their own raw bytes at the identical cursor (1692,
same checkValue/`cLength`/`gLength` as this session measured, confirmed
byte-for-byte identical) and found the missing piece: the pre-header
quad (`version`, pad, `checkValue`, `cLength`, `gLength`) ends at
block-relative `+0x10`, but `+0x10` (absolute 1708) is not itself a
multiple of 8 for this block - their shared Mesh-sub-block reader applies
one more conditional `align8` there before the header proper (flags,
channelCount, ...) begins, landing it 4 bytes later at `+0x14`
(1712). The 4 bytes at `+0x10`-`+0x13` genuinely ARE zero in the file (not
a misread) - they are alignment padding, not the flags byte; the real
flags byte one align-step later reads `0x01` (bulk-in-g), not `0x00`.

**This reader already had this exact rule, just not wired to this
caller.** `src/zone_geometry.cpp`'s `headerDisplacementFor(anchor)` -
`alignUp(anchor + 16, 8) - anchor` - was written and MEASURED for
`.gzn_pc`'s own additive, non-8-guaranteed Mesh-sub-block chain
(HANDOFF Sec9.55.2: 2,596 anchors closing at `+0x10`, 247 at `+0x14`,
zero ambiguous) and is used by `.gzn_pc`'s own `ZoneGeometry::locate()`.
`src/level_mesh.cpp`'s `resolveReferencedMeshes()` - the `+0x48`
reference chain, the SAME shape (additive `cursor += cLength()`, no
external alignment guarantee for index ≥ 1) - was simply never wired to
the same rule, instead calling `sr3mesh::MeshBlock::parse()` with its
unconditional `+0x10` default (`kHeaderStart`, correct only for the
`cursor % 8 == 0` case, which is all every OTHER caller in the project
ever needed since their own upstream alignment steps guarantee it).
**Fixed** by computing `headerDisplacement = roundUp8(cursor + 16) -
cursor` per reference and passing it through, reusing the exact
already-established formula rather than inventing a new one.

**Verification, in order:**
1. `src/level_mesh.cpp` rebuilt alone at `/W4` - zero warnings.
2. `tests/synthetic_clmesh_test.cpp` gained
   `testResolvedReferenceChainSurvivesNonEightAlignedSecondBlock` - two
   real back-to-back HEAD meshes, sized so the second genuinely lands on
   `cursor % 8 == 4` (asserted directly, not assumed). Required a
   companion fix to the fixture builder itself: `appendMeshSubBlock`'s
   `headerAt` was hardcoded `0x10` "by construction" (true only for a
   single mesh) and its g-segment start was 16-aligned, which desyncs
   from the resolver's own purely-additive g-cursor for a second segment
   - both corrected to mirror production exactly. **Confirmed as a real,
   non-vacuous mutation test**: reverted the production fix, rebuilt
   `level_mesh.obj` alone, reran - the new test FAILED
   (`meshes.size() == 2` false) exactly as expected; restored the fix,
   rebuilt again, full 42/42 green. (A first attempt at this check gave a
   false "still passes" reading from a stale `level_mesh.obj` that hadn't
   been recompiled after the revert - caught immediately by rebuilding
   before trusting it, the same stale-object hazard this project has
   named repeatedly, §9.62/§9.63.4/§9.63.9/§9.64.)
3. **Real-data, full population, independently rebuilt**: reran this
   session's own `diag_meshblock_refs` diagnostic (rebuilt against the
   fixed `level_mesh.obj`) against all five archives. `bank_floor4_destroy`
   and `hotel_complex` (all name variants, Classes 2 and 3, 84 references)
   are GONE from the failure list entirely - exactly the predicted delta.
   **TOTAL: 113 → 29 unresolved`, `filesImperfect: 40 → 28`.** The
   remaining 29 are EXACTLY Class 1 unchanged (the `~l1`-suffixed stems
   with no paired `.glmesh_pc` at chain index 0 - `ceilingventa~l1`,
   `vent_metala~l1`, `diner_wall_1/2_a01~l1`, `dnr_counter_curve_a01~l1`,
   `mat_smiling_jacks_a01~l1`, `sauce_pan_c/d/e01~l1`, `stool_diner_a01~l1`)
   - a genuinely separate question this fix does not touch.

**Class 1 itself is further narrowed by Team A, not yet independently
re-verified by this session**: of the 29, they report 20 are real
cross-bundle deduplication (11 byte-identical placements sharing one
g-file across DIFFERENT `.str2_pc` bundles, confirmed directly on their
side) rather than genuinely missing data - this reader's own pairing is
deliberately same-bundle-only (matching `validate_clmesh.cpp`'s own
established, conservative rule), so it correctly reports "no g-file
in THIS bundle" without claiming there is no g-file anywhere in the
archive. The remaining, genuinely unexplained gap per their count: **8
files, 9 references, all one `smiling_jacks` diner-prop family, no
matching g-file anywhere in the archive.** Not independently confirmed
by this session as of this entry - the 113→29 result above is; the
20-vs-9 split within Class 1 is Team A's own finding, cited, not
re-derived here.

**What this whole thread demonstrates, worth keeping as its own
lesson**: neither team's first independent measurement was right (this
session's 113 undercounted by missing a real bug; Team A's ~1,417
overcounted from a genuine search-methodology gap), and the eventual

### 9.67 First tree reader — `sr3tree`, `.csrt_pc`/`.gsrt_pc` (2026-09-14), built entirely from blocks this project already knew

With every item from today's clmesh arc genuinely closed (§9.64-§9.66)
and no further ungated work sitting in the "needs a DECISION" table or
requiring Team A's disassembly, an Explore-agent survey of HANDOFF's own
open-item list turned up `spec-tree-format.md` — a Team A spec, fully
`[CONFIRMED — disassembly + empirical]` per its own §1, for a format
(`.csrt_pc`/`.gsrt_pc`, type 36, `Tree`) this project had never built a
reader for. Read in full before writing any code, per the hard rule. The
spec's own headline: **"Trees are an assembly of blocks this project
already knows, plus one new fixed header."** True on inspection — the
shared material-reference block (`sr3geometry::MaterialBlock`), the same
inline-material-definition routine `spec-foliage-format.md` §6 uses
(`FUN_00e71090`), and the shared "Mesh" sub-block (`sr3mesh::MeshBlock`)
account for most of the file; only the fixed `0x208`-byte `'TREE'` block,
the `0x170`-byte geometry sub-structure, and the `0x60`-byte collision
capsules are new.

**New library, `sr3tree`**: `include/sr3tree/errors.h`, `include/sr3tree/tree.h`,
`src/tree.cpp` — one `Tree::parse(content, gContent)` walking, in spec §3's
own order: material-reference block → mandatory strictly-greater 16-byte
pad (`spec-geometry-format.md` §3.1.1, the same rule `sr3foliage` already
uses) → `'TREE'` block (magic `0x54524545`, version `> 0xCB`) → geometry
sub-structure → material-set block (own name table, `count × 8` pointer
slots, then length-prefixed inline material records — independently
re-implemented rather than cross-depending on `sr3foliage`'s copy, per
this project's own convention) → the generic index list (`FUN_00e401d0`,
resolved here to `u32` elements per spec §7) → 4 LOD presence entries,
each gating a g-backed `sr3mesh::MeshBlock` → three opaque runtime arrays
(located, not decoded — spec §3's own table marks them so) → collision
capsules. The walk must land EXACTLY on end-of-file, the same oracle
every other reader in this project uses (spec §3: replay-verified 11/11).

**A lesson from today's own §9.66 applied PRE-EMPTIVELY, not found the
hard way a second time**: spec §3 states the Mesh sub-blocks are "each
advanced by its own length field" — the identical shape as `.clmesh_pc`'s
`+0x48` reference chain that turned out to have a missing conditional
align8. `src/tree.cpp` computes `headerDisplacement = roundUp8(cursor +
16) - cursor` per LOD slot from the very first version, exactly like
`src/zone_geometry.cpp`'s already-established `headerDisplacementFor()` —
not the unconditional `+0x10` default that had to be fixed in clmesh
after the bug already shipped. Verified this matters, not just guarded
against a theoretical risk: `tests/synthetic_tree_test.cpp`'s
multi-LOD-slot test asserts a later slot's own Mesh header lands on a
non-8-aligned cursor (it does, by construction — a single-channel Mesh
sub-block's own `cLength` is not a multiple of 8), and temporarily hard-
coding the displacement back to `0x10` crashes the test outright rather
than just failing a check — confirming the fix is load-bearing here too,
not defensive dead code.

**Synthetic tests**: `tests/synthetic_tree_test.cpp`, 6 tests — a
well-formed single-LOD-slot tree (material fields, texture-binding name
resolution, capsule fields all asserted against known values), a
zero-material/zero-LOD/zero-capsule edge case that must parse cleanly,
the multi-LOD-slot misalignment case above, and four mutation cases (bad
`'TREE'` magic, version not `> 0xCB`, wrong LOD slot count, a
material-count mismatch between the geometry sub-structure and the
material-set block) plus a truncation case — all must throw. All 6 green;
`tree.cpp` and the tests both rebuild clean at `/W4`, zero warnings.

**Real-data validation, `tools/validation/validate_tree.cpp`, all three
archives the spec names (`sr3_city_0`, `dlc2`, `dlc3`) — matches every
population statistic spec §1/§2 states, exactly:**

```

distinct stems            : 11        (spec: 11 distinct trees)
parsed OK                 : 28 / 28   (spec: replay lands 11/11 - here, every shipped copy)

Zero failures, zero mismatches, first attempt — no iteration needed

**Wired into the build**: `CMakeLists.txt` gained the `sr3tree` static

`sr3clmesh_tests` (42/42), `sr3mesh_tests`, and `sr3bonepalette_tests`

**What this reader deliberately does NOT decode** (spec §12's own open-item

### 9.68 `reynolds` — the last 1/46 multi-set mesh — closed by vertex duplication, a renderer engineering choice, not a decode (2026-09-14)

§9.63.10's own last open item: `reynolds` was the one shipped multi-set
character mesh (of 46) that still refused to render, because two draw
ranges in the group actually drawn disagree about which bone-palette SET
the SAME vertex index should skin through, and one CPU vertex array can
only carry one set's remap per index. §9.63.10 itself named the fix
approach when it shipped the refusal — "duplicate the conflicting
vertices... a renderer engineering choice and not a decode" — and left it
undone. This section does it.

**Exact conflict, diagnosed before writing any fix code.**
`reynolds.ccmesh_pc`/`.gcmesh_pc`/`.rig_pc` live in `characters.vpp_pc` →
`saints_male_reynolds.str2_pc`. One channel (layout 3, 5405 vertices), 2
bone-palette sets (`{start=0,count=60}`, `{start=60,count=16}`), 8 draw
groups, group 0 has 6 ranges. Group 0's ranges and their
`drawRangePaletteSets()` value: ranges 0/1/2 set 0 (indices 0-3388, then
3389-6197), ranges 3/4 set 1 (6198-8339), range 5 set 0 again — but only
19 indices (8340-8358), a tiny accessory-sized strip. **The conflict is
exactly**: vertex indices **4494, 4496, 4498** are first claimed by range
4 (set 1), then range 5's own tiny strip reuses them wanting set 0 — 3
distinct indices, 6 total vertex-uses (vertex 4496 alone is referenced 4
times within range 5). A purpose-built diagnostic
(`diag_reynolds_conflicts.cpp`, session scratchpad) established this by
reimplementing `assignPaletteSetsPerVertex()`'s own first-claim-wins walk
with full per-conflict logging, rather than working from the aggregate
"6 vertex-uses" count alone.

**Design: vertex DUPLICATION with per-range index redirection**, not a
global vertex remap — the same original index could in principle need
different replacements in different ranges (not needed for `reynolds`
itself, six of one, but the general mechanism supports it without extra
cost). Dedup rule: one duplicate per `(originalVertexIndex, wantedSet)`
pair, reused for every subsequent reference needing that exact pairing —
so vertex 4496's 4 references in range 5 create ONE duplicate, not four.

**What was built, three layers:**

1. **`include/sr3rig/bone_palette.h` / `src/bone_palette.cpp`** — new
   `VertexDuplicationResult` struct and
   `resolveVertexSetConflictsByDuplication(mesh, vertexCount, groupIndex)`.
   Refuses for exactly the same structural reasons
   `assignPaletteSetsPerVertex()` already refuses on (no sets, draw groups
   not located, selector array unreadable, an out-of-range set index) — it
   does not loosen that contract, it only replaces "refuse on a real
   conflict" with "resolve it." On success: `setOfVertex` (original count,
   first-claim-wins, identical in construction to
   `PaletteSetAssignment::setOfVertex`), `duplicateSourceIndex` /
   `duplicateSetOfVertex` (one entry per NEW duplicate created), and
   `redirectPerRange` (a `std::vector<std::map<uint32_t,uint32_t>>`, one
   map per range in `mesh.drawGroups()[groupIndex]`, mapping an original
   vertex index to its duplicate's GPU slot for THAT range's own index
   references only).
2. **`include/sr3render/mesh_renderer.h` / `src/mesh_renderer.cpp`** —
   `MeshRenderer::upload()` previously decoded vertices AND built the
   index buffer entirely internally from `mesh`, with no way for a caller
   to inject extra vertices or redirect specific index references. New
   `sr3render::VertexDuplication` struct (`sourceIndex`,
   `redirectPerRange` — same shape as the `sr3rig` result, a deliberate
   mirroring) and a new optional trailing `const VertexDuplication*
   duplication = nullptr` parameter. `nullptr` (every pre-existing call
   site) is the exact old code path — verified, not assumed, see below.
   Implementation: total GPU vertex count becomes `vertices.size() +
   sourceIndex.size()`; `overridePositions`' size check now accepts this
   extended count; the GPU-vertex build loop sources normal/UV for an
   extra slot from `vertices[sourceIndex[vi - vertices.size()]]`
   (position still from `overridePositions[vi]`, since a duplicate's
   skinned position genuinely differs from its source's); the per-range
   index-build loop (rewritten with an explicit range index `r` so
   `redirectPerRange[r]` can be looked up) redirects specific emitted
   indices before appending them.
3. **`tools/sr3_viewer.cpp`** — a new shared helper `applyMultiSetSkinning()`
   (used by both `runPose()` and `runAnimPose()`, which previously had
   near-duplicated `kPaletteMultiSet` blocks) wraps
   `resolveVertexSetConflictsByDuplication()` + appending the duplicate
   `sr3mesh::Vertex` copies to `verts` + `remapBlendIndicesThroughPaletteSets()`
   over the EXTENDED array — so each duplicate's own blend indices resolve
   against ITS OWN correct set, not copied post-remap from the original.
   Both call sites build a `sr3render::VertexDuplication` (empty unless
   `duplicatesCreated != 0`) and thread it through every
   `renderer.upload()` call in that function (`runPose`: 2 call sites;
   `runAnimPose`: 2, one inside the per-frame animation-sampling loop).

### 9.69 `MaterialBindings::parse` rewritten to locate records by direct arithmetic — closes the vehicle material↔run association gap (2026-09-18)

**Origin: a Team A cross-reference, not a fresh dispatch.** Six candidate
associations between a vehicle draw range's material id and its texture-
binding run had all been refuted (`spec-vehicle-geometry.md` §7.1 item 1,
all at or below chance). Separately, an unconnected 2026-09-12 pass
(§11.2) had already fully disassembled and validated the shared per-
material record parser (`FUN_00e71090` — the same inline material-
definition helper this project already knew from trees/foliage) for an
unrelated reason, and found the record's own **array A** — a 12-byte
`{blob offset, sampler hash, slot index}` triple — sitting at a **fixed
offset** inside each material's own record. §11.2 itself stopped one step
short, reading its own "no identity field in the record" finding as a dead
end without noticing array A does not need one: it belongs to material `i`
by direct construction, the same way the per-material loop's own iteration
already establishes identity positionally. Team A closed the loop 2026-09-
18, re-ran the existing exact parser across all 393 `.ccar_pc` files (0
excluded on its own hard exact-consumption gate, 16,781 binding-run entries
recovered), chased down a sanity-check mismatch against an older scanner
rather than leaving it unexplained (fully accounted for by the older
scanner's own length ≥ 2 filter silently dropping legitimate single-texture
materials), and relayed the finding via `purrsian-3d` with a pointer to the
already-updated `spec-vehicle-geometry.md` §7.1/§11.2. Independently
re-read both sections in full here before writing any code (relayed
technical claims get verified, never adopted on trust —
`peer-relay-authorization.md`); confirmed the file had genuinely grown
(63,316 → 121,593 bytes) and the write-up matched what was relayed exactly.

**A second, independent copy of the same finding already existed in this
project's own spec set.** `spec-vertex-format.md` §12.8 ("A relayed finding,
verified: §8.3's texture-binding search can be replaced by direct
arithmetic," dated 2026-09-12/13) had separately received and empirically
verified the identical formula — chaining from the Mesh sub-block's own
`c_len` through §8.4's fixed-stride descriptor arrays to each material
record's self-declared size — against **2,002/2,002 character files and
365/365 vehicle files, every material index on each, zero exceptions**.
That section explicitly flagged the improvement as "stated but not applied"
to the shipping reader, pending a session that owned `material_binding.cpp`.
This is that session.

**What changed, `src/material_binding.cpp` / `include/sr3geometry/material_binding.h`:**
`MaterialBindings::parse()` previously found a material's binding run by a
sliding 4-byte-stepped search over the tail of the file, guarded by run
length ≥ 2 and non-zero hashes, and accepted the whole result only when
`runs found == declared material count` exactly. That guard could never
hold for vehicles: they declare roughly **twice** the materials their draw
ranges reference (`spec-vertex-format.md` §8.4.3, mean slack 21.6/44,
49.9%), so the equality was structurally unsatisfiable, not merely rare —
measured at the time as **3/372** vehicles located, all the rest refused.

The rewrite walks directly to each material's own record instead of
searching for it (`spec-vertex-format.md` §12.8, §8.4; `spec-vehicle-
geometry.md` §11.2): from `meshBlockEnd` (already `mo + c_len`), skip the
fixed-stride arrays sized by `N2` (subheader `+0x0E`, vehicles' second
count — characters always carry 0) and by `materialCount` (`+0x0C`), then
walk the per-material loop whose `i`-th iteration **is** material `i`'s own
self-declaring-length record — a `u32` size field, an 8-aligned `0x30`-byte
header (texture-binding count at `+0x0C`), then that many 12-byte entries
starting at a fixed `+0x30` offset past the header. No count-matching guess
is needed because each record's position follows from the one before it.
Per-entry validation is unchanged in substance but now drops a single bad
entry rather than discarding the whole file (§8.4.2's two checks: the
sampler hash must be a real 32-bit constant, ≥256 and not `-1`; the name
offset must resolve to a NUL-terminated name landing on a boundary, not
mid-string) — safe now because the record's position is no longer
contingent on every entry agreeing. A material whose own header declares
zero bindings, or whose array is entirely rejected, correctly ends up with
an empty texture list rather than being treated as a location failure;
`located()` now means "the record chain was walked successfully," not "a
guess-and-check search happened to succeed."

**Verified, real data, full re-measurement (`tools/validation/validate_binding_roles.cpp`,
rebuilt against the new `material_binding.obj`):**

| | characters (`characters`+`dlc1-3`+`customize_item`+`items`) | vehicles (`vehicles`+`dlc1-3`) |
|---|---|---|
| files with a paired g-file | 2,002 | 393 |
| bindings located | **1,995 / 2,002** | **393 / 393** (was 3/372) |
| binding runs / texture entries | 4,448 / 15,322 | 17,026 / 36,010 |

The 7 unlocated character files are all one class, not scattered failures —
`nudelew_dist`, `oleg_privacybar` (×2 archive paths), `cf_privacy_top`,
`cm_privacy_bottom`, `cf_privacy_bottom`, `cm_privacy_top`: degenerate
"privacy bar" censor-overlay placeholders, 666–1,370 bytes total file size,
too small to contain a full `0x30`-byte per-material record after the
declared array skips — confirmed per-file with a purpose-built diagnostic
(`diag_unlocated_chars.cpp`, session scratchpad) rather than assumed from
the count alone. This is the same class of genuinely-absent binding the
reader was always designed to report as "no binding" rather than guess at,
now showing up proportionally in the larger population (549→2,002 files)
where the original reader's own comment recorded "3" at the smaller one.
Vehicle sampler hashes recovered independently match the cross-format
constants already documented in `spec-vehicle-geometry.md` §7.1
(`0x2808EB90`, `0x69B48F91`, both shared with character meshes).

**Visual regression check**: re-rendered `brad` textured
(`sr3_viewer_sec969.exe` — new binary, built with the refreshed
`material_binding.obj`, kept alongside the untouched `sr3_viewer.exe`
rather than overwritten). Identical 5-material binding (3×
`Brad_SM_Upper_D.tga`, 2× `Brad_SM_Lower_D.tga`) to what this reader always
produced for that file; the PNG shows the same correctly-textured suit,
ID badge, sunglasses, and skin tone as every prior session's checks. No
character-path regression.

**New synthetic suite**: `tests/synthetic_material_binding_test.cpp` (new
file, no prior synthetic coverage existed for this reader at all — an
honest pre-existing gap, closed here rather than carried forward). Built
directly from `spec-vertex-format.md` §8.4/§8.4.2/§12.8 and
`spec-vehicle-geometry.md` §11.2, never from the reader's own source, with
a from-scratch fixture builder (sub-header + descriptor arrays + chained
per-material records). 8 tests: the basic direct walk with a known
diffuse/normal pair; the same fixture with `N2 > 0` (the vehicle-shaped
array-skip, proven to desynchronise the whole chain if done wrong); a
material whose header declares zero bindings resolving to "no textures"
rather than a failure (§8.4.3's vehicle case); a bad-hash entry dropped
without invalidating its material's other entries or the file; a mid-string
name offset rejected by the boundary check; a truncated file reporting
`!located()` rather than throwing or reading past the end; `materialCount
== 0`; and the pre-existing wrong-magic-throws regression. All 8 pass,
`/W4` clean, first build. Wired into `CMakeLists.txt` as a new
`sr3materialbinding_tests` executable linking `sr3geometry` (kept separate
from `sr3geometry_tests`/`synthetic_ccmesh_test.cpp`, matching the existing
`sr3anim`/`sr3animpayload` precedent for a distinct concern sharing one
library) and copied to `build_verify/`.

**Scope, stated precisely**: this closes the READER gap — vehicles' real
per-material texture-binding data is now recoverable at all, at the same
reliability as characters. It does **not** newly implement vehicle
rendering: `tools/sr3_viewer.cpp`'s `mesh` command is still hard-wired to
the `.ccmesh_pc`/`MaterialBlock`/`GeometryBlock::parse()` path and does not
accept `.ccar_pc` files (that needs `sr3vehicle::Vehicle::parse()` +
`GeometryBlock::parseAt()`, already used by the validation harnesses but
never wired into the interactive viewer). The decision table's "Rendering
vehicles" row (`Geometry decodes; surfacing does not exist`) is unchanged
by this section and remains accurate. Vehicle paint itself is also
unchanged from §7.1's own `[HYPOTHESIS]`: the bound textures are still
generic/shared (`shd_damagenormal_n.tga` and siblings), with real paint
believed to come from `.cvtf_pc` at runtime.

The decision table's "Vehicle material↔run association" row is updated to
CLOSED in the same pass as this section.

**Addendum 2026-09-18, same day: the 17,026 vs 16,781 "runs" gap, reconciled
exactly, not left as "probably a convention difference."** Team A re-ran
their own harness independently rather than trusting the relayed figures,
and the two sides' TEXTURE-ENTRY counts matched exactly (36,010 both ways,
computed independently) while the "binding run" counts differed by 245
(1.45%). Confirmed by direct count
(`diag_runs_vs_entries.cpp`, session scratchpad, same population): this
project's own `validate_binding_roles.cpp` counts a "run" once per material
in `MaterialBindings::materials()` **regardless of whether it has any
textures** (245 of 17,026 located vehicle materials have `A_count == 0` -
zero array-A entries, a real and expected outcome per §8.4.3's "vehicles
declare roughly twice the materials their draw ranges reference"). Team A's
16,781 counts only materials with **at least one** binding. `17,026 - 16,781
== 245` exactly - the gap is entirely and only this definitional choice, not
a data disagreement of any kind. Neither figure is wrong; they are two
different countable quantities that happen to share the name "runs."

### 9.70 `sr3rig` attachment records were decoded wrong — a real reader bug, found by a Team A correction (2026-09-20)

**Context.** After a pause (relayed by the orchestrator; the user then said
directly in this window that work should proceed on the orchestrator's
say-so and that permission questions should be minimised — see the
`feedback-peer-go-ahead` memory), Team A had synced ~30 grown/corrected specs.
`spec-rig-format.md` §13 (2026-09-20) retracts §6's reading of the 0x40-byte
attachment record: **it is a 3×3 rotation matrix + translation, not a
quaternion at +0x20.** My `sr3rig::Rig::parse` had taken +0x20 for a
quaternion (`Attachment::quaternion`, header comment "genuine unit
quaternions") — i.e. it was reading row 2 of the matrix plus the
translation's x as a "unit quaternion", which looked right (within 10% of
unit norm) precisely because that vector is a unit row plus a small x. A
reader that stayed green on a wrong decode: the old synthetic fixture had
the same misreading built in (measurement-discipline: a fixture derived from
the reader proves only agreement).

**Fix (`include/sr3rig/rig.h`, `src/rig.cpp`).** `Attachment` is now
`rotationRows` (3×3, rows at +0x08/+0x14/+0x20, stored as-is, not transposed),
`translation` (+0x2C), `parentBoneIndex` (+0x38), `tag` (+0x3C, int32).
`field_0x2C_boneIndex()` ("detail bones begin here", HYPOTHESIS) is replaced by
`leadingGroupCount()` (K, +0x2C), `trailingGroupCount()` (T, +0x28) and
`groupPartitionHolds()` (K+T == bone count); spec §13.2 finds no runtime
reader of either field, so the bone-LOD reading is UNSUPPORTED and the
accessors report counts, not a boundary. `findBone()` is now a first-match
case-insensitive STRING compare (spec §13.1: the engine never uses the hash
table for lookup); it used to compare hashes, which could accept a colliding
name the engine would reject. Only `tools/validation/probe_bindpose_residual.cpp`
used the renamed accessor (updated). `Bone::nameHash`/`hashTableMatchesNames()`
stay (the table is still exactly the lowercased-name hash, 585/585).

**Verified.** `tests/synthetic_rig_test.cpp` rebuilt around the §13.4 layout
(every matrix entry and translation component distinct so a wrong stride or a
transposed row cannot pass by symmetry; signed tag round-trip; K/T partition
holds and does-not-hold cases; `findBone` with a deliberately corrupted hash
and with case-differing twin bones, which the old hash-based version fails).
**Mutation-checked**: pointing the matrix read at +0x20 makes the new test fail
(24+ CHECK FAILED), so it is not vacuous. Real data, all 585 rigs
(`preload_rigs` + `characters`, `validate_rig.exe`, /W4 clean): **12,480/12,480
attachments orthonormal with det +1**; the same test with the first row at
each of seven other 4-byte offsets (+0x00…+0x1C) scores **0/12,480 each**;
**tag == -1 12,480/12,480**; **header +0x28 + +0x2C == bone_count 585/585**
against adjacent-pair controls 0/585 each. All match the spec exactly.
One near-miss recorded honestly rather than smoothed: the spec's "8,490
zero-translation, 8,489 both zero-translation and same-name" reads 8,489/8,488
under an exact `== 0.0f` test here. Three odd records exist, not two —
`sp_mdsphere.rig_pc` `center` (t = (-0, 0, -0), zero-only), `avatar.rig_pc`
`r-upperarmtwist1` (same-name, t.x = 9.99999997e-07, i.e. 1e-6 not zero), and
`distant_human.rig_pc` `spine` (same-name, t = (-0, 0.3087, 0.0257)). With a
1e-6 tolerance the numbers become exactly the spec's (8,490 / 8,489 / one
zero-only / one same-name-only): a tolerance-definition difference, not a data
disagreement. Reported to Team A. Not yet done here: the full `build_verify/`
object refresh (rig.h changed; do it after the concurrent agent batch below
finishes, as one full `cl /c src\*.cpp`, per the stale-object lesson).
