**Process note for this batch (9.71–9.7x).** After the rig fix I dispatched
parallel Sonnet 5 agents, one per reader, each in an isolated scratchpad build
directory (never `build_verify/`, never CMake/HANDOFF/specs), and re-verified
every headline number myself from freshly-built binaries before recording it.
Working from `spec-asm-format.md` 51,702 bytes, mtime 2026-09-20 08:24
(unchanged start to end of the task).

**Result.** The reader in `include/sr3asm/manifest.h` + `src/manifest.cpp`
was built from the OLDER spec (it scanned for plausible fields) and could not
parse the layout the spec now gives; the agent rewrote it for spec §7 (version
11: header, three tables, records with `record_flags`/`container_kind`/
`source_name`/`extra`/entries, `payload_length`). Independently re-run by me
(fresh build of `validate_asm_population.exe`, `/W4` clean): **805 `.asm_pc`
files in 20 archives, 20,956,590 bytes, 8,362 records, 390,134 entries —
every spec figure MATCH; library exact-EOF 805/805, records parsed == header
count 805/805; a second, independent walker in the harness agrees 805/805
including per-record digests; the three tables are byte-identical in all 805.**
Cross-check against the real sibling `.str2_pc` directories: `header_region_size`
== sibling `payload_start` on 7,990/7,990 and `payload_length` == sibling header
field `0x168` on 7,990/7,990 (8,057 records have a sibling, 305 do not). The
synthetic test is built from the spec text including §7.5's worked example byte
for byte; the agent mutation-tested it (8 mutated reader copies, all caught).
**Controls that collapse the gate** (each 3/805 = only the zero-record files, or
0/805): `entry_count` as u8, no `source_name`, size table moved/dropped, entry
tail 12 or 14 bytes, no `payload_length`, record area ±1/2 bytes, `record_flags`
as u8, truncate/append/insert/delete a byte. Honest limit, stated in the spec
and reproduced: skipping the `extra` blob still scores 805/805 (`extra_len` is 0
everywhere) so only the synthetic test guards it, and the EOF gate cannot catch
a mislabel of same-width fields (covered instead by the sibling cross-check and
table-membership correlations).

**Two disagreements with the spec, reported to Team A, neither blocking.**
(1) §9.4 says the manifest file list equals the sibling directory "in name":
true only case-insensitively — case-exact 6,608/8,057, case-insensitive

`ViolaBC_body_high.cpeg_pc` vs sibling `violabc_body_high.cpeg_pc`). (2) The
spec does not say how to resolve a manifest record whose name matches a
`.str2_pc` in more than one archive: 68 records do, and the choice matters for
24; preferring the same archive gives 8,057/8,057.

**Tool + wiring.** `tools/asm_dump.cpp` replaced (the old one referenced
removed record fields `refName` and two sizes); a new
`tools/validation/validate_asm_population.cpp` was added. CMake: optionally
`add_executable(validate_asm_population ...)` linking `sr3asm`. The reader is
stricter than the engine (rejects any version other than 11 and a wrong magic,
and, as a policy of the agent's, a negative `entry_count` — the spec is silent).

### 9.72 `sr3tree`: the wind-state table and LOD distances, decoded from spec §13 (2026-09-20)

Worked from `spec-tree-format.md` 45,427 bytes, mtime 2026-09-20 14:00 (Team A's
consumer-side pass, agent AE). §9.67's reader had left the `'TREE'` `+0x3C`
"tuning table" and geometry `+0xE0…` as OPEN; the spec resolved both. **Real
bug in the old reader's framing, not just an omission:** the table starts at
block `+0x38`, not `+0x3C` (float index `k` lives at `0x38 + 4k`; `k=0` is 5.0 in
11/11 and the old reader skipped it).

**Changed (`include/sr3tree/tree.h`, `src/tree.cpp`).** The 115-float
`tuningTable` is gone. `TreeBlock` now holds `windFloats[38]` (`k = 0x00…0x25`,
the file-loaded floats) and a typed `wind` (`WindParameters`: response times,
four `WindOscillatorBand` with amplitude/frequency at level 0/1 and exponent,
gust fields), keeping the spec's labels (amplitude/frequency names HIGH
CONFIDENCE, gust fields inert for trees, `k2`'s GPU role OPEN) and
`windRuntimeRegionAllZero()` for block `+0xD0…+0x207` (observed, never a parse
error). Geometry gains `lodDistances[4]` (`+0xE0…+0xEC`, A<B<C<D metres),
`lodDerivedOnDisk[2]` (`+0xF0/+0xF4`, exposed raw — the spec does not say whether
"(B−A)s" uses scaled or unscaled values, so not recomputed), `cullDistance()`
(= D) and pure functions `lodParameterForDistance`/`ForSquaredDistance`,
`windSteadyState(params, level = 0.1)`. No GPU upload, no per-frame simulation.

**Verified by me from a fresh build** (`validate_tree_wind_lod.exe`, 11 distinct
trees / 28 shipped copies, `/W4` clean, **0 gate mismatches**): W1 `k ≥ 0x26`
zero 11/11 (independent raw dword scan agrees); W2 band-frequency pairs
ascending 44/44, one-float-shifted control 0/33; W3 gust ranges 11/11 + 11/11;
W4 exponents > 0 44/44; W6 five parameter sets in groups 5,2,1,2,1; L1 `A<B<C<D`
11/11 while the same predicate at the 12 other 4-float windows in
`+0xC0…+0xFC` scores at most 3/11; L2 derived fields zero on disk 11/11;
§13.4's derived table reproduced by `windSteadyState()` in 132/132 values (worst
0.66%, table rounding). **Zero regression vs §9.67:** `validate_tree.exe`
unchanged output — 28 attempted, 11 distinct, 28 parsed, 96 materials, 1 shader
hash, radius 0.06–1.1, material counts 3:16 4:12, LOD counts 2:17 3:11, capsule

### 9.73 `sr3cutscene`: channel 1 is a unit quaternion; decoded accessors + sampler (2026-09-20)

Worked from `spec-cutscene-camera-format.md` 37,420 bytes, mtime 2026-09-20
09:49 (§10, the sampler decode). The old reader surfaced channel 1 as opaque 8-byte
values ("encoding OPEN"). **Verified by me from a fresh build**
(`validate_csc_sampler.exe`, `/W4` clean): 96 distinct `.csc_pc` files (192
archive entries, 0 name conflicts), 1,405 shots, 96/96 parse with exact size;
**31,898/31,898 channel-1 keys are unit-norm** as 4 × s16 × 16385/2^28 within
2 LSB (`|norm−1|` ≤ 1.69 LSB, median +3.19e-7; the data-implied scale equals the
spec's to a ratio of 0.9999997). Controls that fail: scale 1/32767 and 2^-15 →
0/31,898; unsigned s16 22%; big-endian 1; random quads 0; the weaker scales
2^-14 and 2/32767 pass the tolerance (96.7% / 99.94%) but fail the median pin
(−6.1e-5, −3.0e-5 vs 2e-6). **Honest limit, reproduced:** unit norm is
invariant under any permutation of (x,y,z,w) (all 24 orders give identical
counts, and a second probe on the rotation matrix is also order-blind), so the
(x,y,z,w) order rests on the spec's disassembly claim alone; only a weak hint
(raw slot 3 is ≥ 0 on 80.5% of keys vs 51–65% elsewhere) supports it. Other
spec figures reproduced: FOV 0.0349–1.7453 rad, 2,345/2,345 keys in (0, π); DOF
ordering ch4≤ch5≤ch6≤ch7 on 3,929/3,958 keys; key times absolute on 9,260/9,260
tracks (shot-relative control 558); all 68,736 keys inside their shot.

**Reader change (`include/sr3cutscene/camera_script.h`, `src/camera_script.cpp`).**
Raw and decoded quaternion accessors, `quaternionToMatrix`, `slerpShortestArc`,
per-track samplers, `sampleShot`/`sample`/`shotIndexAt`, `CameraSample` (FOV in
radians and degrees, DOF gate + values); evaluated in double, asserts nothing
about axes or handedness. The agent's independent decoder + sampler agrees with
the library at 204,912 sample times (worst difference 0, decoded quaternions
bit-equal). Synthetic tests built from §10 text pass. `tools/csc_dump.cpp`'s
"encoding OPEN" labels updated (it still prints channel 1 raw).

**Three disagreements with the spec (reported to Team A).** (1) §3's header: keyframe
data starts at `+0x08`, not `+0x0C` — the unique arrays tile `[0x08, record_offset)`
with no gap in 96/96 files and tile from `0x0C` in 0/96 (my run reproduced both
counts). The "zero padding word" at `+0x08` is the first shot's channel-0 times
array's first key (0.0f, the first shot's start time). The widths and structure
are right; the "12-byte header, align to 12" explanation looks wrong. Reader
behaviour was already correct (comments only). (2) Channels 3–7 share one times
array in all 1,009 shots that carry them; §3/§8 don't mention the sharing.
(3) §10.6.3/§4's "more than one frame" tail counts reproduce only with a
threshold of about 0.0335 s, not 1/30 s: at 0.0335 s I get 927 shots and 39/96
files (the spec's numbers); at 1/30 s, 1,091 and 26/96. Median, p90 and max tail
match. §10.6.4 (tail hold, hard cuts, downstream cut smoothing) stays open: the
data is only consistent with them.

Worked from `spec-save-format.md` 232,315 bytes, mtime 2026-09-20 08:24 (~1,110

project's own `test-fixtures\saves`): 16 distinct snapshots, 4 directories, 3
profiles. `sr3def_profile` is in no archive (0 name hits over 405,694 entry
names in 39 archives; compressed nested containers not expanded) — loose files
only, as §1 says.

**Gates, re-run by me from freshly built binaries (`/W4` clean):**
- **Profile (§7): 3/3 distinct profiles pass; 179 records consume exactly
  891/891 bytes** (chunk 1: 0/0), 179 = 217 − 38 omitted ids, lengths

  tail, zlib-style init/complement, end shifted, tail ±1, one byte flipped, start

### 9.75 `sr3foliage`: the `+0x38` table is a per-LOD fade/draw-group/billboard table (2026-09-20)

Worked from `spec-foliage-format.md` 23,412 bytes, mtime 2026-09-20 14:00 (§11,
agent AE). The old reader surfaced the outer block's "`+0x38` table" as six
anonymous floats per record (HYPOTHESIS). **The framing was wrong in two ways,
both now fixed:** the table is at `B + i32(B+0x38)` (a signed offset relative to
the outer-block base, NOT at `B+0x38`; read from `B+0x38` it scores 0/19), and
words 4 and 5 are `u32`s (`drawGroupIndex` 0/1/2, `billboardFlag` 0/1), not
floats (`fol_weed_a01` printed 0 where the real values are group 1/2 and
billboard 1).

**Verified by me from a fresh build** (`validate_foliage_lod.exe`, `/W4` clean,
19 `.cfmesh_pc` files, "ALL GATES MATCH THE SPEC'S NUMBERS"): tail from the
table start to EOF == `count × 24` 19/19, controls at strides 16/20/28/32 0/19
each; `fadeInStart ≤ fadeInEnd` and `fadeOutStart ≤ fadeOutEnd` 37/37 records
each; `billboardFlag ∈ {0,1}` 19/19 (histogram 0:35, 1:2); `drawGroupIndex` 0×19,
1×16, 2×2; records per file 1×3, 2×14, 3×2; consecutive LODs cross-fade over the
same interval in 15/18 pairs, the three exceptions being `fol_weed_a01` and both
pairs of `oas_fol_grass_a`; the material-handle table is located 19/19, identity
`0…n−1` 19/19, header count == material count 19/19. An independent raw-byte
pass (not using the reader) finds the outer block once per file 19/19 and the
reader's decode is bit-identical to it 19/19. **Zero regression:**
`validate_foliage` output identical to the old log (parse 19/19, 33 records, 2
shader hashes, 13 variant hashes, 79 bindings).

**Reader (`include/sr3foliage/foliage_mesh.h`, `src/foliage_mesh.cpp`).**
`LodRecord` has `fadeInStart/End`, `fadeOutStart/End`, `drawGroupIndex`,
`billboardFlag`; new `lodRecordCount()`, `hasLodTable()`, `lodTableOffset()`,
`lodTableTailBytes()`, `outerField34()` (raw, OPEN), `materialHandleTable()`
(offset, header words, handles, `isIdentity()`). `parse()` now throws unless the
tail equals `count × 24` exactly (and on a negative offset other than −1, or a
table start before the name table); a non-identity handle table is NOT an error
(the on-disk values are load-time placeholders). Synthetic suite rewritten from
the spec text; **13 mutants of a copy of the reader, all killed** (table at
`B+0x38`, offset not B-relative, strides 16/20/28/32, count taken from `+0x34`,
tail slack tolerated, group/billboard swapped, fadeIn reading fadeOut, handle
header size 8, and combinations without the tail check). The fadeIn ramp's shader
use stays HIGH CONFIDENCE (not read); no ramp constants are derived.
`tools/foliage_dump.cpp` now prints the named fields.

**Disagreements with the spec (reported to Team A).** (1) §3 says the runtime
slot array is zero-filled: it is 0/19 zero. Each 8-byte slot is
`{u32 = B-relative offset of material record i, u32 0}` (19/19). (2) §4 marks
`+0x10/+0x14` runtime-only; on disk `+0x10` is non-zero and equals the Mesh
block end (`meshRel` + the length at `mesh+0x08`) 19/19, the handle table starts
exactly at `align8` of it 19/19, and `+0x14` is 0. (3) Outer `+0x24` is not in
§4: 19 distinct non-zero heap-pointer-like values, not decoded. (4) §11.2's
"plants 8–32" is loose: plant fadeOut values go down to 5–6
(`fol_grass_lg_a01`, `oas_fol_grass_a`). The reader uses none of (1)–(3). An

### 9.76 `.fxo_pc` header formula + first `.cefct_pc` reader; **the container's directory `+0x08` is NOT the physical stream offset** (2026-09-20)

Worked from `spec-fxo-format.md` 47,793 B (08:24), `spec-effects-format.md`
69,762 B (09:49), `spec-vpp-container.md` 76,518 B (08:24), all unchanged during
the run. **Verified by me from fresh builds** (`validate_fxo_header.exe`,
`validate_cefct_population.exe`, both `/W4` clean, both synthetic suites pass).

**THE HEADLINE — a container-layer finding, not an fxo one.** Decoding
`.fxo_pc` through `vpp::Container` (directory `+0x08` offsets) yields only 108 of
844 entries (`NoValidZlibHeaderAtOffset` ×420, `ZlibStreamError` ×316 + 847 for
`.fxo_pc_dx11`, 1,585 failures in `shaders.vpp_pc` alone), and of the 108 that
"decode" (`OkUnconfirmedContent`) the data is SHORT — exact consumption 2/108, the
decoded bytes stop at ~20–90% of the header-implied size. Not a formula error
(the trusted sample and the two exact files are right): **`+0x08` does not locate
the stream.** The physical offset is `payloadStart + Σ over earlier entries of
roundup(+0x10, 0x800)` (spec §3.3's loader accumulation; flags bit `0x1`). Oracle:
the unbounded inflate length equals the entry's OWN `+0x0C`. **Reproduced by me:
1,693/1,693 top-level compressed `.fxo*` entries in `shaders.vpp_pc` inflate to
exactly `+0x0C` at the corrected offset (failed identity or offset outside the
file: 0), versus 2/256 at `+0x08`**; the agent also got 1,908/1,908 sampled
over the 9 flags-`0x4801` archives. This is the "only entry 0 of a mode-(a)
container decodes" limitation from `spec-xtbl-format.md` §1 and the reason
`vpp::Container` has the `RecoveredSharedStream` backward-walk workaround. **NOT
fixed in `src/container.cpp` (outside the agent's edit set; and paused).** The
corrected rule is proven only on flags-`0x4801` archives. **This is the top
candidate when work resumes:** re-implement the physical-offset rule in
`vpp::Container`, then re-measure everything that was excluded as "at risk"
(76 mode-(a) index>0 PEG c-files, non-first xtbl entries, the 847
`.fxo_pc_dx11`, and re-run the archive-wide decode-status census).

**PART 1 (`.fxo_pc`).** Trusted sample (entry 0 of `shaders.vpp_pc`, 1,408 B):
16/16 spec-stated values reproduced (H = 200, first blob 208, lengths 732@0xA8 /
464@0xB0, dword at 0xB8 = `0xFFFF0000`, end == 1,408); T1/T3 hash(CRC of lowercased
name) + register vs the bytecode constant table 5/5. **At the corrected offsets:
`.fxo_pc` 844/844 applicable, 844/844 exact consumption (837 distinct), 7,276/7,276
blobs carry the right-stage D3D9 version token and end token** (my run of
section 6a). Controls: align-8 instead of 16 passes 24 (differs on 820); no
alignment 16; unaligned first blob 588 (differs on 256, the spec right on all
256); H without the `0x10·c8` term 0; without the stage-table entries 0; without
the `8·(c3+c4)` terms 12. Supplementary `.fxo_pc_dx11`: 847/847 exact, 277 have
`nMid = 1` and consume only with the middle blobs stepped over (so §8.3's "none
seen" is now 277), `T8+0x02 ∈ [0,nMid)` 277/277, 8,166/8,166 blobs begin "DXBC";
the two bare `.fxo` are raw DXBC without the wrapper. Disagreements: T1–T4
hash+register match 18,652/19,928 (1,269 hash a name absent from every constant
table, 8 differ in register); version 14 ×1,691 (>14 never seen); T0 is populated
in 784 files, T4 in 181, T2 in 1.

**PART 2 (`.cefct_pc`, Team A's enumeration ask).** New library `sr3effects`
(`include/sr3effects/effects.h`, `src/effects.cpp`) built from the spec's CONFIRMED
fields, synthetic test from the spec text. **Reproduced by me over all 38 archives:
1,812 `.cefct_pc` entries (547 distinct contents), all parse; non-zero counts, occurrences
/ distinct files: `root+0x40` 346/135, `root+0x70` 595/168, `root+0x90` 478/119**;
count-value distributions identical to the agent's (e.g. `0x40`: 1×109 2×69 3×29 …
202×2; `0x70`: 1×520 2×55 3×11 4×2 8×2 11×5; `0x90`: 1×179 2×98 3×178 4×6 5×6 6×2
8×2 26×5 33×2). Combinations (agent): none 871, `0x90` only 86, `0x70` only 176,
`0x70+0x90` 333, `0x40` only 249, `0x40+0x90` 11, `0x40+0x70` 38, all three 48.
`root+0x40` stride `0x88` tiles exactly on 346/346 (wrong strides 0/346). Cleanest
examples (per-entry `Ok`, `preload_effects.vpp_pc`): `0x40` `vfx_cybertank_projectile`,
`vfx_kneecappers`, `vfx_lasersight`; `0x70` `vfx_carunderglow`, `vfx_brakelight`;
`0x90` `vfx_sun_glare`, `vfx_amberrunninglights`; large counts in cutscene effects
(`vfx_roof_destruction` 202, `18_in_planelights` 11, `vfx_mbrawl_cflashes` 33).
**A denominator lesson the spec's own gate hides:** the spec's strict end-field gate
(`root+0x38 == size − root`) holds 1,468/1,812 and FAILS 344, **all with `root+0x40 > 0`**
— under that gate `root+0x40` is non-zero in only 2 files (my "SET E" run) versus 346 under the
structural gate. Every trailing byte of those 344 is a 2-aligned NUL-terminated
texture-name string table (344/344), so the end pointer is simply not EOF there.

**Disagreements with the spec (effects), reported to Team A:** §5.2 name-table
length = Σ(strlen+1) of the texture names only (1,812/1,812), not names plus the

### 9.99 Adopted from external decompilation-project research: `WALLS.md`, `STATE.md`, one new rule (2026-09-28)

Orchestrator relayed a user-commissioned research document (`AI-WORKFLOW-INSTRUCTIONS.md`, distilled
from public Claude-assisted decompilation projects — Snowboard Kids 2, dc3-decomp, Ratchet & Clank,
1379.tech's recomp work, others) and asked what to fold into this project's own working rules. Read the
source document directly (not just the relay's summary) before deciding — full text in that file.

**Adopted, concretely, this session:**
- **`WALLS.md`** (new file) — a flat, dedicated ruled-out-approaches index, consolidating what was
  scattered across §D/§E and individual §9.xx sections (the `<root><Table>` non-universality, the
  first-location-only undercounting bug pattern, the length-capped-decoder trap, statistical controls
  needing a shuffle baseline, the vtable-offset-coincidence trap that bit Team A's render-pipeline work
  twice). Every future new-format/new-investigation agent brief should say "check WALLS.md first."
- **`STATE.md`** (new file) — a real-denominator snapshot table (19 binary/container readers, ~236
  typed `.xtbl` tables across 10 domains, rendering-milestone status), sourced to HANDOFF sections
  rather than re-arguing anything, for "how far along are we" without reading all of §9.
- **Rule 14** (§ "rules that mattered most" list): "what would a wrong answer that still passes this
  gate look like?" — a sharper, directly-actionable framing of this project's existing rule 12 (an
  oracle must be able to fail). Added to every future agent brief, not just harness design.
- **Already-practiced, now explicitly named rather than just emergent**: PASS/FAIL-with-denominators
  in every harness (already universal this project); attaching the most similar closed spec/reader as

materially closer match to the source bytecode's own shader model (legacy `sampler2D`/`tex2D()`,
`POSITION`/`COLORn`/`TEXCOORDn` semantics) than forcing an SM4 retarget would be, which would introduce
translation-target artifacts (SV_Position renaming, Texture2D+SamplerState splitting) unrelated to the
bytecode's real semantics. Reasoned, stated up front, not a silent substitution.

**Real bugs found and fixed during the population run** (genuine findings caught at ~1,500-blob scale,
not guesses): (1) Stage-1's own documented positional-decode limitation misfiles `IF`/`IFC`/`REP`'s
operand into `Instruction::dest` since these opcodes have no real destination - fixed in the
TRANSLATOR (not Stage 1) via `reinterpretDestAsSource()`, with 3 regression tests added; (2)
`DEPTHOUT`'s HLSL field is scalar `float` but real bytecode still encodes a full `.xyzw` write mask on
it, causing a real `D3DCompile` error (X3018) until clamped to the register's actual component count;
(3) via a dedicated probe built specifically to satisfy the "confirm semantic spelling empirically"
instruction: `TESSFACTOR`/`POSITIONT` are valid `D3DDECLUSAGE` values but REJECTED as vs_3_0 input
semantics by the real compiler (X4502, falls back to TEXCOORD), and PS `COLORn` outputs must be
contiguous from `COLOR0` (X4538) - both defensively handled, 0 real occurrences either way.

### 9.101 Data-side mesh→shader hash-join investigation — ~~CLOSED, decisive negative~~ CORRECTED 2026-09-29: the join DOES work, wrong hash + wrong input string, not a wrong idea

**Correction, same day, before this was even reported further.** The negative conclusion below was
**WRONG**, kept struck through rather than deleted per this project's own standing practice (matching
Team A's own §22.6 precedent in `spec-render-pipeline.md`). Team A's own disassembly trace independently
re-opened this (§22.9-§22.11 there): the on-disk `shaderHash` field genuinely IS a CRC-32 hash of the
shader's own filename — **but of the STAGE-SUFFIX-STRIPPED STEM specifically** (e.g. `ir_sr3carpaint_gr`,
never `ir_sr3carpaint_gr_bs.fxo_pc` and never even `ir_sr3carpaint_gr_bs` — the 13-suffix stage
convention, `spec-fxo-format.md` §6.6, has to be stripped FIRST), using a SPECIFIC CRC-32 parameterization
(reflected `0xEDB88320`, init `0`, no final XOR — `sr3fxo::crc32Raw`, already in this codebase,
`include/sr3fxo/wrapper_header.h`) that is neither `sr3xtbl::NameHash`/`NameHashCaseSensitive` nor
`vpp::hashFilename`. The 6 combinations tried below hashed the FULL filename or the extension-only stem
(still carrying the `_bs`/`_ms`/`_mv`/`_s`/`_v` stage suffix) with the wrong hash functions — two
independent misses stacked, either one alone would have caused the negative.

**Independently re-verified by me, not taken from Team A's relay.** Re-derived the suffix-stripping table
myself from `spec-fxo-format.md` §6.6's own text (13 suffixes, longest-match-first to avoid an ambiguous
double-strip: `_bms`/`_bmc`/`_bs`/`_bc`/`_ms`/`_mc`/`_mv`/`_ts`/`_fd`/`_s`/`_c`/`_t`/`_v`), reused this
project's own existing `sr3fxo::crc32Raw` (not copied from any Team A script), and tested it against **my
own previously-extracted 17 real vehicle `shaderHash` values** (obtained independently below, not from
Team A's harness) AND the tree control value: **17/17 exact match, plus the tree's `0x967A81C0` also now
matches exactly (`tree_s.fxo_pc`, stem `"tree"`)**. Spot-checked the two stems Team A's §22.11 names as
most common: `ir_sr3carpaint_gr` → `0x09B15FCE` (IS in my 17), `ir_sr3carglass_g` → `0x8EB886E6` (IS in my
17). **A third independent convergence**: both `ir_sr3carpaint_gr_v.fxo_pc` and `ir_sr3carglass_g_v.fxo_pc`
are ALSO members of §9.102's filename-blind 49-name vertex-input-signature candidate set — three

agree on real vehicle-body shader identities. **[CONFIRMED — independently reproduced by me, fresh build,
against my own previously-extracted real data, not taken on either peer's word.]**

**New rule, earned directly by this incident (added to "the rules that mattered most" as rule 15):** a
negative result from a hash/name-join test is only as trustworthy as the exact input STRING and hash
PARAMETERIZATION it used — state both explicitly before anyone (including the same session later) treats

indistinguishable "no match" result. Both this session and Team A briefly took the other's relayed
negative/positive at face value before independently re-checking — worth remembering that the relay
discipline (`peer-relay-authorization.md`) applies just as much to a peer's *negative* finding as to a
positive one.

### 9.105 `sr3_viewer pose`/`animpose` no longer refuse multi-channel character meshes — real canonical fix, independently rebuilt/rerun exactly (2026-09-29)

**Task.** Orchestrator-prioritized follow-up to §9.103/§9.104: the two `sr3_viewer.cpp` refusal sites
(fixed comments only, same day) still REFUSED to render `alien_e01`/`alien_es01` at the draw groups
where their ranges span more than one vertex channel, because the code didn't yet read `DrawRange::
submeshIndex` per range - it just knew the data question was answered. This closes that gap for real.
Built by a Sonnet 5 agent; **independently rebuilt from fresh objects and reran the full verification
plan myself** (code review + fresh `/W4` compile + fresh link + both affected synthetic suites + the
orchestrator's own specified MD5 regression + visual confirmation of the new capability) before
recording anything or touching `build_verify/`.

**Real canonical files changed** (an explicit, authorized exception to "agents don't touch canonical
files" - this is a real bug fix, not a diagnostic, same category as §9.68/§9.87's own precedent):
`include/sr3rig/bone_palette.h`/`src/bone_palette.cpp` - `resolveVertexSetConflictsByDuplication()`
gained a 4th, nullable `rangeMask` parameter (null = every pre-existing call site, byte-identical);
`include/sr3render/mesh_renderer.h`/`src/mesh_renderer.cpp` - `MeshRenderer::upload()` gained a matching
5th nullable `rangeMask` parameter, same contract; `tools/sr3_viewer.cpp` - new `MultiChannelMultiSetRender`
class (one `MeshRenderer` per distinct `submeshIndex` a group's ranges use, each fed its own channel
decode + its own per-channel conflict-resolution/remap scoped via `rangeMask`, sharing one depth buffer)
and `runMultiChannelFrames()`, reached only when the existing single-channel remap already produced
`lanesDroppedPaletteOutOfRange != 0` - structurally unreachable for any single-channel mesh, which is
the regression guarantee stated as a property of the code, not just tested behavior.

**Independently verified, every step:**
- **Code review**: read all three diffs in full before rebuilding anything. The `rangeMask` extension is
  minimal (one nullable parameter, no new state, existing null-path unchanged), and the new

**Task** (orchestrator relay, Team A's §23.5/§23.8 open items): what do the 3 bound G-buffer render
targets contain, and where does `IR_GBuffer_DSF_DataSampler` bind — Team A's own literal-string search of

resolution), scanning `shaders.vpp_pc` directly — real data, not disassembly.

below).** All 13 real `ir_light_*` shaders named in §23.6 exist as real `.fxo_pc` files; every one's PS
CTAB declares the same 3 named samplers at the same 3 registers: `IR_GBuffer_LightingSampler`@s12,

§23.5's disassembly-confirmed count of 3 bound color targets, but **NOT independently shown to be the
SAME 3 targets**. **Correction (orchestrator/Team A, same day, caught an overclaim in this entry's first
draft):** a light shader reading its own accumulation target as an input would be architecturally
unusual — Team A's refined §23.5 builds the actual light-accumulation buffer in a separate, later stage,
so `IR_GBuffer_LightingSampler` more plausibly names a PREPASS-WRITTEN LIGHTING-PARAMETER target (e.g.
specular/roughness data), not the final lit-color output the naming coincidence first suggested. **Stated
correctly: these are the 3 samplers `ir_light_*` shaders read from, at registers s12/s13/s14 — not yet a
confirmed answer to what the prepass's 3 bound targets actually hold.** Team A is independently checking
the real target formats, which will settle it. `ir_light_spot*`/`ir_light_point_tex` additionally declare
`Shadow_map_projTM`/`Camera_*`/`ir_shadow_mapSampler`/`Projection_texture*` (shadow-mapped/projected
variants); `ir_light_overdraw_debug` is structurally minimal (1 PS constant, no G-buffer sampler at all)
— a debug-only shader, consistent with its name. **[CONFIRMED — real CTAB data, all 13 files, both
passes each.]**

**Part 2 — `IR_GBuffer_DSF_DataSampler`: 675/844 real `.fxo_pc` files (80%) declare it, ALL at sampler
register s9** (1,329/1,329 blob-level hits, population-exact, zero exceptions — a whole-archive scan, not
a sample). Consistent with, and independently corroborates, `ir_sr3carpaint_gr_v.fxo_pc`'s own already-
known s9 value (§20.12.2). **Not present in any of the 13 `ir_light_*` deferred-lighting shaders** —
it's a FORWARD-material-pass sampler, not a deferred-lighting one: heavily concentrated among ordinary
opaque/decal/foliage/glass/vehicle materials (`ir_sr3carpaint_*`, `ir_decal_*`, `ir_bbsimple*`,

lighting pass's own targets. **This is a real, useful, independent angle Team A's exe-string search
couldn't produce** (the name only exists inside the shader bytecode's own CTAB, compiled separately from
the exe — consistent with, not contradicting, their zero-hits result). **The exact engine-side binding

**[CONFIRMED — whole-archive population scan, 844/844 `.fxo_pc` entries parsed cleanly, 0 parse
failures, exact counts throughout.]**

**Part 3, same day — the "prepass parameter buffer vs. final accumulated light" reconciliation, done by
tracing real bytecode.** Team A/orchestrator flagged (after Part 1's correction, above) that a light
shader reading its own accumulation target as input would be architecturally odd, and asked what the
shader's bytecode actually DOES with the `IR_GBuffer_LightingSampler`(s12) read. Traced directly
(`tools scratchpad trace_lighting_sampler.cpp`, disassembles the real PS bytecode and follows every
downstream use of the sampled register): in `ir_light_directional`, `ir_light_point`, and
`ir_light_local_ambient` (3 structurally different light types, both real T8 passes each, 6 blobs total)
— **the sampled value is never added/blended wholesale into the output.** Instead its components are
individually unpacked with scale+bias `MAD`s against named constants, then fed into `POW` (a specular-
exponent-shaped op), `NRM` (normalize — applied to a LIGHT-COLOR value would be meaningless; a
direction/parameter vector, not so), `RCP`, and `DP3`, before finally contributing to the pixel's lit
output through further math. **This is real, consistent, decisive bytecode evidence FOR the
"prepass-written lighting-PARAMETER buffer" hypothesis** (packed specular/roughness/fresnel-shaped
surface data) **and AGAINST "final accumulated light color, read back and re-blended."** Honest limit:
this identifies the USAGE PATTERN, not the exact per-channel semantic meaning (what x/y/z individually
decode to) — that would need per-constant tracing this pass didn't attempt. **[CONFIRMED — real
disassembled bytecode, 3 distinct light-shader types, all real PS blobs of each.]**

**Part 4, same day — `IR_Light_Pos`/`Color`/`Info`/`Spot_Info`'s real PS registers, confirmed from the
clean CTAB side, closing Team A's own HIGH-CONFIDENCE-not-confirmed flag (`spec-render-pipeline.md`

needed) across all 11 real light-shader files that declare these names: **`IR_Light_Pos` is register c0
in every one, zero exceptions. `IR_Light_Info`'s register is always exactly `IR_Light_Color`'s register

declare `Info` confirm this, zero exceptions. **`IR_Spot_Info`'s register is always exactly `IR_Light_
Info`'s register +1** (e.g. `ir_light_spot`: Info@c14/Spot_Info@c15) — 4/4 spot variants confirm this,
zero exceptions. **[CONFIRMED — real CTAB data, population-exact, 11/11 real files, 0 exceptions.]**

+ `readConstantTable` + `translateToHlsl`) and reproduced this exact final line myself. Team A's own

executable's initialized memory** — no code path could even hash-check it by name — and explicitly
flagged as NOT-YET-TRACED whether any of the 14 zero-defaulted names is used multiplicatively in this
specific shader's own bytecode. **That open question is now closed, by direct bytecode read: yes, and
it's the shader's FINAL, all-channel multiplier.** Since the shipped game plainly shows painted (non-black)
cars, this means a non-zero value for register c37 must come from somewhere Team A's static/literal-data
search wouldn't find — most plausibly something COMPUTED at runtime rather than loaded from static
initialized data, which is exactly the shape of the still-open "material-buffer GPU-upload call site" gap

guessed**: `ir_ambient_occlusionSampler` was initially bound to the "neutral white" placeholder, but the
real HLSL computes `r0.y = saturate(1 - AO.x)` — white (1.0) means fully occluded, zeroing the ambient
term; fixed with a dedicated black placeholder. The tool's first chosen light direction had the wrong Z
sign for its own view convention (G-buffer normals are view-space, +Z is into-screen in
`computeOrbitViewMatrix`), saturating N·L to 0 over the whole surface; fixed by flipping the sign.

reservedBytes` (default 0) — bytes to skip in `decodeChannel()`'s cursor walk without decoding them into

### 9.117 Engine→script hook-firing pass + `thread_*` coroutine scheduler — 133 confirmed hooks fired against all 804 real scripts, new all-inclusive stub-hit ranking (2026-09-29)

**Task.** Orchestrator's queue item 1, "the main item": close the gap §9.113 left open — `lua_pcall` on a
script's top level only runs its top-level statements, so a script that's mostly `function some_hook_name()
... end` definitions never gets its own logic exercised; the real engine calls INTO those functions later,
by name. Built by a Sonnet 5 agent (2nd attempt, 1st died to the same rate limit as the zone-tile task,
not a real failure); **fully independently rebuilt by me from FRESH source** — compiled the vendored Lua
5.1 myself again, compiled all 4 `sr3luahost` source files (incl. the 2 new ones) under `/W4` (0 warnings,
confirmed), built and ran the synthetic test suite, then rebuilt and reran `lua_host_run` against the real
archive cache end-to-end.

**The 133-entry hook table (`include/sr3luahost/hook_registry.h` + `src/lua_hook_registry.cpp`) — I
cross-checked every name, group, and count by hand against `spec-lua-bindings.md` §12.3/§12.4/§12.6's own
numbered listings** (not just skimmed): 73 Group 1 (existence-gated, CONFIRMED literal call-site names),
2 Group 2 (`_PrepareForDynamicGlobals`/`_DynamicGlobalsLoadComplete`, UNCONDITIONAL real call per §12.4's
documented asymmetry — existence still measured for honesty, never gates the call), 58 Group 3
(mission-numbered, existence-gated, tagged distinctly as HIGH-CONFIDENCE/pattern-based — only 2 of the
underlying 60 strings were individually dispatcher-confirmed, already counted in Group 1). Every one of
the 133 names, in order, matches the spec exactly; sums to 73+2+58=133. Groups 4/5 (unbounded
sprintf-templated families / null runtime-populated tables) correctly excluded from concrete firing, per
the spec's own text.

**`Host::fireConfirmedHooks()`** (`host.h`/`lua_host.cpp`), read and verified line-by-line: real
`lua_getglobal`+`lua_isfunction` existence check (measured for every group); Group 1/3 skip the call if
not a function (matches the real engine's own silent-check behavior); Group 2 always attempts the call
regardless. Every hook called with 0 arguments (spec doesn't confirm per-hook argument shapes — stated
plainly in the tool's own output, not invented). A real Lua 5.1 instruction-count watchdog
(`lua_sethook`+`LUA_MASKCOUNT`, budget 5,000,000) wraps ONLY the hook-call `lua_pcall`, never
`runChunk()` — a real, evidenced necessity: `game_lib.lua`'s own text (grepped directly) contains
`repeat thread_yield() until teleport_check_done(...)`-shaped loops, and every stub returns nil, so an
unguarded hook body reaching an equivalent pattern would hang the tool forever.

**`thread_*` scheduler** (`include/sr3luahost/thread_scheduler.h` + `src/lua_thread_scheduler.cpp`):
`thread_new` creates a real (but never-resumed) Lua 5.1 thread via `lua_newthread`+`luaL_ref`; a handle is

### 9.119 Two clean-side checks for "what calls `<stem>_start`" — a real, decisive table-driven finding (`mission_checkpoints.xtbl`) plus a clean negative on Lua-side dynamic dispatch (2026-09-29)

**Task.** Orchestrator's follow-up to §9.118: Team A found no mission-lifecycle sprintf template anywhere
in the exe (an exhaustive negative), yet 63/51/50 real scripts define top-level `<stem>_start`/`_run`/
`_success`. Two real, data-only checks, done directly: (1) do any real `.xtbl` table rows name these
functions or their script stems; (2) do any real scripts build these names DYNAMICALLY (`_G[...]`,
`loadstring`, string concatenation) rather than the engine calling a static name. Two new standalone
tools, same archive-walk convention as every other census tool here: `tools/xtbl_name_grep.cpp` (plain
substring search over every real, decompressed `.xtbl` file's own text — `.xtbl` is XML, `spec-tables-*.md`
§1 — not limited to any one typed-reader domain, exhaustive over all 1,888 real `.xtbl` files found),
`tools/lua_dynamic_dispatch_grep.cpp` (pattern search over all 804 real scripts' own text).

**Check 1 — a real, substantial positive: `mission_checkpoints.xtbl`.** Searched for the 54 distinct real
stems (from §9.118's own `_start`/`_run`/`_success` matches) plus their 151 full `<stem>_start`/`_run`/
`_success` function names, 205 needles total, across all 1,888 real `.xtbl` files (4,711 raw substring
hits, but the overwhelming majority are noise from short 3-4-char stems like `m01`/`sh01` matching inside
unrelated longer identifiers — checked directly, not assumed: **zero** of the 151 full function-name
needles matched anywhere). Filtering to the longer, low-false-positive-risk stems and inspecting real
context isolates one real, decisive table: **`mission_checkpoints.xtbl`** (both the base-game copy in
`misc_tables.vpp_pc` and a DLC-extending copy in `patch_compressed.vpp_pc`) has a `<MissionName>` field
whose exact value equals the real mission's own script stem — confirmed for **35 of the 54 real
`_start`-defining stems (64.8%)**: `m01`-`m24` (24), `sh01`-`sh04` (4), `mm_p_03`, `dlc2_m01`/`_m02`/`_m03`,
`dlc3_m01`/`_m02`/`_m03` (35 total, exact `<MissionName>X</MissionName>` values extracted and counted
directly, not estimated). Real schema (read directly, `misc_tables.vpp_pc`'s copy): each `<MissionCheckpoints>`
row has `<Name>` (e.g. `m01-01`), `<MissionName>` (e.g. `m01`), `<Index>`, `<CheckpointName>` (e.g.
`m01_checkpoint_plant_bombs`), `<_Editor><Category>Entries:m01</Category></_Editor>`, `<Debug>`. The
remaining ~19 non-covered stems (`dlc1_mm_01`-`06`, `cutscene_titles`, `hud_collection`, etc.) are NOT
main-campaign missions in this table's own scheme — consistent with those being side-activity/UI scripts
whose own `_start` convention is unrelated to mission-checkpoint tracking specifically.

**What this does and doesn't establish, stated plainly**: this is real, decisive evidence that the engine
identifies missions by their EXACT script stem through data (not just a Lua-side or purely-disassembly
convention) — a genuinely new, useful data point. It does **not**, by itself, prove this specific table is
what triggers a call to `<stem>_start` (this table's own fields are about CHECKPOINT tracking/save-state,
not dispatch) — but it strongly narrows where a real disassembly trace should look next: whatever reads
`mission_checkpoints.xtbl`'s `MissionName` field at runtime is a strong candidate to also be (or lead to)
the real mission-entry dispatcher. **Relayed to Team A directly, as instructed**, since this changes where
their own disassembly search should look.

**Check 2 — a clean, exhaustive negative on Lua-side dynamic dispatch.** Searched all 804 real scripts'
own text for `_G[`, `_G.`, `rawget(_G`, `loadstring`, `getfenv`, `setfenv`, and quoted `"_start"`/`"_run"`/
`"_success"`/`"_init"`/`"_cleanup"` string literals (single- and double-quoted). **Zero matches, across the
full population** — no real shipped script builds one of these entry-point names dynamically anywhere.
This rules out "the Lua side does its own generic name-based dispatch" as an explanation; the real
mechanism, whatever it is, lives on the engine/native side (consistent with check 1's own table-driven
finding pointing the same direction).

**Task.** Third and decisive follow-up to §9.118/§9.119: neither Team A's exhaustive sprintf/strcat

(§9.118's own population), search every one of the 804 real scripts' own `sr3lua::ScriptAnalysis::calls`
(untouched by the `isTopLevel` addition) for a call to that EXACT name, and classify same-script /

called anywhere in the real shipped Lua source at all.** The 441 never-called figure is the decisive
signal: the overwhelming majority of these functions have no Lua-side caller whatsoever — consistent only
with the engine calling them directly, natively, by name.

**The specific pattern, confirmed by direct inspection of 3 real scripts (not inferred from the count
alone)** — every single one of the 24 base-game `mNN_run` functions, plus every `dlc2_m0N`/`dlc3_m0N`/

itself is called by essentially NOTHING in the Lua source (only 2 of the 63 real `_start` names show up as
called at all, both non-mission UI cases: `hud_collection_start`/`main_menu_load_start`/`reward_granted_start`
— none of the 54 real mission-shaped `_start` names appear as a call site anywhere).

**Ties directly to §9.119's `mission_checkpoints.xtbl` finding**: `_start`'s own real parameter is named
`<stem>_checkpoint` and the table's own real schema tracks exactly that — a per-mission `<Index>`/
`<CheckpointName>` under a `<MissionName>` key matching the script's stem. The coherent picture, real
evidence on both sides, engine-side mechanism still not disassembly-traced: the engine reads
`mission_checkpoints.xtbl` for the current mission's checkpoint state, then calls `<stem>_start(checkpoint,
is_restart)` directly by name (native/engine-side — consistent with §14.7's own sprintf/strcat negative,

call — no further engine involvement needed for that hop. **Relayed to Team A** as the concrete shape to
now trace disassembly-side (a direct/table-driven call, not a template).

### 9.123 Bare-name-reference census — the fourth and final cheap data-side check on "what calls `<stem>_start`"; a clean negative, thread now exhausted on this project's own side (2026-09-29)

**Task.** Fourth follow-up: neither §9.118 (definitions), §9.119 (dynamic dispatch/table strings), nor
§9.121 (call sites) covers a `<stem>_start` function referenced as a plain VALUE without being called —
a table field (`{start = m01_start}`), a bare function argument, an assignment RHS. New tool `tools/
lua_bare_reference_census.cpp`: runs both `sr3lua::Parser::analyze()` (for authoritative real call/define
`(line,col)` positions) and a raw `sr3lua::Lexer` token walk (for every `Name` token's own position) over
the same source per script; any of the 54 real distinct `_start` full names' token occurrences that
matches neither a known call nor a known define position is a real, non-call, non-define reference.
**Stated plainly, per this tool's own header comment: this is pattern/position matching, not full
expression-context classification** — it proves a token exists outside call/define positions, not what
kind of value-use it is.

**Result, full population, 0 parse/lex failures**: **74 total `_start`-name token occurrences across all
804 scripts; ALL 74 match a known call or define position; 0 bare references.** A clean, exhaustive
negative — no real shipped script hands any `<stem>_start` function around as a value anywhere.

**This closes the cheap, data-side leg of the "what calls `<stem>_start`" investigation on this project's
own side.** Combined real state across all 4 checks this session (§9.118/§9.119/§9.121/§9.123): definitions
exist (63 real instances, 54 distinct); no dynamic string-building (0/804); no bare value-passing (0/74);
`_start` itself is called from Lua only in 2 non-mission UI cases, never for any of the 54 real mission
stems; `_run` is always called from within that same script's own `_start`. Team A's parallel disassembly
work independently reached the same wall from their side (pre-baked literal search also negative,
0/35 stems, after their earlier sprintf/strcat negatives) and concluded the real mechanism is likely
either numeric dispatch or a function VALUE captured directly at chunk-load time (not a name lookup at
all) — a genuine, disassembly-only next step, not something this project's clean-room data-side tools can
resolve further. **Per this project's own "no invented fixes" policy: documented here as the current,
honest state of this thread rather than guessed past — parked pending a new lead from Team A's own side,
not chased further from data alone.**

Built by a Sonnet 5 agent from `spec-d3d9-sm2-sm3-bytecode.md` (§9.96) alone, explicitly instructed not

validate_d3d9bc_population.cpp`. Wired into `CMakeLists.txt` + `build_one.bat` by me.

**Population gate, independently reproduced, exact:** 844/844 `.fxo_pc` entries decompressed; **7,276
blobs attempted, 7,276/7,276 walked cleanly** to a valid end token with zero overrun/underrun/trailing
bytes. **Correction (2026-09-28, Team A caught this precisely):** this matches the 7,276 figure
`spec-fxo-format.md` §9 cites - but that citation is ITSELF attributed there to Team B, 2026-09-20,
explicitly marked "not yet re-derived" by Team A and "treat as a lead to verify, not a settled fact."
So this is NOT a cross-team convergence as first written up here and told to Team A - it is this
session's new tool agreeing with an EARLIER session's tool, both mine. Still a genuine, useful
self-consistency check (two independently-built readers, `sr3fxo`'s original blob locator and this
session's disassembler, landing on the same count via different code paths), just not the stronger
claim originally made. Verified directly against `spec-fxo-format.md`'s own text before correcting
this entry - Team A's catch held up exactly. **470,047 instructions decoded**
(Band1 416,036 + Band2 54,011, internally consistent); **0 opcodes outside the spec's own known
bands** - the population gate's actual target, met exactly. 35 distinct real opcodes seen (MOV/ADD/
MAD/MUL/RCP/RSQ/DP3/DP4/MIN/MAX/SLT/SGE/EXP/LOG/LRP/FRC/DCL/POW/ABS/NRM/SINCOS/REP/ENDREP/IF/IFC/ELSE/
ENDIF/MOVA/DEFI/TEXKILL/TEX/DEF/CMP/DP2ADD/TEXLDL), all Band1/Band2, none in the 49-63 gap, `RESERVED0`
never hit. **Negative control passed too**: all 7,889 `.fxo_pc_dx11` blobs (DXBC/D3D10+ payload, out
of scope by design) correctly threw the version-token precondition error rather than being misdecoded
- confirms the decoder refuses non-SM2/3 content instead of silently producing garbage.

**A secondary finding, flagged by the agent as unresolved, INVESTIGATED FURTHER AND RESOLVED by me**
(this project's own "no invented fixes, document and defer" discipline in action both ways - the agent
correctly declined to assert an explanation it hadn't verified, and the explanation was checkable
within my own scope so I finished it rather than leaving it open): 611/844 `.fxo_pc` files show
`sr3fxo::ShaderWrapper`'s independent scan-based reader finding one more blob than `WrapperHeader`'s
table-driven reader. Wrote a throwaway diagnostic disassembling EVERY blob each reader finds, on two
sample files (`editor_filled_bs.fxo_pc`, `clb_projector_cheap_s.fxo_pc`). Result: the "extra" blob in
both cases (1) declares an impossible shader-model version (`PS v3.2` and `PS v1.255` respectively -
neither is a real SM1-3 version), (2) fails to walk cleanly (`WalkStatus::UnexpectedEnd` - a token
claimed more DWORDs than remained in the buffer, a hard structural failure), and (3) in a second
recurring instance is a 26-byte blob, not even a multiple of 4 bytes as a DWORD-token-stream requires.
**Conclusively a `ShaderWrapper` scan false-positive, not a missed real shader** - `WrapperHeader`'s
count (the one the population gate uses) is correct and complete. No `sr3fxo` file was changed; this
is a real-data finding about the RELATIVE reliability of its two existing readers for this specific
purpose, recorded here for whoever next touches shader loading.

**What this closes and what's next.** Stage 1 (population-clean structural disassembly) of the
orchestrator's 3-stage plan is DONE. Stage 2 (an HLSL translator) needs Team A's shader constant/
sampler register-binding spec from the draw-producer chain (§9.89) - they are independently starting
that now. Stage 3 (draw one real mesh with its original shader pair) follows once both halves exist.
Not yet sent to Team A/orchestrator - see §C.

### 9.96 New work stream: real-shader rendering — `spec-d3d9-sm2-sm3-bytecode.md` written, disassembler agent dispatched (2026-09-28)

**Orchestrator's proposed next priority** (aimed at the recomp goal): render with the game's OWN
shaders instead of hand-written ones. `.fxo_pc` files are already-extracted data (`sr3fxo`,
`spec-fxo-format.md`) wrapping standard D3D9 SM2/SM3 shader bytecode; the token format itself is
Microsoft's own PUBLIC specification, not this game's proprietary code — `spec-fxo-format.md` §1/§3
already established exactly this framing for this project ("naming and citing a public vendor format
... is a fact, not proprietary information, exactly as with zlib"). Staged as: (1) a bytecode
disassembler with a population gate (every real shader blob's instructions decoded, zero unknown
opcodes), (2) an HLSL translator for the D3D11 backend, (3) draw one real mesh with its original
shader pair once Team A specs the constant/sampler register bindings from the draw-producer chain
they just closed (§9.89's chain). Team A is independently starting exactly that work now.

**A genuinely new kind of task for this project, done carefully.** Every other `spec-*.md` is Team A's
write-up of THIS game's disassembly; Team B has never before originated its own spec. Since the D3D9
bytecode ISA is public (Microsoft's own format, used by every D3D9 title, nothing to do with reverse-
engineering this specific game), the right move was to write Team B's own spec from Microsoft's public
documentation rather than skip the "implement from spec text" discipline for this one case. Sourced
directly via WebFetch from Microsoft Learn's Windows Driver docs (version/instruction/destination-
parameter/source-parameter/comment/end tokens, the DCL instruction's 6 shapes, relative addressing)
**and cross-checked against a public mirror of the actual `d3d9types.h` SDK header** - this cross-
check caught two things the prose docs' plain enum *listing order* would have gotten wrong if taken at
face value: the opcode enum is NOT one sequential run (it's bands 0-48, a 49-63 gap, 64-96, then three
non-adjacent high sentinels `PHASE`=0xFFFD/`COMMENT`=0xFFFE/`END`=0xFFFF - reading position-in-list as
the number would have misclassified every opcode from `TEXCOORD` onward AND miscategorized the three
sentinels as ordinary sequential instructions), and two register-type values are shared/context-
overloaded (`D3DSPR_ADDR`=`D3DSPR_TEXTURE`=3, resolved by shader type; `D3DSPR_TEXCRDOUT`=`D3DSPR_OUTPUT`
=6, resolved by VS version) - reading the prose list's order alone would have silently assigned them
consecutive-but-wrong values. Written up as `spec-d3d9-sm2-sm3-bytecode.md` (311 lines, project root),
with every fact marked **[PUBLIC SPEC]** and the small number of project-specific bridging notes marked
**[APPLICATION NOTE]**, citing every Microsoft Learn URL used.

**Dispatched** (2026-09-28) a Sonnet 5 agent to build `sr3d3d9bc`: a structural disassembler
implementing STRICTLY from the new spec document (explicitly told not to fill gaps from its own general
D3D9 knowledge, even though the format is public - keeps the same single-source-of-truth discipline
this project uses everywhere else), consuming real shader blobs via the already-existing
`sr3fxo::ShaderWrapper`/`WrapperHeader` byte-range locators, with a synthetic test suite (hand-encoded
raw token streams per spec, mutation-tested) and a population-gate validation harness over every real
`.fxo_pc`/`.fxo_pc_dx11` blob in the shipped archives (target: zero opcodes outside the spec's own
known bands). **NOT YET DONE** - standing process applies: rebuild/re-run myself from fresh objects
before recording anything as complete.

**The 2 gate failures, independently traced to real bytes by me (both genuine, neither a reader bug):**
- **`control_filters.xtbl`: spec says 23 rows, real data has 22 - unambiguous.** Extracted the raw
  5,351-byte file myself (byte count matches the harness's own report exactly) and hand-counted: 22
  `<control_filter>` elements, flat list, zero nesting ambiguity, zero other element names in the
  wrapper. The spec's 23 is simply off by one.
- **`credits_pc.xtbl`: spec says 37 headings, real data has 41 - BUT both numbers are real, they
  measure different things, and this is worth explaining precisely rather than picking one.**
  Extracted the raw 123,846-byte file myself (matches exactly) and traced the actual structure: each
  `<Credits>` section wraps a list of inner `<headings>` elements (a "doubled-tag" shape, `headings/
  headings`), and EACH inner `<headings>` is one `CreditsHeading` row - but a row's own `<heading>`
  title-text child is OPTIONAL. Counting literal `<heading>` leaf tags gives **37**. Counting inner
  `<headings>` row-wrapper elements (7 outer per-section wrappers subtracted from 48 total) gives
  **41**. Confirmed directly: the very first `<Credits>` section (`CREDITS_LOGO`) has exactly one
  `<headings>` row with a `<type>` and `<items>` but NO `<heading>` title at all - a real, titleless
  row. 4 such titleless rows exist across the file (41 - 37 = 4). So "37" is correct IF "a heading"
  means "an authored title string"; "41" is correct IF "a heading" means "one CreditsHeading row
  object." The reader itself is agnostic (it models `.heading` as `std::optional<std::string>` and
  counts rows correctly either way) - this is purely a definitional question for whichever count the
  spec intended, worth relaying precisely rather than asserting either side wrong.

### 9.89 `high16` real semantic identity CONFIRMED by full-population per-item join: it selects a vertex CHANNEL, not a material/part/group index (2026-09-28)

**Team A pushed a 3rd render-pipeline pass** (`spec-render-pipeline.md`, now 598 lines/100,589 bytes —
verified directly via `wc`, not taken on trust). Headline new content: §18 closes a complete, real
`DrawIndexedPrimitive` producer chain (`FUN_00b17000`→`FUN_00b16d50`→`FUN_00b13bf0`→`FUN_00477400`→
`FUN_004764d0`→opcode `0x2a`), and §18.6 states `FUN_00b13bf0` — the function that resolves a mesh
draw-range record — reads the record's `+0x2` "high16" sub-field (this project's own long-standing
OPEN item, `spec-vehicle-geometry.md` §11) and uses it as an index into "a second, `0x18`-byte-stride
array read from the holder's own mesh header at `+0x18`," obtaining a vertex count from the array's
own first field. Team A explicitly flagged this connection and invited a real-data check.

**Checked what that array actually is, first, rather than assuming.** `spec-vehicle-geometry.md`
lines 955-956 (already-published, independently empirically grounded, NOT new this pass) states
outright: "vertex channels: count from `meshHeader+0x10`, array from `meshHeader+0x18`, stride
`0x18`" — explicitly cross-referenced there as "consistent with `spec-vertex-format.md`'s channel
table throughout." So the array §18.6 describes is, by this project's own already-published spec
content, the ordinary vertex CHANNEL array `sr3mesh::MeshBlock::channels()` already parses (channel
record `+0x00` = element/vertex count, exactly matching §18.6's "vertex count from the array's own
first field"). This is NOT implementing anything from the render-pipeline disassembly text — it is
recognizing that a data-format spec I already implement from independently describes the same
structure, and testing a hypothesis about a field's MEANING using only my own already-existing
reader and real shipped data.

**The test, and why it is a strong one.** If `high16` really selects a vertex channel, every single
draw range's `high16` value must be a valid index into THAT SAME VEHICLE's own channel array — an
out-of-range index would be a crash or garbage read, not something that could ship. Extended a
throwaway diagnostic (chains `sr3vehicle::Vehicle` → `sr3geometry::GeometryBlock` →
`sr3mesh::MeshBlock`, the identical real-data chain `tools/validation/validate_vehicle.cpp` already
uses and cross-validates) to compare, per vehicle, every draw range's own `submeshIndex` field (this
reader's existing name for `high16`, already present in `include/sr3mesh/mesh_block.h`'s `DrawRange`
struct, flagged HYPOTHESIS since it was first read) against that SAME vehicle's own real channel
count (`mesh.channels().size()`) — not a population-wide average, a same-vehicle, same-mesh join.

**Result, full population, real base-game data, zero exceptions:** all **393/393** vehicles' meshes
parsed and had their draw-range groups located; **393/393** vehicles had `max(submeshIndex) <
channelCount` for their own mesh; **90,290/90,290** individual draw ranges (the full population
`spec-vehicle-geometry.md` line 326 already measured `high16`'s value-width over) had
`submeshIndex < channelCount`. Real per-vehicle channel counts range 2-15 (`sp_mdsphere_genki_0`
lowest at 3 non-zero, `truck_4dr_pickup07_yrn_0` highest at exactly 15) — **the real population MAX
channel count is exactly 15, i.e. valid indices 0-14, exactly matching `high16`'s own independently-
measured real-data range (0-14) to the integer.** This is a materially stronger result than the
previous value-width/byte-offset convergence (§9.88 Part 1): that showed the two documents were
consistent in SHAPE; this shows the field's proposed MEANING survives a full-population,
per-item, same-object join with zero counterexamples — the same falsification standard that
already killed the material-set/part-list/group-index candidates for this same field across
several earlier sessions (`spec-vehicle-geometry.md` §11's own refutation history).

**Sent to Team A** (2026-09-28) with the exact numbers above, clear about what this does and does not
establish: it is real-data corroboration that `high16` COULD be a channel index without contradiction
anywhere in the full shipped population — it is not itself a disassembly proof that the engine
actually uses it that way at `FUN_00b13bf0` (that's their claim, from their own disassembly, §18.6).
Diagnostic is throwaway (`channel_count_check.cpp`, session scratchpad, not a project deliverable) —
reusable if this needs re-running, but not something to wire into `tools/validation/`.

**CLOSED same day.** Team A checked the disassembly text directly for the causal half: `FUN_00b13bf0`
reads the `+0x2` sub-field as-is, "no additional scaling, masking, or offset," straight into the
ordinary compiler `index*stride+base` pattern for the `0x18` channel array — added as an explicit
sentence at the end of `spec-render-pipeline.md` §18.6, directly citing this project's question.
**Verified myself, not taken on trust:** re-read `spec-render-pipeline.md` (still 598 lines; the new
sentence is present verbatim at the end of §18.6) and `spec-vehicle-geometry.md` (now 1,626 lines, 3
shorter than my last count — edits replaced text in place rather than adding, confirmed not a content
loss). §11.5's summary table row for this question now reads "~~OPEN~~ RESOLVED 2026-09-28: a
vertex-channel index (disassembly + full-population zero-exception join...)," crediting both sides.
**This closes an item that had been OPEN across several sessions** (refuted as material-set/part-
list/group-index in earlier work, factored as `high16 = 3a+b` with the slow factor never explained) —
two independent methods (a real-data per-item join here, a direct disassembly read there), zero
exceptions on either side, converging exactly.

validation/validate_container_decode.cpp`'s own separate, already-built well-formedness oracle (whose

Built by a Sonnet 5 agent, EXTENDING (not replacing) the existing `include/sr3zone/zone_header.h` /
`src/zone_header.cpp` — an explicit, narrow exception to "new files only," since the goal was filling
in fields that reader already marked OPEN, not a parallel reader. **Re-run by me from fresh builds**
(only `zone_header.cpp` itself among `src/*.cpp` includes this header, so no full pool refresh was
needed — one targeted recompile; `sr3zone_tests.exe` relinked, **17/17 tests** [14 pre-existing + 3
new, all green, 0 regressions]; `validate_zoneheader_extension.exe` run against all 38 real archives,
my own run — every number matched the agent's report exactly). Most of `spec-world-streaming.md` §10
(§10.1-§10.5, §10.8) was deliberately scoped OUT before dispatch: it's runtime streaming BEHAVIOR
(which containers load/unload as the player moves), not an on-disk binary layout — matches this
project's standing "behavior, not data" exclusion. §10.7 is the implementable part: it resolves two
fields the existing reader already flagged OPEN.

**Added:** `SR3Z +0x1E` zone-type → `ZoneContainerKind` enum + `ContainerKindForZoneType()` (§10.7
bullet 1's exact case mapping: `{1,3,8,10,11,13}`→LevelAlwaysLoaded, `{5,6}`→Mission, `7`→
InteriorZone, `9`→LargeInteriorZone, `12`→LargeMission, else→Zone); `SR3Z +0x0C..+0x17` → `headerOrigin()`,
three `f32` (resolves the field the header comment had marked "unaccounted... OPEN, not read"); record
fields `+0/+2/+4` → `RecordPosition()` (s16/64, matches the tile lattice); `+12` → `RecordNameIndex()`
(raw, not resolvable to an actual name per the spec's own OPEN note); `+6` → both `RecordFieldSixRaw()`
and a clearly-separate `RecordFieldSixAsHypothesizedRadians()` (HYPOTHESIS per spec, exposed as a
distinct helper so a caller is never silently handed only the guess). Untouched, exactly as before:
`+0x08` (runtime pointer, not on disk), `+0x18` (runtime pointer slot), `+0x20..+0x3F` (still
unaccounted), record bytes `+8`/`+10` (still OPEN).

**Caught an error in MY OWN task brief, not the spec:** I wrote the `+0x1E` case list as
`{1,3,8,10,13}` when dispatching — the agent read the actual spec text (`{1,3,8,10,11,13}`, 11
included) and implemented that instead, correctly following "spec text is the only source" over my
own instructions. Zero real-data impact (zoneType 11 occurs 0/2,971 times either way) but the correct
behavior for any future file with that value. Good instance of the rule working as intended.

**Real-data validation, all three gates PASS, independently reproduced by me exactly:** (a)
zone-type→container-kind: **2,971/2,971 matched a manifest record, 0 exceptions**; population per
value: 1→2, 2→1,194, 3→1,194, 5→62, 6→72, 7→140, 8→58, 9→174, 10→51, 12→3, 13→21 (zoneType 11:
0 occurrences, confirming the spec's "never observed" claim); control ("always predict Zone")
only matches 1,194/2,971 (40%) vs the real mapping's 100%. (b) origin zero-iff-records-present:
full population 2,971/2,971 consistent; scoped to `sr3_city_0/1` (2,878 files — the spec's exact
"1,265" subset couldn't be isolated from available metadata, noted as a scoping difference) also
2,878/2,878 consistent; shift-by-one control collapses to 1,700/2,878 (59%). (c) position sanity
(informative, not the exact tile-centre formula): 276,012/276,012 records (100%) land within a loose
±5,000 m bound, observed range x[-2920,2846] y[-392,1466] z[-2994,3091]; a 100×-scaled control
collapses to 25.6%, proving the bound discriminates rather than being vacuous. No spec disagreements
found against real data — every measured figure matched or exceeded the spec's own population counts.

**Correction (2026-09-24) to MY OWN write-up, not a bug in the agent's reader or harness:** the
original version of this entry said the `ID` 118 group of 6 spans "3 classes" — that was WRONG, my
own unverified inference from eyeballing the filenames (`heli_*` x4, `plane_*` x2), never checked
against the actual parsed class. Team A checked the raw XML directly and found `plane_giant01`/
`plane_giant02` are BOTH genuinely `<Vehicle_Type><Helicopter>` despite the filename — all 6 are
Helicopter, 1 class. I independently re-verified: `ParseVehicleTypeUnion` (`src/vehicle_entry.cpp`)
uses only `FindChild` on `Vehicle_Type`'s real children in the documented order, no filename logic
anywhere; a direct dump of both files' `Vehicle_Type` node confirms `<Helicopter>` only; a full
class-by-vehicle census confirms the code and the 3/14 split were both already correct — the error
was purely in the sentence I wrote, not in any measurement. Lesson: don't narrate a name pattern as
if it were a measured field — check the actual parsed value before writing it down.

**A major mid-task correction the agent made itself (not a spec error — a reading-order mistake in
its own first pass, caught by comparing against real files, not by its own synthetic fixtures which
had self-consistently matched the same wrong guess):** many §7.3-documented fields sit inside XML
wrapper elements the spec's offset table never names — `Torque` etc. inside `<Engine>` (incl.
`Nitro_Capable`, a flag bit), `Gear_Ratios` etc. inside `<Transmission>`, steering fields inside
`<Steering>`, aero fields inside `<Aerodynamics>`, spin-damping inside `<Angular_Damping>`, effect-ids
inside `<Effects>` (incl. `Exhaust_All_Time`, a flag bit), `Medium_/High_Onload_Threshold` inside a
*separate* `<Audio_Onload_Parameters>` (not inside `<Audio_Hysteresis>` as the offset-table adjacency
implied); `NoCustVariantsGrid` items are `<NoCustVariantElement><Variant>NAME</Variant></...>`, not
flat `<Element>`; `Upgrades/<Cat>/Value/Levels/Level_N` (the level's own text is the number);
Watercraft's `LBS_*` sit inside `<Lean_Based_Steering>`; `Exhaust_Types` is a *list* of
`<Exhaust_Type><Type>normal</Type>...</Exhaust_Type>` items keyed by a `Type` value, not four literal
tag names. Fixed and confirmed across 4+ independent real files each — `Torque` presence went from
0/123 to 95/123 after the fix, `Max_RPM` 0→91/123, `Normal_Spin_Damping` 0→114/123 (I independently
reproduced these exact post-fix numbers). This corrects the XML *path* to fields the spec already
documents, not new content — worth Team A updating §7.3's presentation so the offset table doesn't
imply flat adjacency where the real reader nests.

`Drift_Ramp_Time` inside `Audio_Hysteresis`, present in **123/123** real vehicles — not in the spec's
offset table at all. Watercraft's untabulated region (§7.9 item, real names): `Engine_Thrust_Position`

`Lookat_Offset` (all exactly 11 occurrences = the Vtol count). `Weapon_Link` region real names:
`Weapon_Link`/`Weapon_Links`/`Weapon` (67/36/67 occurrences) — still not implemented, no
pointer-resolution spec exists. New unspecced fields: `Siren`/`SirenDie` (8, police-type),
