### 9.79 `sr3xtbl` foundation: tolerant XML parser + engine accessors + CRC-32 row hash (2026-09-20)

Built by a Sonnet 5 agent from `spec-xtbl-format.md` (27,532 B), `spec-tables-traffic-ai.md`
§1 (89,706 B), `spec-vehicle-data.md` §7.2; **re-run by me from fresh builds** (`sr3xtbl` compiled
into the pool at `/W4`, `sr3xtbl_tests` green, `validate_xtbl_population.exe` "ALL GATES PASSED").
Files: `include/sr3xtbl/{xtbl,errors}.h`, `src/xtbl.cpp`, `tests/synthetic_xtbl_test.cpp`,
`tools/validation/validate_xtbl_population.cpp`; CMake `sr3xtbl` + `sr3xtbl_tests` added;
`build_one.bat` gained `xtbl.obj`. **API:** `ParseDocument(bytes, ParseOptions)` -> `Document
{root(), table(), warnings()}`; `Node{name(), text() (nullptr == engine NULL), children(),
attributes()}`; `FindChild/NextSibling/CountChildren/NthChild/Children/ChildText/CopyText`,
`ParseInt32/UInt32/UInt16/Int16/UInt8/Int8/Bool/Float` (`GetX` = the "if present" reader,
`ReadXAlways` = `Always<T>{value, present}` so absence is never silently defaulted), `ReadVec3`,
`FlagMask`, `HasFlag`, `EnumIndex`, `NameHash(text, seed=0)` (+ case-sensitive/OrZero variants).
**Recovery policy (each recorded in `warnings()`):** a close tag naming no open element closes the
innermost open one (`MismatchedCloseTag`); one naming an ancestor closes everything above it; a
0x1F control byte is kept verbatim (`ControlCharacterInText`); a tag tail that is not `name="value"`
pairs makes the whole tag text the element name (`NameContainsWhitespace`); unclosed elements at EOF
close with a warning; whitespace-only text under an element that has children is NULL, leaf text is
never trimmed; entities `&lt; &gt; &amp;` are decoded (whether the engine decodes them is unknown);
`FormatError` for empty input, a first non-blank byte other than `<`, a UTF-16 BOM, no root, or a cut
inside a tag/comment/CDATA/PI.

**Real data (mine, all 38 archives / 6,431 containers / 405,694 entries):** **2,222** xtbl-family
entries (2,080 compressed + 142 raw DLC; `.xtbl` 1,888, `.cte_xtbl` 334, nothing else ends in
"xtbl"), **2,222/2,222 decode Ok and parse, 0 rejected**; **2,214 with zero warnings and exactly 8
entries with warnings = the 4 distinct files Team A named** (`template.xtbl`; `07_out.cte_xtbl` and
`07_out-lightset.xtbl` for the 0x1F; `xbox360_text.xtbl` with 101 whitespace-in-name tags), the
three defect classes exactly. Controls: an independent strict oracle rejects exactly those 8 and
agrees on element count and depth for the other 2,214; truncation inside a tag is rejected 318/318,
after a `>` parses with `UnclosedAtEof` 318/318, an injected bad close tag gives exactly one warning
with the same element count 316/316, input without its leading `<` rejected 318/318. Survey: no BOM,
declaration, comment, PI, CDATA or DOCTYPE anywhere; entities only `&lt; &gt;` (~4,500 each) and
`&amp;` (21); self-closing always `<X />` (8,047); an attribute occurs once in each of 141 entries
(`<TableDescription source=".."/>`); CRLF in 2,208 entries, LF-only 12; UTF-8 non-ASCII in 4;
mixed content (text + children) really occurs (1,827 elements in 56 entries); tab indent 1,719,
space indent 373. Shape: root is `root` (2,217) or `Root` (5); **`root -> Table` in 1,962/2,222; the
260 without it are 128 blend_tree files, 122 state_machine files and 10 others** (action_nodes,
node_graph_files, control_filters, control_parameters, networks, default_global, 3 lightset/district
files); 299 distinct row names, 58,089 rows (top: `CRC` 10,630, `Entry` 5,590, `NewEntity` 5,539);
`Camera/camera`, `Category/category`, `Color_Entry/color_entry` differ only in case.

**The row-key hash is REAL (§1.4): reflected CRC-32, lowercased bytes, init 0, no final XOR** — table
anchors 0 / 0x77073096 / 0xEE0E612C and the standard check value `0xCBF43926` (seed 0xFFFFFFFF +
complement) reproduce; against **16 distinct real saves** (my run; the agent used 14): base
unlockable ids **4,992/4,992** = `NameHash(Name)` of `unlockables.xtbl`/`patch_unlockables.xtbl` rows,
DLC block **784/784** = `NameHash(Name)` of the dlc1/2/3 rows in file order (Team A's 784/784), cheat
ids **151/151** = `NameHash` of `cheats.xtbl` `<UnlockString>`; controls all 0 (no-lowercase hash,
standard complemented CRC, 4,000 random ids). Only seed 0 checked on real data.

**Spec disagreements (reported to Team A):** (1) `spec-xtbl-format.md` §2 "root then one Table" is not
universal (260 entries above). (2) §3.4 "floats have exactly 6 decimals" is false: 33 exponent-form
values (`1.49011611938e-08`) and 67 values with 21-29 integer digits in the `01_z01`/`02_z02` cutscene
tables. (3) `spec-tables-progression.md` §4.1 "order = save order": the base slot order is NOT file
order (176/4,992 slots ascending; 1,392/1,424 slots' `<Priority>` target sits at an earlier slot).
(4) traffic-ai §1.3 says the integer part may be hex, yet a token starting `0x` returns 0.0, so the hex
branch is unreachable, and no real text starts with `0x`. Uncertain (agent): attributes are not in
the engine model; text of a mixed element (segments concatenated); sign of zero for `0x` floats;
exponent rounding and a `+` exponent; integer-part overflow (wraps mod 2^32).

### 9.78 `vpp::Container` decoded compressed entries at the WRONG offset — fixed; every compressed entry now decodes (2026-09-20)

**The bug, and why it hid for the whole project.** `Container` located a compressed
entry at `payloadStart + (+0x08)`. But `+0x08` is a LOGICAL offset (the offline
packer's spacing by `round_up(+0x0C, 0x800)`); it locates raw entries physically and
is *wrong* for compressed ones. Because the decoder capped its output at `+0x0C`, a
wrong offset that landed inside some OTHER entry's zlib stream still "succeeded" with
the right byte count and the wrong bytes (a prefix of a neighbour's data) — the
"silent corruption" of `spec-xtbl-format.md` §1, the reason for the
`OkUnconfirmedContent` downgrade, and (with the `RecoveredSharedStream` backward-walk
heuristic) a stack of workarounds for a bug that was never in the data. Found by the
fxo agent (§9.76: only 108/844 `.fxo_pc` decoded, 2/108 exact), then generalised here.

**The two real rules, measured over ALL 6,431 shipped containers with an oracle
independent of any offset rule** (`tools/validation/validate_container_offsets.cpp`;
oracle = a zlib stream at the candidate offset inflates to EXACTLY the entry's own
`+0x0C` bytes and then stops — output NOT capped, since a cap made a wrong offset look
right — and consumes `+0x10 … +0x10+8` input bytes, a second independent field):
- **Mode (a)** (flags bit `0x2` clear; all ten shipped instances are flags `0x4801`):
  streams are laid end to end, physical(i) = `payloadStart + Σ_{j<i} roundup(size_j,
  0x800)` with `size_j = +0x10` for a compressed entry when flags bit `0x1` is set (else
  `+0x0C`) — which is exactly the loader's own slot accumulation that the spec had
  discarded as "write-only scratch". **4,272/4,272** compressed entries locate
  (tight and loose), all 4,263 non-first ones; the old `+0x08` rule locates 14
  (`+0x0C`-spacing 14). Team A independently confirmed on 3,263 entries with their own
  protocol (`modea_offset_check.py`), and folded it into `spec-vpp-container.md` §7.
- **Mode (b)** (flags bit `0x2` set, e.g. `0x4803`): ONE stream from `payloadStart`
  whose decoded length is exactly Σ(`+0x0C` of the compressed entries), each entry the
  slice at its `+0x08` (= the packed running sum of the earlier compressed `+0x0C`).
  **6,239/6,239** containers with ≥ 1 compressed entry satisfy both invariants, including
  the 68 that also hold raw entries.

**Fix (`include/vpp/payload_locator.h`, `src/payload_locator.cpp`, `include/vpp/format.h`,
`include/vpp/container.h`, `src/container.cpp`).** `PayloadLocation` gains
`logicalOffset` (the raw `+0x08`) and `sharedStream`; `offset` is now the PHYSICAL
position (corrected for compressed entries). `Container`'s constructor assigns it by the
rules above; `decompressEntry` dispatches to `decompressModeA` (stream at the corrected
offset) or `decompressModeB` (slice of the shared stream, decoded lazily and cached in a
mutable prefix that grows geometrically — a `Container` is therefore not safe for
concurrent `decompressEntry()` calls). `format.h` gains `kSlotsByCompressedSizeFlag`
(`0x1`). `inflateToSize` now treats "produced exactly `+0x0C` bytes" as success even if
zlib reports an error in the same call (real entries end their deflate data with a short
sync-flush-style tail then padding, so `inflate()` reads on into it and reports "invalid
stored block lengths" AFTER the payload — this second bug alone made every mode-(a)
non-first entry fail until fixed). `tryRecoverSharedStreamTail` and the
`OkUnconfirmedContent` downgrade are DELETED; the enumerators `OkUnconfirmedContent`,
`ContentValidated`, `ContentValidationFailed`, `RecoveredSharedStream(LongChain)` remain
(a hundred tools name them; ~436 mentions in 96 files) but `Container` never returns
them — retiring them is a pure cleanup. `xtbl` content refinement
(`refineWithXtblValidation`) still exists but its "root's first child must be `<Table>`"
rule is only a proxy for the old corruption and rejects legitimate other-shaped tables.
Not observed in shipped data, so UNVERIFIED: a mode-(a) container mixing raw and
compressed entries; a mode-(a) container with flags bit `0x1` clear AND compressed
entries (both keep the loader's accumulation rule).

**Verified by me (fresh builds, `/W4` clean, `validate_container_decode.exe`, every entry
of every container):** mode (a) **4,272/4,272 Ok** (was 9); mode (b) **385,168/385,168 Ok**
(all 378,929 non-first). Content oracles, independent of the offset arithmetic: **2,079/2,080
`.xtbl`/`.cte_xtbl` are well-formed XML** (1,817 in the `<root><Table>` shape; the one
exception is a genuine typo IN THE SHIPPED DATA — `misc_tables.vpp_pc :: template.xtbl`
contains `<RampExposure>False</Exposure>`, complete at its declared 232 bytes — so the
`sr3xtbl` parser must tolerate mismatched closing tags the way the engine does);
**844/844 `.fxo_pc` decode to the wrapper magic `0x4B42A1EE`** (was 0/844); **69,761/69,761
`.cpeg_pc`/`.cvbm_pc` carry the PEG header words** (`+0x10 == +0x14`, `+0x12 == 0`),
including the 77 that were unreachable (§9.77's "at-risk" 76). `.fxo_pc` through the fixed
library: **844/844 exact consumption** (was 2/108), **847/847 `.fxo_pc_dx11`** decoded (was
0). Synthetic archive test rewritten around the two rules (a multi-entry `0x4801` fixture
whose physical and logical offsets deliberately disagree; a control reading the old way
that must NOT reproduce the entry; the shared-stream fixture decoded out of order; a
broken `+0x08` packing reported not guessed; the flag being authoritative) and
**mutation-checked: three mutants (the old rule, size accumulation by uncompressed size,
mode (b) ignored) all killed**. All 24 synthetic suites re-linked against a full
`build_verify/` object refresh (every `src/*.cpp` recompiled at `/W4`, zero warnings) and
pass; all 93 tools/harnesses syntax-check against the changed headers.

**Populations re-run through the fixed container (Team A's ask), by me, fresh builds:**
- **PEG (§9.77):** the 76 mode-(a) index > 0 c-files (cvbm 45 + cpeg 31) that were 0/76
  unreachable now **parse 76/76** (0 failures, 0 decode failures); every other gate is
  unchanged (70,524/70,524 parsed, 76,651 records, all `size == sum of levels` gates, pairs
  70,471). So 70,600 c-files parse in total.
- **`.cefct_pc` (§9.76):** all **1,812** now decode `Ok` (before: Ok 240, RecoveredSharedStream
  3, RecoveredSharedStreamLongChain 1,569) and the enumeration is IDENTICAL —
  `root+0x40` 346/135, `root+0x70` 595/168, `root+0x90` 478/119, the same count-value
  distributions — i.e. the old backward-walk heuristic had recovered exactly the right bytes for
  those entries; the exact slicing reproduces them (an independent agreement between two
  mechanisms). Layout gates unchanged (B 1,812; the spec's strict end-field gate E 1,468).
- **`.fxo_pc` (§9.76):** through the library itself now 844/844 exact consumption (was 2/108),
  847/847 `.fxo_pc_dx11`. Not re-run: asm (all 805 are stored raw, unaffected).

**`sr3_viewer` relinked** (`build_verify/sr3_viewer_sec978.exe`, explicit object list against the
refreshed pool; the existing `sr3_viewer.exe` was NOT overwritten — the permission classifier
refused that earlier). A textured `brad` render is deterministic per binary but differs from the
§9.69 render: **18,193 of 648,000 pixels (2.8%), max channel delta 34, mean 1.5.** Explained, not
noise: the old texture reader read a record's size field as 16 bits, so it reported `brad_sm_upper_d`
(512x512 BC1) as **43,688 bytes** — 174,760 mod 65,536 + 0, i.e. a truncated mip chain — where the
rewritten reader (§9.77) reports the true **174,760**. Every texture over 64 KB was being uploaded
with a wrong/truncated mip chain; the difference is the correct lower mips now being sampled. CMake
harness targets still pending. Also: `save_browser` updated (play time is seconds).
